Google Gemini Partners With Watch Duty to Clear Static From Firefighter Radio

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (477 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On Friday, Google’s Gemini team announced the results of a newly introduced partnership with the wildfire-tracking app Watch Duty, after Gemini engineers spent six months embedded with Watch Duty’s first responders.
  • Industry observers note that the Gemini AI improvements got a real-world test during Washington state’s Railroad Fire in July 2026, when Watch Duty issued what it calls its first-ever nighttime Critical Alert.
  • It has been revealed that “This is something the tool also has the capability to do if reports of flooding are communicated via radio,” remarked Dave Merritt, co-founder and chief technology officer of Watch Duty.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Friday, Google’s Gemini team announced the results of a newly introduced partnership with the wildfire-tracking app Watch Duty, after Gemini engineers spent six months embedded with Watch Duty’s first responders. The results cut vital new wildfire dispatch translations down to seconds and helped improve radio communications, which can be rough on the front lines of a new fire.

Industry observers note that the Gemini AI improvements got a real-world test during Washington state’s Railroad Fire in July 2026, when Watch Duty issued what it calls its first-ever nighttime Critical Alert. The alert stemmed from a nearly unintelligible, static-filled 911 call that the Gemini tool transcribed in under 30 seconds. That kind of assistance can help Watch Duty send alerts to affected communities more quickly and enable first responders to update maps more accurately and make better-informed decisions.

It has been revealed that “This is something the tool also has the capability to do if reports of flooding are communicated via radio,” remarked Dave Merritt, co-founder and chief technology officer of Watch Duty. “Across disasters, we hear feedback every day that first responders are using Watch Duty for additional situational awareness, especially for disasters that span multiple counties.”.

Watch Duty reporters are active and retired first responders who can manually monitor up to 20 different feeds, though static and rapid-fire jargon can make them difficult to follow.

Gemini workers used more than 20,000 hours of Watch Duty radio recordings to train the AI tool to recognize firefighting terms that aren’t in the average dictionary or books that AIs are typically trained on.

Google says the tool is not designed to replace human decision-making in life-or-death situations.

“This tool takes on the demanding work of listening, freeing Watch Duty’s volunteers to focus on what matters most: confirming fires and getting warnings to people while they can still act,” said Stephanie Chew, Google project team lead.

The project was completed at no cost thanks to a Google.org fellowship, and the resulting Watch Duty app features are free to use.

From the data collected, Gemini engineers and Watch Duty identified several measures of success.

According to recent reports, one metric was the word error rate, which fell by around 15% after the AI model was implemented. Another sign of success was a jump in Watch Duty volunteers’ satisfaction with their radio transcription tools, from around 35% to 92%.

Sources indicate that the Gemini tool continues to analyze approximately 200 hours of radio speech traffic from 400 feeds per day. The tool was made to handle more than 10,000 radio feeds if necessary.

According to recent reports, the integration could pave the way for broader use across public safety. The platform’s built-in scalability could eventually bring similar audio-clearing tools to local fire departments, 911 call centers and Coast Guard operations, where clear communication is critical under pressure.

Despite those continued challenges, top Wall Street analysts are bullish on the prospects of several stocks due to their long-run growth potential and exposure to lucrative business lines, including AI.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Recent findings suggest that cybersecurity manufacturer CrowdStrike Holdings (CRWD) is this week's first stock pick. The company is scheduled to announce fiscal second-quarter results on August 26.

Ahead of Q2 FY27 earnings, Truist analyst Junaid Siddiqui reiterated a buy rating on CrowdStrike stock and raised his price target to $245 from $187.50. Following CrowdStrike's impressive fiscal first-quarter performance and guidance raise, Siddiqui expects another strong quarter.

In a recent development, the 5-star analyst's optimism is backed by continued strength in Falcon Flex adoption and encouraging large deal activity. Siddiqui also cited continued momentum across emerging products. With the FY27 outlook assuming persistent strength in CrowdStrike's net newly introduced annual recurring revenue (ARR), Siddiqui is more focused on the longevity of key growth catalysts such as Falcon Flex adoption, platform consolidation and AI-led demand.

The analyst highlighted that talks with partners were encouraging, with pipeline generation and momentum in large deals remaining healthy in the fiscal second quarter despite tough, year-over-year comparisons.

"We continue to view CrowdStrike as one of the primary beneficiaries of platform consolidation, though we expect investors to remain focused on competitive dynamics and whether current growth levels represent a latest baseline or a period of demand acceleration," the analyst mentioned.

Siddiqui ranks No. 226 among more than 12,400 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 80% of the time, delivering an average return of about 40%. See CrowdStrike Financials on TipRanks.

In a recent development, shares of personal computer maker Dell Technologies (DELL) have rallied 251% this year, driven by strong demand for AI servers. Recently, Evercore analyst Amit Daryanani reiterated a buy rating on DELL and raised his price target to $550 from $500.

According to recent reports, the 5-star analyst contends that while Dell's AI compute segment is getting investors' attention, the organization's Storage business is underappreciated and well-positioned to drive revenue and profit acceleration. Daryanani expects the storage business to see higher demand once enterprises start to bring workload back on-premises.

It has been revealed that the analyst highlighted that Dell's Storage business, estimated to account for only 10% of FY27 revenue, is one of the factors that could help improve profit margins, given its higher profitability compared to AI servers. Daryanani estimates that the Storage business's operating margin is currently in the low-20% range, while margins for the AI server and traditional server businesses are in the mid-single-digit and mid-teens range, respectively.

Overall, Daryanani views the Storage business as an notable catalyst for three reasons: Dell has one of the broadest storage portfolios in the industry; Storage has a significantly higher margin profile than AI servers; and the shift toward proprietary, software-defined storage and AI-focused platforms.

"We think DELL's storage business is becoming increasingly strategic as AI infrastructure deployments move beyond GPU procurement and toward full stack + AI-ready architectures," mentioned Daryanani.

  • The v26.45 update concerns location tracking during outdoor workouts.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that some of the most popular Android smartwatches just got a battery-saving upgrade. Google released an updated version of Google Play Services on Tuesday that can help extend the battery life of a Wear OS smartwatch.

The v26.45 update concerns location tracking during outdoor workouts. Wear OS smartwatch users can now use their phone’s Global Navigation Satellite System to track their location during an outdoor workout, which can conserve battery life by outsourcing the smartwatch’s energy to the smartphone when it isn’t in Battery Saver mode.

According to recent reports, also: Pixel Watch 4 vs. Watch 5: Is Google’s latest model worth it?

Constantly communicating with satellites during an outdoor workout can be a battery drain, and every minute of battery life counts when you use your smartwatch for communication, workout tracking, and health monitoring. GPS services, a bright, always-on display, and continuous health sensors like SpO2 can squeeze the most juice out of your smartwatch.

Sources indicate that wear OS software is used by many of the most popular smartwatch brands, including Google, Samsung, and OnePlus. Both the Google Pixel Watch and Samsung Galaxy Watch’s largest batteries last approximately 40 hours. That’s nearly two days of use from two top Android smartwatches, but you’d be surprised how quickly it can drain.

Also: Galaxy Watch 9 review: Health data overload, but built for the future.

The update improves battery life without users having to take any action or change any settings — the Google Play Services version 26.45 works quietly under the hood.

That’s not the only Google Play Services revision that Wear OS smartwatch owners can take advantage of. Another recent update lets users view on their phone a larger preview of any watch face they want to install on their smartwatch.

Don’t Miss Out on GTA 6 Launch Week: Here’s How to Take Rockstar’s New Game Anywhere

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (779 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that look, we weren’t all lucky enough to lock in PTO for the release of Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • According to recent reports, A lot of folks are still working away, daydreaming about getting back on the sticks and knocking off corner stores as Jason and Lucia right now.
  • But even if you find yourself away from home, that doesn’t mean you’re completely locked out of playing GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that look, we weren’t all lucky enough to lock in PTO for the release of Grand Theft Auto 6. Not everyone gets to write a review of the most anticipated video game in recent memory, or live blog their first 24 hours roaming around Vice City.

According to recent reports, A lot of folks are still working away, daydreaming about getting back on the sticks and knocking off corner stores as Jason and Lucia right now. Some people are even on work trips or vacations away from their home consoles right now – let’s keep them in our thoughts.

But even if you find yourself away from home, that doesn’t mean you’re completely locked out of playing GTA 6. Sure, the game may presently be console-locked to the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S, but there are still clever ways to get the game booted up when you’re on the go.

Here’s everything you need to know about the remote play features that you’ll need to take this modern Bonnie and Clyde story on the road.

So long as you have a PS5 or an Xbox with GTA 6 downloaded and ready to go, you can experience the game through smaller devices even when you’re away from home.

Both modern consoles support remote play, a feature that lets you stream your game from your home setup.

If you’re looking to turn on the Xbox’s remote play feature, you need to access the Profile & System settings in the Xbox guide. From there, you need to navigate to the Devices & Connections menu and choose the Remote features option.

According to recent reports, you’ll need to enable the remote features and put your console into sleep mode in order to pair your chosen remote play device. Remote play devices include smartphones, tablets and Windows computers.

Gamers who own a PlayStation 5 will need to follow similar steps to get remote play functioning on a mobile device. Within the PlayStation’s settings menu, navigate to the System tab and choose Remote Play. Toggle the Enable Remote Play option. From there, all of the necessary device pairing and gameplay setup will happen through the PS Remote Play app, which you can download on your handheld device.

Industry observers note that whether you own a PlayStation or an Xbox, you’ll want to ensure your console settings are tuned so it stays connected to the internet in rest mode. You’ll also need to enable the console to turn on via a network connection. These settings will allow you to start a remote play session anytime, even if you’ve already left your home.

Industry observers note that if you’re using PlayStation’s remote play feature, you don’t have to fiddle around with gaming tablets or third-party handheld devices in order to find a comfortable way to play GTA 6. Sony’s PlayStation Portal is the perfect console accessory for natural gameplay, since it retains the DualShock controller design.

It has been revealed that GTA 6 isn’t coming out on PC for a while still. That limits how many options you have when it comes to taking the game on the go with you. If (for whatever reason) you don’t have access to any remote play options, that leaves you with only the most inconvenient and unwieldy way to take the new crime simulator with you on the road.

You’ll have to lug around your PS5 or Xbox wherever you go to get in some GTA time – but hey, at least the gaming industry’s deteriorating respect for physical media means you won’t have to keep track of a disc.

The PS5 Slim is probably the easiest current-gen console to carry with you, since the digital edition weighs less than 6 pounds. But you’re giving up the best possible performance available on the PS5 Pro.

Either way, you’ll be carrying around a large, expensive piece of hardware, so this option should only be considered if you really can’t get remote play functioning for whatever reason.

According to recent reports, microsoft’s video game ecosystem is huge, with Game Pass and streaming options available for PC players. But the Xbox brand isn’t offering gamers a cheat code to play GTA 6 on their beefy rigs (or any convenient handheld devices).

GTA 6 is only available on Xbox consoles with Xbox Cloud Gaming at this time. The upside is that this option lets you play the boundary-pushing new game on the Xbox One, which is very close to being two console generations old.

At that point, you’re better off biting the bullet on a current-generation console and considering the available remote play options.

Twenty percent of holiday shoppers are using AI agents as their first stop for research and advice, but they are not ready to have agents make purchases, according to the latest Salesforce research.

Also: What to know about early Black Friday sales.

Recent findings suggest that salesforce surveyed more than 2,500 shoppers in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia and found that 74% of shoppers trust recommendations from AI agents. Salesforce research forecasts AI-driven shopping recommendations to drive $75.8 billion in Cyber Week spending, up 13% from 2025.

Sources indicate that also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer.

Recent findings suggest that brands are also being noticed by AI agents, with 30% of shoppers saying they were first introduced to a upcoming brand via AI. And most importantly, 1 in 10 (11%) shoppers would avoid a brand if an AI agent told them to.

Here are some of the key findings from the 2026 holiday shopping research.

Retailers that use AI shopping agents are seeing bigger orders and more loyal customers. The survey found that shoppers who use AI agent referrals are twice as likely to make a purchase. In addition, 39% of shoppers have used AI agents on an e-commerce site, and 80% had a positive experience, while 75% felt more loyal to the brand as a result of the AI agent experience.

Recent findings suggest that shoppers who use AI agents spend 8% more than the average buyer and purchase 23% more items per order. Brands that use AI agents are seeing seven times faster sales growth than brands without them.

1 in 3 consumers has used an AI agent, including the widely adopted Meta Muse, now used by 12% of all consumers. Grok Bot is also in high demand.

Industry observers note that the survey found that 28% of consumers give their agents multiple tasks per day. The most common use of AI agents is price comparisons, product reviews, and brainstorming for gift items. Brand discovery is a major benefit of AI agent use cases.

Agents as advisors are growing, but agents are not buying products yet, with only 19% of personal agent owners using logic to check out. Only 9% of consumers allow their personal AI agents to have unrestricted access to their financial details, and 36% have set up a separate credit card for their AI agents.

Also: ZDNET’s favorite tech devices for 2026.

The majority of consumers (73%) are not comfortable giving personal AI agents their payment information, and 49% are not interested in agents making purchases on their behalf. Consumers do not want to share their purchase history or personal data that could potentially lead to unwanted charges. Shoppers will abandon an AI agent after 2-3 mistakes. If an AI agent makes a bad recommendation, 1 in 3 consumers will blame the AI.

Retailers must adopt AI shopping agents in order to compete. Retailers must be able to service and respond to shopper agents. The ability to detect intent, buying signals, sources of dissatisfaction, and other consumer-related buying patterns at machine scale (significantly faster and higher volume than human scale) will require retailers to invest in AI agentic engagement capabilities.

Also: 50 AI agents tried to build a thriving Minecraft civilization – it didn’t end well.

Today, AI agents advise consumers on their holiday shopping journeys, but in the very near future, they will autonomously make purchasing decisions with little to no involvement from their human counterparts. The future of shopping will be more autonomous, highly personalized, and nearly frictionless. Brands that invest in agentic AI will garner the most loyalty and future business.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that apple rolled out the second public beta of iOS 27.3 on Thursday, Nov.
  • Apple historically releases an iOS patch in December, so I expect iOS 27.3 to land on iPhones later this year.
  • Industry observers note that since this is a beta, I recommend downloading it on something other than your primary device.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that apple rolled out the second public beta of iOS 27.3 on Thursday, Nov. 19, more than two months after the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro lineup and iOS 27. The headliner here is the return of the fresh Health app: After briefly testing the redesigned Health app in an early iOS 27.2 beta, Apple has put the revamped app back in the recent beta cycle.

Apple historically releases an iOS patch in December, so I expect iOS 27.3 to land on iPhones later this year.

Industry observers note that since this is a beta, I recommend downloading it on something other than your primary device. This isn’t the final version of iOS 27.3, so the upgrade might be buggy and battery life may be short, so it’s best to keep those troubles on a secondary device.

Also, since this isn’t the final version, there could be more features to land on your iPhone when Apple releases 27.3.

Here are some features developers and beta testers can try now in the second iOS 27.3 beta.

The redesigned Health app returns in the iOS 27.3 beta after Apple tested the feature in the iOS 27.2 beta process. Developers and beta testers can explore the refreshed app and see things like a new Longevity tab and your Health Age.

Apple wrote online that we can expect the redesigned Health app to land on devices later this year.

If developers and beta testers have an Apple Watch that is running the watchOS 27.3 beta as well as an iPhone running the iOS 27.3 beta, those folks can test out Apple’s Live Rewind and Siri Recap in Audio Intelligence.

Live Rewind allows you to pull up a text transcript of a conversation in the past 15 seconds on your Apple Watch, and Siri Recap can automatically give you a summary of meetings, conversations and other events. Live Rewind snippets are replaced by new audio and then deleted, and Siri Recaps delete themselves after seven days if you don’t manually delete them sooner. However, you can also save both of these in the Siri app and export them to the Notes or Journal apps on your iPhone.

While both Live Rewind and Siri Recap are automatically deleted over time, I’m uncomfortable with the ability to save snippets or recaps, which raises concerns about people recording my conversations without my knowledge. Even if Audio Intelligence just summarizes what I said, I still find both features creepy.

And while I recognize the utility for certain groups of people, I also think it’s better to just, y’know… talk to someone instead of asking your watch what they just stated.

In a recent development, siri AI gets a huge update in the iOS 27.3 beta. The feature can now do more actions in supported apps, like Apple Music and Messages. For example, if you go into Apple Music, you can ask Siri to create a playlist for you, and in Messages, you can ask Siri to schedule, edit or unsend messages. If you open an app and ask Siri what it can do, the digital assistant should give you some examples of its capabilities.

You can also use Siri in Safari to scan an entire webpage — even parts of the page that aren’t in your direct view — to give you helpful information. So if you are looking at a menu online, you can ask Siri to find the gluten-free or vegetarian options.

The beta also brings Siri AI to traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish and Norwegian.

In the latest iOS 27.3 beta, developers and beta testers can find video podcasts in the Apple TV app, as well as in the Podcasts app. You can find video podcasts by going into the app, tapping Home across the bottom of your screen and scrolling down to the Video Podcasts section.

This means you can watch a video podcast in the Apple TV app on your iPhone while commuting, and then you can finish that video later on an Apple TV 4K or another device with access to Apple TV.

Industry observers note that each workout recommends exercises, reps, sets and weights in order to help you meet your goals. And if you’re unfamiliar with an exercise, you can also watch video tutorials to see how to perform that exercise.

StandBy mode also gets an upgrade in the iOS 27.3 beta. In the beta, you can add full weather and calendar slides to the mode and choose from more colors.

Apple introduced StandBy mode alongside iOS 17, and it was one of my favorite iPhone features. I’m happy Apple is finally showing it some love and adding more features and capabilities so it feels more like a home or desk hub.

If you’re a fan of dark mode, the iOS 27.3 beta has a treat for you. The beta gives you a upcoming setting in Safari called Adaptive Dark Mode. When enabled, it forces dark mode onto webpages in Safari that may not have a dark mode option otherwise.

Here’s where to find the option.

Industry observers note that 1. Tap Settings.2. Tap Apps.3. Tap Safari.4. Tap Adaptive Dark Mode.5. Tap On.

If you have an iPhone Duo and are running the iOS 27.3 beta, you have upcoming options to lock and unlock your device. In the beta, you can enable your device to lock simply by closing the Duo. You can find this option in Settings and within the Display & Brightness menu.

Next, people with the Duo can unlock the device using that phone’s front camera and without opening the foldable. You will have had to recently unlocked your device with Touch ID or your passcode. You can find this option in Settings and in the Touch ID & Passcode menu.

Recent findings suggest that those are a few of the new features developers can try now with the second beta of iOS 27.3. Apple has not said when exactly it will release iOS 27.3 to the general public, but we expect it to land on devices before the end of the year.

According to recent reports, just months after its release, Google is making its Spark agent free and officially renaming its capabilities “Tasks.” You can now toggle to it from the standard Gemini Chat setting. Reports show the rebrand started gradually in mid-October.

Industry observers note that also: Ready for a Siri AI agent? Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster.

In a recent development, openAI offers its Dots agents as part of its $100 per month ChatGPT Pro tier, and Anthropic’s Claude Duet is available with paid plans, which start at $20 per month. That makes Tasks and Meta Muse — the latter was called the “worst AI agent for privacy” by ZDNET’s David Gewirtz — Big Tech’s most affordable personal agents on the market, though you’ll have to pay for more than five hours of access at a time.

Industry observers note that if Tasks sounds familiar, it should: The manufacturer already has a product called Google Tasks, which lets you turn emails into a checkable to-do list on the side of your inbox, among other places like Chat and Docs. This is the agentic version, obviously.

Gewirtz, ZDNET’s AI tester-in-residence, wasn’t blown away by then-Spark when he tried it last month, but had reason to believe in its eventual improvement. It’s unclear whether Tasks is meaningfully different from Spark, aside from being out of beta.

Abilities aside, what sets Tasks apart here is cost. Dots and Duet haven’t exactly impressed thus far, so free alternatives don’t have a high bar to reach yet.

Also: I tested OpenAI Dot and Anthropic Duet for weeks.

During Gewirtz’s test, when the agent was part of his $20 per month Google AI Pro initiative, he used only 20% of the total five hours of usage on “four fairly substantial tests.” Without an AI plan, Gemini’s context window is 32k tokens.

Industry observers note that at launch in September, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg remarked Muse is “free to use for up to 100M tokens per week,” though Meta’s help center is not so explicit. As with most agentic products, more frequent users may want to buy more access, but more casual users now have two options to compare.

AI companies are vying to hook customers with their various personal agents, and price and privacy are major factors to consider. Being free with limits, Muse and Tasks are perhaps geared toward a more apprehensive user who wants to try an agent, but isn’t giving it countless tasks to take on all day. Given Muse’s reputation, some may find Tasks a bit less aggressive or risky.

According to recent reports, also: Don’t use Muse? How Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages.

As with other agents, Tasks, which runs on its newest Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, can handle a variety of jobs for you, from grocery shopping to booking appointments and analyzing your heating bill. Agents like these are designed for a chronically overwhelmed society trained by a reliance on tech to seek convenience and productivity in nearly every aspect of life.

Industry observers note that the feature is free in the US, Canada, Korea, Japan, Australia, and India. US owners can also start tasks by emailing or texting Gemini, and can have the agent call businesses for them (except in Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Montana, and Nebraska).

The change from Spark to Tasks comes just a day after Google retired Gems (which let you tailor Gemini to specific tasks), and converted existing Gems into Skills. The upcoming landing page for Tasks emphasizes personal finance and cost-cutting as a use case, positioning itself alongside personal finance features from Anthropic and OpenAI.

It has been revealed that “Put Gemini on the hunt for ways to save. Identify recurring expenses you no longer need, get alerts for your most-desired deals, and more,” the page reads.

AI agents remain a privacy and security risk, because of their ability to autonomously and proactively handle tasks like placing orders (which you can set spending caps for) and reviewing files.

It has been revealed that also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer.

“You can adjust task settings, disconnect Google and third-party apps, or delete chat history anytime,’ Google’s blog on the release said. Google’s upcoming Memory summary feature for Gemini lets owners view and edit the personal info the chatbot has on them.

But that reliance on AI means you’ll need the right type of iPhone to enjoy all the benefits.

The analysis draws on certain stats and lab data, such as your resting heart rate, sleep, heart rate variability (HRV), cholesterol, and A1C (average blood glucose levels), to deliver a health age, which may differ from your chronological age. The results can show you areas that may be of concern or that you need to focus on.

Also: Apple Watch Series 12 review: Finally, the health tracker I’ve been waiting for.

Apple promises that the analysis is performed on your device without recording, storing, or sharing the video.

In a recent development, the new app will be able to correlate your test results with data collected by your iPhone and Apple Watch to give you a more comprehensive picture of your health. Also: I tested the Apple Watch Series 12 heart-rate claims against my gold-standard Polar strap.

Available from the Insights section, a series of strength exercise videos are designed to help you build your body strength. The videos cover all the key areas of your body to give you a full workout.

Sources indicate that some of the newly introduced features, such as the strength videos, will be available to all iPhone users. But the ones that rely on AI will run only on phones that support Apple Intelligence. That means you’ll need an iPhone 15 Pro or Pro Max, any iPhone 16 or 17, an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max, an iPhone Air, or an iPhone Duo.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you think you've had a bad week, just be glad you're not on Nvidia's (NVDA -14.01%) management team.
  • Shares of the top AI stock fell 23% this week, wiping out roughly $1 trillion from its market cap.
  • Reuters mentioned that the SEC was investigating Nvidia's accounting practices, but did not provide many details beyond that.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jeremy Bowman – Nov 21, 2026 at 1:10AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

If you think you've had a bad week, just be glad you're not on Nvidia's (NVDA -14.01%) management team.

Shares of the top AI stock fell 23% this week, wiping out roughly $1 trillion from its market cap. It was its worst weekly performance since October 2008 during the height of the financial crisis. The slide was initially sparked by Jensen Huang's resignation the week before, and even a strong earnings report on Tuesday wasn't enough to stem the sell-off. On Friday, Nvidia stock plunged 14%, heading sharply lower in the afternoon after Reuters reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission had opened an investigation into the tech giant over accounting irregularities. That comes in addition to multiple investigations from different agencies and branches of the federal government over Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese agent and possible violation of chip export rules.

Reuters mentioned that the SEC was investigating Nvidia's accounting practices, but did not provide many details beyond that. Its report came three days after The Wall Street Journal said the SEC was investigating Nvidia, but did not say what for.

According to recent reports, given the other news last week and the Commerce Dept. issuing tighter chip export rules to Southeast Asia, the SEC probe could focus on how Nvidia reports geographic revenue, which potentially obfuscates where its chips end up. Last year, it changed how it records geographic revenue, shifting it from billing addresses to customer headquarters. As a result of that change, the manufacturer no longer reports revenue from Singapore as its own line item.

In fiscal 2026, Nvidia recorded $19.7 billion in revenue from customers headquartered in China, likely from permitted chips, though the SEC may be curious about how chips that ended up in China via other countries were recorded.

It's crucial for investors to understand that an investigation doesn't mean that Nvidia committed fraud, or that it will face any enforcement actions.

A probe is not evidence of wrongdoing, and many are closed without going further.

Industry observers note that given the other news surrounding Nvidia, the SEC probe seems less surprising and may not be as impactful on the stock as it otherwise would be, as the manufacturer is already in turmoil. Even a finding of wrongdoing wouldn't be a terminal event for Nvidia, though it could damage its reputation, in addition to any fines or consequences the company could face.

Executives at Super Micro Computer, a server-maker and close partner of Nvidia, were charged by the DOJ with conspiring to divert AI servers to China, though Supermicro's internal investigation found that no one on the senior management team was aware of the diversion scheme.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

It will take months or longer for the investigations into Nvidia to play out, and the company is likely to continue to receive scrutiny from the media in the wake of Huang's departure and the myriad investigations now surrounding it.

Investors will note that Nvidia's forward P/E has fallen all the way to 8 as the stock has plunged, but with so much uncertainty surrounding the stock, buying it seems speculative at this point, and the stock's future performance depends on what the investigations uncover.

Nvidia's "circular financing" is also in the spotlight after the change in leadership, and that could get attention from the SEC as well.

According to recent reports, there's simply so much we don't know about the stock and its future right now. Risk-tolerant investors may choose to buy the stock at the current price, but they should be aware that the volatility for Nvidia, after it's fallen for seven sessions in a row, is likely to continue.

Tech Report: Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want

  • “We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot presently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

“We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

“We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”.

Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz.

Alisson, Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo all made their first appearances and contributed to a lively first-half in which Iraola’s commitment to man-to-man marking and an intensive pressing structure were evident out of possession. With the ball in the first half they demonstrated the kind of slick passing that Bournemouth employed to carve opponents open on the counter-attack.

A nimble one-two between Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai allowed the Dutch midfielder to set up Alexander Isak to score with a shot from 16 yards and the most expensive player in English football history laid claim to the second, too, when he seemed to hook in a rebound from Lukas Hradecky’s save while lying in the six-yard box.

Later he would graciously acknowledge that he and Florian Wirtz had connected with the ball simultaneously and he was happy to yield the credit to his team-mate.

Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw.

Sources indicate that at that point it seemed that victory would be a cakewalk but just before half-time Aleksandr Golovin caught Van Dijk out with a feint and late swerve to the right, tripping over the Liverpool captain’s clumsy hack. Despite a heavy limp, Golovin hammered the penalty past Alisson’s dive to make it 2-1 at the break.

Iraola rationed his early changes at the start of the second half to two but Liverpool could not regain their rhythm and Mika Biereth capitalised on a Gravenberch error to score the equaliser after battling to be first to the rebound when Giorgi Mamardashvili saved his first effort, stroking his effort through Wataru Endo’s legs.

Sources indicate that cue five substitutions as soon as that goal had gone in and a raft more followed, killing the remaining half-hour of all momentum and cohesion. By the time Brunner exploited a dozy mix-up between Milos Kerkez and Federico Chiesa about whose responsibility he was at a corner to flash his header past Mamardashvili, only two of the 22 starters were still on the pitch.

According to recent reports, liverpool: Alisson (Mamardashvili 46), Tsimikas (Kerkez 59), Van Dijk (c) (Chambers 59), Ndukwe (Endo 46), Frimpong (Ramsay 75), Gravenberch (Nyoni 59), Gakpo (Ngumoha 59), Wirtz (McConnell 59), Koumas (Chiesa 75), Isak (Muñoz 59)Substitutes: Morrison, Davies.Goals: Isak (16), Wirtz (29)Monaco: Hradecky, Nazinho (Mawissa 75), Dier (c) (Kehrer 75), S Sané, Vanderson (Teze 46), Golovin (Idumbo 75), Cabral (Soubeir 75), Camara (Benzahra 64), Detourbet (Coulibaly 64), Biereth (Brunner 80), Abline (Konaté 64).Substitutes: Assab, Kohn, Lienard, Nibombe, Touré. Goals: Golovin (44 pen), Biereth (56), Brunner (88).

They played well in the first half, as they did against Leeds, but lost all shape and structure in the second half to lose 3-2.

It has been revealed that yellow card for Konate for clattering into Endo late. That’s the last of the action.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 3 (Brunner)  Brilliant near-post glancing header from a devilishly whippy, dipping corner. Kerkez doing his best Rip van Winkle impression.

Diligent defensive work by Ngumoha stops Konate’s run down the outside left.

It has been revealed that A final substitution, hopefully. Brunner replaces Biereth. Konate’s shot, a pearoller, is easily saved by Mamardashvili after A mix-up between Kerkez and Munoz.

In a recent development, as usual, the substitutions have killed the game. Watched Leeds vs RB Leipzig yesterday. They played two 60 minute matches which kept it more competitive for longer but still descended into a kickabout late on.

Mawissa, Kehrer, Idumbo and Soubeir have replaced Nazinho, Dier, Golovin and Cabral.

Monaco also made changes, four I think. Will catch up with then once they’re confirmed. Ramsey is into the game straight away tp stop Coulibaly’s shot.

Ramsay, Chiesa and Elliott are coming on for Szoboszlai, Frimpong and Koumas. Lovely applause for Elliott.

Recent findings suggest that konate sweeps a left-foot shot from the left of the box past the right post with Mamardashvili forced into a headlong dive. Liverpool have lost their defensive shape and intensity, allowing Monaco to punch holes through the lines with some direct running.

Nazinho gets round Frimpong down the Monaco left and cuts back the perfect pass to put it on a plate for Coulibaly who hammers a left-foot shot from the right of the D that Mamardashvili throws up his hands to block. That would have stung. Good save. A flag would have meant it wouldn’t have counted but even so Frimpong’s defensive work wasn’t good enough.

In a recent development, it’s been very scrappy since the changes but then Ngumoha pounces on to a loose ball, glides up the right and tries to play Koumas in behind the back four. Sadly, he overhits the pass which trickles out for a goal-kick. Cue an ovation and cries of ‘Rio! Rio!’.

Three changes for Monaco with Detoubet, Abline and Camara departing for Benzhara, Coulibaly and Konaté.

Ngumoha has gone to the right wing and Koumas is playing through the middle as a false nine.

Liverpool make five changes with Gakpo, Van Dijk, Wirtz, Tsimikas and Isak departing while Munoz makes his ‘debut’ with Ngumoha, Nyoni, Chambers, McConell and Kerkez.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 2 (Biereth) Mistake by Gravenberch allows Golovin to play a pass into the left half of the box for Biereth. His first shot is well saved by Mamardashvili at full stretch but his tenacity allowed him to get to the rebound ahead of Endo, swivel and stick his second effort in to equalise.

Monaco overplay at the edge of the box, Detourbet, Biereth and Abline playing ‘after you. Claud’, instead of shooting.

In a recent development, A slick, short passing move between Gravenberch, Wirtz and Isak ends with Isak on the deck in the box after Gravenberch’s step-over allowed the ball to run to him. Isak took a touch to move the ball on to his left but gave the defender a glimmer of it and he hacked it away before felling Isak as well as collateral damage.

Quiet start to the half. Biereth just pressed Mamardashvili but the keeper managed to sweep the ball away even though under more pressure than he would have expected.

Liverpool try to play out from the back with Mamardashvili spearing a straight pass to Gravenberch who tried to knock it round the corner for Endo but the ball skidded under his studs and out for a throw-in.

Sources indicate that isak is apparently claiming both goals. Replays are indistinct. He could have clipped it in off his heel as he had a swing at the ball while grounded at the same time as Wirtz.

Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw.

Endo has slotted in at centre-back alongside Van Dijk.

Half-time changes: Mamardashvili for Alisson and Endo for Ndukwe.

For Monaco, Teze for Vanderson at right-back.

In a recent development, much to admire in that first-half performance from Liverpool’s front six and centre-backs, the latter two particularly out of possession and winning it back. The man-to-man system is working well for them. But they should be out of sight by now instead of leading by only a goal.

Liverpool free-kick on the right after a foul on Koumas. Szoboszlai whips in the cross and Van Dijk gets up first to the left of the penalty spot but bludgeons his header about a foot wide of the right post.

Charlie Adam says the penalty was ‘a soft one’ but Van Dijk did not adjust when Golovin shifted it to his right, stuck out a leg and Golovim understandably decided to topple over the hurdle.

Recent findings suggest that liverpool 2 Monaco 1 (Golovin, pen) Speared it into the top right. Alisson went the right way but was beaten for pace and power.

Recent findings suggest that the referee, Jarred Gillett, gives Monaco a penalty. It was deserved, too. Golovin went on a driving run down the middle, shifted it to his right and was tripped by Van Dijk.

Liverpool are well worth their lead. They are streets ahead of Monaco.

A microcosm of the game so far: Liverpool pass goes astray, a player wins it back – this time Gakpo – by snapping into a tackle before laying it off to his left for the unmarked Tsimikas to skim a low shot about a foot wide of the left post from 25 yards.

Monaco have done very little since that wee salvo in the opening minute but just now Abline was given too much space from distance but whacked his shot into the Kop.

Big cheer from the crowd for Hugo Ekitike.

The impressive Koumas diddles Nazinho with a Cruyff turn but then thumps his shot straight into Hradecky’s chest.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 0 (Wirtz) Pass chipped out to Koumas down the right who arcs a cross to the back post. Gakpo meets it with a header back across goal to Isak whose first effort from a couple of yards is blocked but the ball gets stuck under Isak’s falling body and Wirtz is Johnny on the Spot to stab it in from a 18 inches as Dier tried to scramble it away.

Liverpool have been impressive so far but if there has been a weakness it’s still the balance in central midfield defensively. Going forward both Gravenberch and Szobiszlai have dovetailed together well. They win the ball back when Van Dijk steps out and the midfield two fly forward to tee up Koumas for a shot that strikes Dier.

Chance for Wirtz, who opens his body from the left of the D to try to bend a shot into the bottom right corner but fizzes it the wrong side of the post.

It’s been pretty breathless since the goal, Liverpool dozily letting Monaco through the middle before twice cutting Monaco apart in midfield only for Isak to overrun a pass in the box delivered by Wirtz and then Koumas to shoot over.

Recent findings suggest that liverpool 1 Monaco 0 (Isak) Chip to Gakpo down the left of the box, he clips it first time back to Gravenberch in the D who lays it off to Szoboszlai. Ping-ping-ping. Szoboszlai keeps the tempo high with return, the one in the one-two with Gravenberch who picks out Isak to bury a shot from about 15 yards into the bottom left corner.

Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz.

Excellent move from Liverpool, instigated by Ndukwe’s fine tackle on Biereth. He knocks it short to Gravenberch who arrows a 60-yard pass out to Koumas hurtling down the right. He measures his cross perfectly for Gakpo stealing in off the left wing and though he connects powerfully with the meat of his brow, he bashes it straight at the keeper. He was offside in any case, it transpires.

Charlie Adam on co-comms points out that Liverpool are going man-to-man now in classic Iraola/Bielsa style and when the camera goes high you can see it, especially with the full-backs.

Liverpool are carving the middle of the park up with incisive passing. Szoboszlai starts a move that sends Isak down the left of the box. He traps the chip, turns back to face away from goal and taps a pass back to Wirtz who gallops on to it and bends a shot that Hradecky dives low to his left to beat away with a firm left wrist. Frimpong pounces on the rebound and clips a tame effort straight at Hradecky who had swiftly restored himself to the vertical.

Van Dijk gobbles up a long pass over Ndukwe, snuffing out any possibility of Biereth getting there first.

It has been revealed that tsimikas is free down the left but overhits his cross on the run when Isak was begging for a cut-back. The left-back went for the back post and ballooned his centre behind, miles beyond Koumas and Wirtz.

In a recent development, liverpool defend the corner solidly and Frimpong races away on the counter, bombing on to the ball and sprinting into the Monaco half. But his touch is not as sound as his pace and Monaco deal with him when he fluffs his control.

A period of applause in memory of Kevin Keegan ❤️ pic.twitter.com/AkPZG7babe.

Liverpool kick off defending the Kop. They roll the ball back to Frimpong who chips a long pass up the right to Koumas who hares on to the pass down the right and crosses, just beyond Isak. Hradecky gathers and bowls the ball out. A mistake by Tisimikas lets Biereth barrel through the inside-right to hammer a shot that Alisson turns behind for a corner.

The crowd applauds in the modern way. My goodness he was a terrific player. Saw him play for Liverpool, Southampton and Newcastle. Absolutely relentless.

In a recent development, virgil van Dijk has the pennant. Liverpool are wearing all red with the paint splashes of the 1990 kit. Monaco are in a very pale green.

For me it’s a special game, most of the players and people will be ‘it’s [just] a pre-season friendly’, but for me it’s a lot more than this. It will be the first time I have the chance to go out, to feel this stadium and I hope we can also perform well.

It’s a good game for us, because it’s going to be demanding, it’s a team that wants to dominate and they also want to press high so we will see how we are.

I think the cases of Ali[sson], Cody, and Virgil I think it’s their first game. It shouldn’t go longer than 45 minutes, maybe a little bit more if they feel comfortable.

Also for some of the others Ryan, Flo, and Alex, it’s the second game so we have to be aware of those things.

But the league starts in two weeks, so we cannot wait also too much; we have to give them quality minutes.

Sources indicate that I think today is going to be a good reference, two games – Monaco and Como – teams that try dominate the game, they are very good in possession, so they will demand us the best without the ball. If we want to control the game and also physical teams, they are probably a very good test.

I hope we are at the level and we can do very good games.

Liverpool Alisson; Frimpong, Ndukwe, Van Dijk, Tsimikas; Szoboszlai, Gakpo; Koumaz, Wirtz, Gakpo; Isak.

Monaco Hradecky; Vanderson, Dier, Sané, Nazinho; Detourbet, Cabral, Camara, Golovin, Abline, Biereth.

Eric Dier captains Monagesques:.

Le 𝐗𝐈 qui débutera cette rencontre face à 𝐋𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐩𝐨𝐨𝐥 📋 pic.twitter.com/2cOYRbzUEN.

In a recent development, 🥳 Feliz aniversário, 𝐅𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐩𝐞 𝐋𝐮𝐢́𝐬! 🎉Notre coach fête aujourd'hui ses 41 ans 🎂 pic.twitter.com/VTd4BQ5rRK.

Alisson, Van Dijk and Gakpo return, Ndukwe continues in defence.

The Reds to take on AS Monaco at Anfield!Watch the match LIVE on All Red Video 📺.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the first of two Liverpool home friendlies after their preseason tour of the United States. Andoni Iraola’s side saw off Wrexham and Sunderland in their first two matches but gave away a two-goal lead at half-time in the final fixture and ended up being beaten 4-2 by Leeds United in Chicago in the last game after multiple changes. What did we learn? Not a huge amount in the absence of Virgil van Dijk, Alisson, Víctor Muñoz, Cody Gakpo and Alexis Mac Allister, the first four of whom are available today other than an ongoing vulnerability from set-pieces and Curtis Jones looking like he is in desperate need of a fresh start.

This afternoon at Anfield they take on AS Monaco who finished seventh in Ligue 1 this season but are under latest management with the recruitment of the former Chelsea and Atlético left-back Filipe Luís as head coach. It’s quite the coup for Le Rocher given he led Flamengo to their first Brazilian title in five years, the Copa Libertadores and the Copa do Brasil in his 18 months in charge.

In pre-season so far he has overseen a 5-2 win over fourth-tier AS Saint-Priest, a 2-0 defeat by Sporting Clube, a 2-2 draw with Cercle Bruges and a 1-0 victory over Getafe. They have sold their best player, Maghnes Akliouche, to PSG for £43m and Aladji Bamba to Newcastle for £34m but have so far retained Mamadou Coulibaly and Folarin Balogun, signed and made Ansu Fati’s loan move into a long-term deal.

Iraola may well persevere with Trey Nyoni in midfield who, after his performances on tour, ought to be on the threshold of a breakthrough season and it would be interesting to see him paired with Ryan Gravenberch just behind Dominik Szoboszlai.

Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who played well in America after coming on for the injured Joe Gomez, does not have a UK work permit and will have to go abroad on loan for the season but Jérémy Jacquet, who has yet to feature, was due to have a fitness test this morning and would be a welcome to boost to a squad whose defence still requires significant reinforcements.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Google Wallet app is available for iPhone users in the US for the first time.
  • Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.
  • The newly introduced Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Google Wallet app is available for iPhone users in the US for the first time. iOS users who download the fresh Google Wallet app can manage online payments for faster checkout at places that support Google Pay. However, Apple restricts Google’s ability to offer tap-to-pay service on the iOS app, so users won’t be able to use Google Wallet for contactless checkout on iPhone.

Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.

The newly introduced Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes. Google Wallet app users on iOS will also be able to view receipts and track orders pulled from Gmail in one app.

There used to be a Google Pay app for iOS, but it was discontinued in 2024. The old Google Pay app also didn’t support tap-to-pay on iPhone, but it offered limited functionality, including support for loyalty and gift cards, as well as purchase tracking.

The biggest difference between the old Google Pay app for iOS and the fresh Google Wallet is the AI component, which supports agentic shopping, likely as Google’s longer-term play.

According to recent reports, one of Google’s goals for the Wallet app on iOS is to make it a central place to manage purchases made by its AI agents. The Agents section in Google Wallet for iPhone lets you manage and monitor purchases made through Gemini.

Agentic commerce is on the rise, as evidenced by the growing use of Meta’s Muse. Gemini can make purchases and payments through the Tasks feature, which lets you give Gemini permission to buy the items you want and set your maximum budget.

Also: Google Wallet just turned your Android phone into a digital house key.

The Google Wallet app for iOS becomes the central hub for purchase management in agentic commerce through Gemini. In it, you can view active tasks to see which purchases Gemini is working on, as well as completed purchases and receipts.

Google has been working on two technologies to support its agentic commerce strategy: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) and Agent Payments Protocol (AP2).

UCP is a technical language that enables AI agents to communicate with retailers and make purchases, while AP2 is the payment framework that establishes rules and authorization for agents to make payments.

Google Wallet serves as both the AI-powered wallet and the consumer-facing record of transactions made by Gemini.

Also: Google Wallet has a lot of latest tricks – these 5 are my favorites.

Along with Google, major retailers supported the development of UCP, including Shopify, Walmart, Target, and Etsy. When Google announced AP2, more than 60 organizations became involved, including PayPal, Salesforce, Mastercard, and American Express.

According to recent reports, anthropic will use your location when using Claude to “improve product experience.” It will use your device’s IP address to identify your city and region, but you can disable this setting — to some extent. The Claude app will not request access to your location unless your prompt has a specific location-based query, like “What are some of the best sushi restaurants around me?” Only then will the app request permission.

However, if you already have given Claude access on Android or iOS, here’s how you can revoke permission.

I was surprised to see a section in the Settings of the Android app that I didn’t see on iOS, but it will also allow you to disable your location right from the app.

One thing to keep in mind is that turning your location off can affect features like searches that require your location, but Anthropic explicitly states that it collects your IP address to infer coarse-grained location to ensure usage of Claude complies with its terms and to prevent abuse — despite questionable allegations.

According to recent reports, like other AI chatbots, Claude has built-in “memory” so it can more easily have context about your conversations. Memory is on by default: The chatbot will remember personal preferences and other information and will be able to take that into consideration in other conversations, even if you don’t explicitly mention it in your current session.

In the web version of Claude, do the following to access your memory settings:.

To prevent Claude from creating latest memories from your conversations:.

Recent findings suggest that if you have had conversations with Claude that were sensitive in nature and still had the “Help improve our AI models” option enabled, odds are that Anthropic has already trained Claude on that conversation. There’s no way to change that.

Recent findings suggest that however, you should find those conversations in your chat history and delete them. After you’ve done that and disabled AI training on your conversations, you should opt for incognito mode for any further sensitive conversations you might want to have going forward.

Incognito chats aren’t saved in your history, nor are they used to train models.

Tech Report: 90% of employers reject resumes that look like AI – yet half use AI to interview

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1077 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, hiring managers are more suspicious than ever of AI use in applications, and it’s impacting who they consider.
  • New data from hiring systems firm Greenhouse found that “nine in ten US employers (90%) believe they’ve turned away real candidates because those applications seemed fake or AI-generated.” Greenhouse clarified that it doesn’t know whether employers are putting applications through AI detection tools or not.
  • It has been revealed that also: How many jobs is your state losing to AI?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, hiring managers are more suspicious than ever of AI use in applications, and it’s impacting who they consider. At the same time, they’re turning to AI to help screen more candidates — meaning those videos you’ve seen on the internet of people pranking AI interviewers aren’t going away anytime soon.

New data from hiring systems firm Greenhouse found that “nine in ten US employers (90%) believe they’ve turned away real candidates because those applications seemed fake or AI-generated.” Greenhouse clarified that it doesn’t know whether employers are putting applications through AI detection tools or not.

It has been revealed that also: How many jobs is your state losing to AI? This dashboard tracks the cuts – and the cost.

“The survey data is self-reported, so it reflects what employers believe has happened, not a measured outcome,” Greenhouse’s Head of Voice AI Ophir Samson told ZDNET via email.

Industry observers note that employers are also reacting to AI by adjusting their hiring processes: 86% of those surveyed reported changes to account for AI’s impact. 57% of them did so by adding another human interview.

“As jobseekers rely more on AI to polish and send out their job applications, employers are finding it harder to tell who’s actually right for the role,” the report stated, echoing an ongoing push-and-pull between applicants and hiring teams. AI resume screeners automatically toss a majority of applications they deem unfit, so applicants try not to get tossed by formatting their material for the screener, which then backfires anyway.

According to recent reports, the report indicates how a tough economy and an influx of AI hiring tools are colliding, arguably to benefit employers over applicants. Greenhouse noted that, ironically, AI tools are helping hiring managers while also making resumes untrustworthy, and applicants would rather be interviewed by AI than not at all.

Also: How to beat the AI algorithm and get the job of your dreams.

“A growing number of employers are using AI not just to filter candidates out, but to have conversations with more candidates, earlier, through AI-powered voice technology,” Greenhouse mentioned, adding that “half now use AI interviews to hear from more candidates, and 40% of those have found strong candidates they would have missed.”.

Greenhouse itself offers a voice AI screening interview tool. Samson told ZDNET that an HR professional ran 200 candidates she’d rejected through Greenhouse’s tool, and it suggested 19.

“All five of the finalists came from that group, and she ultimately hired one from the group,” Samson mentioned.

It has been revealed that what we don’t, and maybe can’t, know is the inverse: whether AI screeners influence hiring managers to turn away candidates they actually should have considered. At least in Greenhouse’s case, Samson stated Voice AI doesn’t make hiring decisions or “automatically advance, reject, or rank candidates.”.

“Recruiters review every output, and one recruiter owns the outcome and can explain how they reached it,” he remarked.

Greenhouse’s report surveyed 1,347 hiring managers and recruiters across the US, UK, Germany, Australia, and Ireland from late September to mid-October, and found that half of employers using voice AI “say the early-stage candidate experience has improved.”.

Also: ‘So perfect, they are literally identical’ – Your AI-polished resumes are recruiters’ upcoming top stressor.

It’s unclear what “improved” means there, though, and whether applicants themselves would agree with that. Still, when given the choice, only 7% of applicants in the US would turn down an AI interview, per an earlier Greenhouse report. Additionally, “70% of those who’ve had a live AI interview say it helped them show their skills,” that report noted.

In a recent development, but how swayed is that by the state of the US job market? October’s job report was better than expected, but it’s still been a tough year overall for job-seekers. Greenhouse’s findings could be as much a reflection of how desperate applicants are as an endorsement of or comfort with AI screenings.

“The job market could be a factor. Our Future of Hiring Candidate Report highlights 81% of job seekers were rejected from a job in the past year without speaking to anyone at the firm, human or AI,” Samson said. “But I’d be careful about reading the data as desperation. Candidates are setting clear conditions: nearly half (49%) want to know if a human will review their responses and 40% want to know how they’ll be evaluated.”.

Also: Why replacing staff with AI backfires – and 5 ways smart leaders generate real value instead.

Samson stated that a software engineer named Ryan Quinlan, who was hired at Blissway, initially thought “talking to an AI” sounded stranger, but that it ultimately “felt like a conversation” that let him mention skills he’d forgotten to include on his resume. Samson said that Ryan has been “a ‘maybe’ on paper,” but that the AI interview helped him get over the line to be considered.

It has been revealed that “For most applicants, a human conversation was never on the table,” Samson noted. “The real choice is a resume lost in a pile, or 15 minutes to tell their story.”.

Greenhouse found that while employers are using AI to screen more candidates, most are maintaining human oversight over the most key decisions in the hiring process.

“Of all the tasks employers would hand to an AI agent, deciding which candidates to advance came last, at just 7%,” Greenhouse mentioned.

A recent California law aims to protect employees from being fired by AI systems that make determinations about their performance without a human co-signing the assessment. As with many AI productivity tools in the workplace, proper adoption ideally equates to more time for human workers to handle more important tasks.

Also: 92% of HR say staff can train for AI jobs – but half of companies still hire outside.

“Of employers who’ve saved time with AI, 85% put it back into candidates, most often by spending more time with shortlisted candidates (45%) and interviewing more candidates earlier (40%),” Greenhouse remarked.

The main question around AI interviewers remains whether they’re correctly capturing your interview the way you’d hope a human interviewer would (though that’s still deeply subjective and out of applicants’ control anyway).

Recent findings suggest that “When AI interviews are implemented thoughtfully and transparently, they pay off for both candidates and recruiters,” Samson said. “Every candidate who uses our Voice AI can opt out, and about 90% rate the experience as excellent.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Meta promised to be carbon-neutral and water-positive by 2030 — that is, the firm would offset as much carbon dioxide as it created and return more water to local watersheds than it used.
  • In Meta’s 2026 sustainability report, released on Thursday, Meta’s data center and sustainability chiefs wrote that the tech giant is “re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets.” In an emailed statement to CNET, a Meta spokesperson added, “We remain committed to net zero, but are re-evaluating the 2030 timeline … We’ll continue to invest in emissions reductions.”.
  • Industry observers note that it’s a disappointing, if unsurprising, announcement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Meta promised to be carbon-neutral and water-positive by 2030 — that is, the firm would offset as much carbon dioxide as it created and return more water to local watersheds than it used. But like every Significant Tech company, Meta is sacrificing its climate goals for artificial intelligence and the data centers needed to run it.

In Meta’s 2026 sustainability report, released on Thursday, Meta’s data center and sustainability chiefs wrote that the tech giant is “re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets.” In an emailed statement to CNET, a Meta spokesperson added, “We remain committed to net zero, but are re-evaluating the 2030 timeline … We’ll continue to invest in emissions reductions.”.

Industry observers note that it’s a disappointing, if unsurprising, announcement. Microsoft, Amazon and Google have also all backtracked on their climate goals in their rush to build hyperscale data centers, the turbocharged server farms needed to keep AI online. Microsoft’s president, Brad Smith, said in 2023 that the company’s net zero goal was “before the explosion in artificial intelligence.”.

Meta’s net emissions in 2025 were 11.8 million metric tons of carbon dioxide, a 45% increase year over year, the company says. Carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases are primary drivers of the climate crisis, worsening natural disasters, causing more extreme weather patterns and disrupting the lives of everyone and everything on the planet.

According to recent reports, take one of Meta’s Louisiana data centers, Hyperion, for example. CEO Mark Zuckerberg revealed the behemoth in 2025, showing how the facility is nearly the size of Manhattan. When it comes online in 2030, it’s expected to create two gigawatts of capacity for AI, with the ability to scale in the future. But it also requires equally massive demands on the state’s energy grid.

Meta details in length its strategies for mitigating the environmental impact of its work, including improved water-use efficiencies in its data centers and approximately 77% less embodied carbon in its fresh data center designs compared to its original ones.

It has been revealed that but, again, AI has made an indelible mark on those efforts. The firm also reports that its electricity consumption “increased 35% year over year as additional data centers came online.”.

Meta wrote that “demand for AI infrastructure has grown faster than almost anyone projected.” Arguably, as one of the biggest hyperscalers driving the buildout of AI infrastructure here in the US and abroad, Meta should have known.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The debasement trade is gaining newly introduced traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.

It has been revealed that the conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S. dollar and Treasury debt in the face of ballooning government spending. Those fears reached a fever pitch last week before, and after, the Treasury Department's unusual step of increasing debt buybacks under Secretary Scott Bessent.

"The size of the Treasury purchases unveiled so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," remarked Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.

Gold touched three-month highs Monday, building on last week's advance of more than 5%. The yellow metal has climbed for five straight weeks and in August is on track for its biggest monthly rise since 1999.

According to recent reports, bitcoin added 2% Monday, to the highest since May. Last week, the digital currency soared 22%, its biggest three-day rally since 2023. Overnight Tuesday, the crypto touched $80,000.

Conversely, investors fled the dollar.

The U.S. dollar index, which tracks the dollar against six other leading currencies, hit three-month lows last week and recorded its third down week in the last four. The index was little changed on Monday as investors expressed little appetite to bid up the greenback.

It has been revealed that the Treasury Department stated last week that it would double the maximum size of its bond buyback, to at least $4 billion from $2 billion. Two senior Treasury officials told CNBC Monday that the department could use its General Account to help fund the intends.

According to recent reports, last week's announcement followed news that the monthly U.S. budget deficit in July reached a five-year high and came at the same time as total federal government debt topped $40 trillion. Bessent told CNBC last week that he wields a "substantial toolkit" to calm the government bond market amid concerns about the government's financial health.

Long-dated U.S. Treasury yields surged last week, at one point sending the 30-year yield to almost a 20-year high of 5.34%, up from 4.82% in late June. Yields dipped and then rebounded in the wake of the Treasury buyback move, a signal that bond investors believed Bessent's moves were inadequate.

"Markets are saying something," the billionaire philanthropist and former energy trader John Arnold stated in a Friday post on X. The weaker dollar, lower Treasury prices and strengthening hard assets, are "all part of the debasement trade," he wrote.

The Treasury's moves could aid the bond market, but also translate into outsized pain for the dollar, according to Nohshad Shah, Citadel Securities' head of fixed income sales for Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

According to recent reports, the stakes are high for monetary policymakers, as a weaker greenback can ease financial conditions, Shah said. U.S. inflation — above the Federal Reserve's 2% target for five years — could worsen.

Industry observers note that the Fed might need to hike interest rates in response, Shah noted. Fed funds futures reflect about a 56% chance the central bank raises borrowing costs at its October meeting, up more than seven percentage points from a week ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Sources indicate that "The bond market's message is straightforward: fiscal or monetary policy should be tighter," Shah remarked in a Monday note. "Households may ultimately pay for policymakers' unwillingness to fix the roof whilst the sun is shining.".

Recent findings suggest that coltman at 21Shares remarked the appetite for alternative stores of value also stems from mounting geopolitical tension. The U.S. on Monday rolled out a global sanctions program focused on segregating Iran from the global economy, days after slapping 50% tariffs on billions of dollars in Canadian exports.

Still, assets that would benefit from a debasement trade have recently received votes of confidence on Wall Street.

Sources indicate that deutsche Bank analyst Michael Hsueh mentioned in a Monday note that gold could surpass his target price of $4,800 an ounce. Already, that level suggests the precious metal only need to rise another 3% or so from where it closed on Friday. "We see the Treasury policy change as underlining the gold constructive view," Hsueh said.

It has been revealed that billionaire investor Ray Dalio recommended investors remain overweight gold and bitcoin ahead of what he warned could become a debt crisis in the U.S. as a result of unchecked government spending. Gold could account for as much as 15% of a model portfolio, the Bridgewater Associates founder said.

"The government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote on LinkedIn Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

Others are less sure, devaluing the notion of a debasement trade.

It's probably too early to endorse the idea unless it's clear that the Fed will go along with the Treasury Department, mentioned Alexander Lis, investing chief at Social Discovery Ventures.

By Dave Kovaleski – Nov 21, 2026 at 1:39AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Target ›.

Value stocks have dominated growth stocks over the past year, an about-face from the previous three years of this market.

The Vanguard Morningstar Value ETF (VTV -1.62%) is up 17% over the past 12 months, while its large-cap counterpart, the Vanguard Morningstar Growth ETF (VUG -5.32%) is up just 1%.

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (599 w)

Signal Is Blocking Screenshots to Protect Your Messages from AI Agents

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (599 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Don’t ask your AI agent to read and decipher that lengthy text message.
  • The privacy-focused messaging and calling app is rolling out a new default setting to stop built-in smartphone AI agents from potentially seeing and saving your Signal data.
  • That threatens Signal’s mission to guarantee privacy, Whittaker wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Don’t ask your AI agent to read and decipher that lengthy text message. And don’t screenshot it either. It may seem harmless, but Signal’s latest setting underlines that it isn’t.

The privacy-focused messaging and calling app is rolling out a new default setting to stop built-in smartphone AI agents from potentially seeing and saving your Signal data. In a blog post announcing the change, Signal President Meredith Whittaker said these AI bots scan what’s on your screen to get to know you, capturing your data and making it available to AI systems to fulfill your requests, such as answering questions you may ask.

That threatens Signal’s mission to guarantee privacy, Whittaker wrote. So it’s putting a stop to it with a default setting to block screenshots in the Signal app on iOS 27 and when AI assistants try to capture information on Android screens by default.

Whittaker said that this isn’t the first time Signal has taken such measures against an operating system. Last year, it blocked screenshots of Signal messages from Microsoft’s Recall AI on Windows 11.

Now the firm is taking a similar approach to Apple’s iOS 27 and Android operating systems, where AI assistants try to read your Signal screen.

Sources indicate that the problem is the same for the three major OS companies. Microsoft, Google and Apple are incorporating AI into their operating systems, and Signal states that compromises the space for third-party developers, including Signal, to build apps for these systems.

“Right now, these agentic AI integrations are changing this environment in a way that’s making it increasingly hostile to privacy,” Whittaker wrote.

Whittaker remarked the screenshot setting won’t fix everything, because AI agents can still sneakily access data on your phone. Tech companies should take steps to give developers more choice, such as an opt-out to disable AI agent access, and provide more documentation on how big tech AI agents work.

Recent findings suggest that “Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience,” Whittaker mentioned. “This is also the reason we are presently unable to implement these protections on MacOS.”.

In a recent development, in most cases, text messages are encrypted when they travel between devices. But AI agents can bypass that. John Strand, CEO of Black Hills Information Security, explained that when you access the information, it has to be decrypted because you cannot read encrypted data.

“So, if an AI agent can access screenshots or directly observe what’s happening on your screen, it can read those messages without ever having to break the encryption itself,” noted Strand. “That’s the scary part. You can have incredibly strong encryption, but if something can see what the user sees, that encryption isn’t going to protect you at that point.”.

If you want to take screenshots in Signal, you can disable the setting, but that could mean AI agents could access you and your senders’ information, like text messages and shared files such as photos.

According to recent reports, strand mentioned the worst-case scenario is that an attacker could see everything you see, from private conversations to passwords. And that’s what Signal is trying to avoid.

“They want to make sure that if something like this happens, they’ve done absolutely everything they reasonably can to protect their customers and the information being accessed through their application,” Strand stated.

Signal, Apple and Google did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
