💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hyundai pulled back the cover on the latest 2027 Elantra sedan and 2028 Elantra Hybrid this week at the LA Auto Show, and, wow, it looks like nothing else in its class.
  • The humble Hyundai Elantra hasn’t historically been a sexy car, but it remains an important one for the brand.
  • Industry observers note that the updated hybrid powertrain pairs a 1.6-liter four-cylinder gasoline engine with a 6-speed dual-clutch automatic gearbox.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hyundai pulled back the cover on the latest 2027 Elantra sedan and 2028 Elantra Hybrid this week at the LA Auto Show, and, wow, it looks like nothing else in its class. The bold styling may not be for everyone — though, personally, I dig it — but economy car shoppers will certainly be interested in the compact hybrid sedan’s targeted 53 mpg and Gleo, Hyundai’s new AI voice assistant that controls the automaker’s new Android Automotive OS-based dashboard tech.

The humble Hyundai Elantra hasn’t historically been a sexy car, but it remains an important one for the brand. It’s the automaker’s second-bestselling vehicle, behind only the Tucson. More importantly, the Elantra is one of the stalwarts of the affordable compact sedan class, a segment that many US automakers have abandoned in favor of more profitable SUVs. At a time when buyers are more sensitive than ever to inflated fuel costs and sticker prices, economy car options like the Elantra and its second-generation hybrid powertrain are worth our attention.

Industry observers note that the updated hybrid powertrain pairs a 1.6-liter four-cylinder gasoline engine with a 6-speed dual-clutch automatic gearbox. Combined output at the front wheels rises to 155 horsepower (up from 139 hp in the current car), thanks to a more powerful 45-kilowatt electric-assist motor (up from 32kW).

Recent findings suggest that an updated regenerative braking system recaptures energy when slowing and now offers an “EV-like one-pedal driving experience” that can bring the car to a complete stop at its maximum setting. Additionally, the hybrid now features a upcoming Stay mode that lets the climate control and infotainment systems run while parked for up to 30 minutes without firing up the gas engine.

Recent findings suggest that sharing the stage in LA, the fresh nonhybrid Elantra arrives with the same 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine and continuously variable transmission as the current generation. At 147 hp with a target of 35 mpg combined, it’s no more powerful than before, but it should also be no less efficient, despite the sedan’s increased size. I’d say the hybrid is the better choice, though it will likely also be the more expensive powertrain option.

In a recent development, inside, a upcoming cockpit design moves the now-hoodless digital instrument cluster, a 9.9-inch “Slim Information Display,” away from the driver and toward the windshield on the dashboard. The new placement, similar to what I’ve seen on recent Toyota models, puts vehicle information closer to the driver’s line of sight.

It has been revealed that pleos Connect, Hyundai’s new Android Automotive OS-based infotainment suite, lives on a 12.9-inch center display. Despite being based on Android, it still features the automaker’s bespoke navigation and media software, rather than Google Maps. The system is said to be over-the-air updatable and features standard wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto for drivers who’d rather bring their own apps on the road.

Sources indicate that the Pleos dashboard OS is matched with Gleo AI (who names these things?!), which is Hyundai’s latest AI voice assistant that lets drivers and passengers talk to the car rather than occupy a hand on the touchscreen. Hyundai indicates the system features “contextual language support, multi-command capability and zone-specific recognition,” which basically means the car knows who’s talking to it and which seat they’re in and can assign context to voice prompts based on the situation.

In a recent development, “Affordable doesn’t have to be anonymous,” noted Olabisi Boyle, Hyundai’s senior vice president of product, at the unveiling. I agree: Hyundai’s designers clearly aren’t afraid to push the design envelope, and the new Elantra is anything but bland.

Sources indicate that the sedan introduces the automaker’s Art of Steel design language, with chunky flared fenders that feel inspired by the brand’s recent new SUVs. The tall greenhouse looks a bit cartoonish if you catch it at the wrong angle, but it provides increased headroom inside. From certain angles, the sedan’s beefy fenders remind me of an angular Korean take on the Subaru WRX. From other viewpoints, I can see inspiration from Hyundai’s N Vision 74 concept and the hydrogen-fueled Nexo, particularly in the triangular rear windows.

In a recent development, the sedan measures 188.8 inches bumper-to-bumper on a 108.3-inch wheelbase that is 1.2 inches longer than the current model’s. Hyundai says the stretch for this generation improves rear-passenger space, now rated at 39.1 inches of legroom on the second row. The Elantra, according to its designers, now approaches the interior volume of a midsize car, a claim I’d take with a grain of salt had I not watched multiple six-foot-plus attendees slip into the back seat with relative ease.

In a recent development, hyundai did not announce pricing or detailed specs at the auto show debut, and availability is still vague. However, based on the stated model years, which are usually slightly offset from calendar years, I expect the 2027 Elantra sedan to arrive in early 2027, with the 2028 Elantra Hybrid following in late 2027.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Black Friday comes but once a year — although sometimes it feels like it lasts for a month.
  • Recent findings suggest that if you’ve been sitting on a holiday shopping list and waiting for prices to drop, we’ve got good news: It’s time to start your shopping engines!
  • In a recent development, you don’t need a calendar full of sale dates to navigate the shopping frenzy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Friday comes but once a year — although sometimes it feels like it lasts for a month. The major day is Nov. 27, but the sales have already started.

Recent findings suggest that if you’ve been sitting on a holiday shopping list and waiting for prices to drop, we’ve got good news: It’s time to start your shopping engines! (So to speak.).

In a recent development, you don’t need a calendar full of sale dates to navigate the shopping frenzy. Focus on the categories likely to offer the biggest savings. Here’s what to buy, and what can wait.

If you’ve got top-priority toys on your list, buy them at a discount if you can find them, claims Kristin McGrath, senior editor at The Krazy Coupon Lady, “just in case they don’t go down in price later.”.

Industry observers note that non-electronic toys are a good bet, says Julie Ramhold, consumer analyst with DealNews.com, because they’re less affected by tariffs on electronic components. That includes Legos, dolls and playsets.

Industry observers note that neeDoh squishies are a hot stocking stuffer this year and may be in short supply. At authorized retailers like Target, they should be relatively affordable, but try to avoid unauthorized resellers who may crank up the price, Ramhold claims.

While you may see mattress stores offering a few doorbusters on Black Friday, don’t feel pressured to jump on a deal.

“Mattresses tend to see some of their strongest discounts around major sales events like Labor Day and Presidents Day,” indicates Ashley Feinstein Gerstley, shopping and savings strategist with Rakuten. “So if you’re not in a rush, it may be worth waiting for one of those windows.”.

Similarly, bedding and towels are often on deep discount during January white sales, Feinstein Gerstley notes.

In a recent development, got some counter space and an itch for a new food processor? Black Friday sales are a great time to price surf for countertop appliances, including blenders, juicers and air fryers.

Holiday decor is only a must-buy during Black Friday sales if you need it for this holiday season.

Electronics are typically a slam-dunk buy at this time of year. “Every store is competing for your business, so televisions, headphones, tablets, laptops — they’re all going to be on sale at the same time,” McGrath notes.

According to recent reports, for best results, research the exact specs of the product you want and put it in your cart ahead of time, says consumer savings expert Andrea Woroch. That way, if a similar (but not identical) product goes on sale, you won’t accidentally buy the wrong thing.

You’ll usually find deeper discounts on items that are associated with fitness resolutions after Upcoming Year’s Day.

“Significant-box retailers like Target and department stores like Macy’s will offer up to 40% off or more on both fitness equipment and activewear during early January sales,” Ramhold indicates.

Many fashion retailers offer Black Friday sales, McGrath notes. So if there’s an item you stock in multiple colors or a work staple you need to replace, keep an eye on your favorite sites for the markdowns.

Shoes, too, are a category to eyeball, including seasonal buys and everyday options like running shoes, Ramhold notes. “Some retailers may offer a BOGO promotion of some kind, but it’ll likely just be a ‘buy one, get one for 50% off,’” she says.

According to recent reports, just shop early for your size and color before inventory runs low, McGrath states. “You don’t want to miss out if there's a great deal.”.

In a recent development, one caveat: Winter apparel will usually see bigger discounts toward the end of the year, Woroch claims. So wait on your boot and coat purchases if you can.

Black Friday also offers the chance to snag deals on things you can use throughout the year:.

Photo gifts: Whether you’re ordering holiday cards or putting together a photo book for your in-laws (or yourself), you can usually find sales from vendors like Snapfish and Shutterfly, among others.

Spa services: Check local businesses for deals on massages, manicures and other self-care treatments.

Streaming subscriptions: If you’re a upcoming customer (or canceled at least a month ago), some streaming platforms offer deep Black Friday discounts.

Black Friday deals are as much about strategy as savings, so make sure you’re maximizing your spending with these tips:.

Let AI help. Tools like ChatGPT and Gemini can do a lot of the legwork for you. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • 10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›.
  • Few companies that have undergone more radical changes recently than Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%), whose co-founder and chief executive officer, Jensen Huang, abruptly resigned earlier this month.
  • Nobody knows for certain what Nvidia's future holds, and it may hinge on who fills the CEO role.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Keithen Drury – Nov 21, 2026 at 4:00AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›.

Few companies that have undergone more radical changes recently than Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%), whose co-founder and chief executive officer, Jensen Huang, abruptly resigned earlier this month. Although there are calls from investors and employees to bring him back, the board of directors has stated that it has no interest in doing that.

Nobody knows for certain what Nvidia's future holds, and it may hinge on who fills the CEO role. However, there is another company that could benefit from this: Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -7.69%). SpaceX is a client of Nvidia's, so how can it benefit?

Well, SpaceX's CEO, Elon Musk, has already made it publicly known that he would love to have Huang run his Terafab division, the manufacturer’s huge factory designed to build compute hardware. That would certainly bring on an excellent technology leader who knows the industry inside and out, but there are no official reports that this is being considered at this time.

So, can SpaceX still benefit from all of this? Let's take a look.

Sources indicate that terafab is SpaceX's semiconductor manufacturing project in Texas. Both SpaceX and Tesla (TSLA -7.64%) are involved in it, along with Intel (INTC -7.97%). Should Terafab come into existence, its primary competitor would be Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM -9.48%).

In a recent development, taiwan Semiconductor is a semiconductor manufacturer that supplies the world with the vast majority of advanced chips. Companies like SpaceX and Tesla cannot get enough chips fast enough, so they are looking to build their own fabrication facilities to replace them. Terafab also integrates memory chip production, so companies like Micron (MU -13.89%) are also in competition with Terafab. Terafab would only supply chips to SpaceX and Tesla, so it wouldn’t challenge Taiwan Semiconductor or Micron for sales to their other customers.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

In a recent development, chip production is no easy business, and countless advanced technologies are difficult to replicate and take years of knowledge. But if a large amount of knowledge could be imported via Jensen Huang, then Terafab could have a shot at success.

Still, it's important to remember that while Huang ran a chip company, the company was mostly centered on design. Nvidia only designs graphics processing units (GPUs), the computing engines inside data centers; it doesn’t manufacture them. Although designing high-tech products requires knowing how they are made, there is a difference between knowing a process and having hands-on experience doing it and troubleshooting it when things go wrong. Huang's knowledge would be a game changer for SpaceX and Tesla, but it may not be enough to crack into this industry.

Although Huang may be a top option for the job, this is still another bold business launch by Musk, and it will be years before this facility is operational.

So, can SpaceX really benefit from Huang’s absence at Nvidia?

There's no doubt that Jensen Huang shaped the design path of Nvidia. The whole world benefited from his prescience and leadership, whether they know it or not, and his shoes will be hard, if not impossible, to fill.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Depending on who is selected as the next CEO of Nvidia, the technical visionary mindset needs to be replicated; otherwise, Nvidia won't be the same manufacturer. This is a huge risk for any company that is currently deploying Nvidia products, such as SpaceX.

In a recent development, spaceX informed investors during its Q2 conference call that it is exclusively using Nvidia products for the foreseeable future. Musk made that decision because Nvidia's upcoming Rubin architecture is best in class. That technology won't change with Huang not in the CEO role, so SpaceX will likely continue to deploy Nvidia hardware.

So, at the end of the day, unless Huang chooses to lead Terafab for Musk, SpaceX is likely better off with Huang in the CEO role at Nvidia. The same could be stated of a whole host of other AI companies that use Nvidia products. But with Nvidia’s board declaring that there is no path for return, it seems likely that Huang’s future lies elsewhere.

In a recent development, “Our cofounders have had many people come up to them and say, ‘Hey, I run a mahjong night on Wednesdays’ or ‘I go to this local bar in Chicago with like five people, and we love playing go, but we lack a Chess.com,’” chief growth officer Albert Cheng states in an interview with The Verge. “The way that Chess.com has grown this community of almost 300 million members has not really happened for a lot of these other types of classic games.”.

It has been revealed that classic Games is aimed at filling that gap. Some of the fresh games, like shoji or xiangqi, are strategy games similar to chess while others are further afield, like sudoku, solitaire, and word. The Classic team chose the new games through “a mix of community feedback, market research, and then just our own confidence in our ability to serve that game well,” Cheng indicates. It’s focused on classics that “have some sort of lifelong journey of learning and a community.”.

Classic Games will feel familiar if you’ve ever played a match on Chess.com. Each game has lessons, leaderboards, and a rating system. Multiplayer games like checkers or mahjong have options for matches against other players or bots, and they use the same bot characters that Chess.com has. (Martin remains the lowest-rated bot across the board, whether it’s on Chess, Gambit, or Classic.) Not all of the games have the same play modes — word and mahjong have puzzles like chess, while sudoku has a set of daily grids and solitaire has daily deals.

The expansion hasn’t put Chess.com itself on the back burner, according to Cheng. If anything, it’s never been better. “Chess is more and more so in the public zeitgeist than I’ve ever seen it, frankly, during my time here,” Cheng notes. “Our daily active consumers are higher than they’ve ever been during the organization’s history.” He declined to share exactly how many daily users Chess.com presently has but remarked the site is “doing amazingly well.”.

Sources indicate that so, while the company is expanding beyond its domain name, chess remains its primary focus. “The amount of folks that are fully dedicated toward building newly introduced games is less than 1 percent of the company,” according to Cheng.

According to recent reports, AI played a key role in helping Chess.com launch 11 new games in a matter of months with a team of only a few people. Earlier this year, Cheng told The Verge his team built Gambit with the help of AI, mainly for coding tasks. He says they used “almost entirely the same approach” for Classic, with AI helping to speed up the coding process again.

“Because these games are built on top of the Chess.com code base and design system and bot characters and rating systems, it’s a huge advantage and allows us to move very promptly alongside AI to bring these types of games to market with a very small team,” Cheng notes. “As we create more and more games, the adjacent games that can be created to it just happen much faster because the infrastructure is there, as opposed to standing everything up from scratch.”.

It has been revealed that AI wasn’t used for Classic Games’ art and design, Cheng indicates. “The look and feel of it is very carefully crafted by humans, and we’re proud of that,” he says. “The truth is, it really is a blend. It’s a small team of really talented folks that have good product and design judgment, and they’re leveraging AI.”.

“We are fortunate in some ways that AI and chess have been intermixed for 30-ish years.”.

Industry observers note that chess.com’s comfort with AI may come from the fact that human chess players have now spent decades playing and learning alongside machines. “We are fortunate in some ways that AI and chess have been intermixed for 30-ish years,” Cheng indicates, calling back to Garry Kasparov’s 1996 chess match against IBM’s Deep Blue supercomputer. “Even before the company was founded 20 years ago, the idea that AI was super powerful at the game of chess was embedded in how the cofounders thought about the company.”.

Elsewhere in the games industry, there’s been increasing tension over the use of AI. Cheng notes that while Chess.com may be using AI to “accelerate” coding tasks, the creative side of things has become more vital. “On the art and the design side, the ratios are shifting a decent amount, where we’re hiring more of those folks,” he says, adding that the organization has “shipped a lot more major features in Chess.com than in previous years” using what they’ve learned from Classic Games’ faster development process.

Chess.com might not be done growing its library of games, either. Cheng noted it will likely expand to “a lot more” games in the future.

  • Many owners responded with good ideas: File for unemployment, try to avoid tapping into retirement savings, and cut expenses as much as possible.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Redditor recently shared that they were struggling to decide which financial steps to take first after a job loss.

In a recent development, should they withdraw money from retirement savings to have more cash on hand — but pay an early withdrawal penalty? Or is it better to rely on the severance payout to handle expenses?

Many owners responded with good ideas: File for unemployment, try to avoid tapping into retirement savings, and cut expenses as much as possible.

For more ideas, I asked three financial experts how to manage money in the immediate aftermath of job loss.

While it’s tempting to make quick decisions about tapping into a retirement fund or selling a house, it’s better to wait on any big moves, says Parker Wine, retirement planning advisor at the financial firm Daniel A. White & Associates in Lewes, Delaware.

In a recent development, that’s because you need time to digest the situation and weigh the pros and cons of different options, he notes. “People can get impulsive and panic, and it’s usually a bad thing to make decisions when you’re panicking,” he says.

Take your time, get second opinions and think through all of your options first, Wine suggests.

If you’re fortunate enough to receive a severance package, wait to sign it until you’ve reviewed it carefully and understand all of the details, says John Rafferty, partner and investment advisor representative at Solomon Financial in Carmel, Indiana.

For example, make sure you know about your health insurance options, such as whether you’ll receive insurance through COBRA or need to take out a upcoming policy in the health insurance marketplace.

Filing for unemployment and checking into any other available workplace benefits — such as help with your latest job search — is also an notable part of understanding what support to expect in the weeks and months ahead, Rafferty adds.

Creating a bare-bones budget stripped of “extras” like restaurant meals or travel can help the severance payment last as long as possible, Rafferty says.

“Now that you don’t have income coming in, ask yourself, ‘How much can I spend and where?’”.

You might be able to cut back on entertainment costs, coffee runs and clothing purchases, for example.

At the same time, it’s important to prioritize the essentials like mortgage payments, rent, utilities and food. Rafferty recommends calling your mortgage company, utilities provider and any other lenders to ask if they have a hardship program for those experiencing financial challenges.

Opting in could give you more time to pay your bills or temporarily lower payments.

Sources indicate that it’s hard to stick to a budget that eliminates all entertainment, so Rafferty suggests finding enjoyable activities that come with a low price tag. Hiking, discovering a new park and participating in free community events are all ways to enjoy downtime on a budget.

In a recent development, “Having that release is mentally a big thing so you can stay prepared for the job search,” he says. “Otherwise, it’s easy to get down and feel negative, and we need things to help us feel positive.”.

Similarly, connecting with friends and family during this time is crucial, states Laura Adams, accredited financial counselor and financial coach in Wilmington, North Carolina.

Recent findings suggest that people often feel a sense of shame or embarrassment after job loss, and Adams encourages people to talk about their feelings and ask for help if needed. “Financial shame can cause us to make emotional rather than confident financial decisions,” she claims.

Recent findings suggest that starting some kind of side hustle to bring in extra cash can also help bridge the gap between the job loss and your next job, Wine states. Substitute teaching, working at a local public golf course and driving for a rideshare service are all options he’s seen people try.

Doing something new also helps stave off boredom while unemployed, but he cautions that you’ll still owe taxes on any side income you bring in, so blueprint accordingly.

According to recent reports, all three financial experts also emphasized that a job loss is easier to handle with an emergency savings fund you can turn to, and suggested building one up — ideally three to six months’ worth of expenses. But starting small helps, too — while employed, if possible.

Recent findings suggest that the Redditor who posted the question mentioned that, like many Americans, they lacked emergency savings. This added urgency to the question of what to prioritize.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sean Williams – Nov 21, 2026 at 4:06AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

The stock market has endured some of its most volatile days in history under President Donald Trump. Nevertheless, the iconic Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI -1.93%), benchmark S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%), and tech-fueled Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -5.28%) have averaged higher returns under Trump than under most other presidents since the late 1890s.

In a recent development, some of this outperformance can be traced directly to Trump's policies. The signing of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act into law in December 2017 slashed the peak marginal corporate income tax rate from 35% to 21%, leading to record share buybacks by S&P 500 companies.

It has been revealed that but the bulk of Wall Street's gains comes courtesy of the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution and the ongoing AI data center build-out. AI is the largest addressable opportunity investors have ever seen, which explains why the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite have blasted to several record highs.

Industry observers note that persistently elevated inflation is a serious problem for President Trump's economy and Wall Street. Image source: Official White House Photo by Andrea Hanks, courtesy of the National Archives.

But if things ever seem too good to be true on Wall Street, caveat emptor!

In a recent development, both President Trump's economy and the AI-driven stock market are in trouble, with persistently elevated inflation to blame. If Fed Chair Kevin Warsh and the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) get aggressive with interest rate hikes, it would likely spell the end of a four-year (and counting) bull market.

The issue is that elevated inflation is no longer just a Trumpflation story. The central bank has identified a new source of inflation that's put FOMC policymakers in quite the pickle.

Recent findings suggest that keep in mind that when the U.S. economy is growing, a modest level of inflation is expected. It's a positive thing when strong demand for goods and services gives businesses some degree of pricing power.

Industry observers note that but the theme of 2026 has been one of persistently elevated inflation. Whereas the FOMC aims for a "timely return" to the 2% long-term inflation target, Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE), the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, reached a three-year high of 4.1% in May and has been moving in the wrong direction, yet again, in recent months.

Trumpflation (i.e., inflation driven by the president's policies) is certainly to blame for some of this pricing pressure.

Recent findings suggest that upcoming from the New York Fed: "By February 2026, tariffs had contributed 2.9 pp to goods price inflation, and without them goods prices would have fallen slightly." About one quarter of every point in higher tariff rates shows up in consumer prices within one year. • A 10% across-the-board tariff yields a 2.6% rise in consumer goods prices after one year. • About two thirds of the increase comes from pricier imports, which get passed through quickly. • Another third comes from U.S. made goods, as producers face higher input costs and less import competition. This takes longer, about 6-12 months, to filter through.

Industry observers note that donald Trump's tariff and trade policy has been one clearly defined source of elevated inflation since the start of his second nonconsecutive term. Following the April 2025 "Liberation Day" tariffs, which the U.S. Supreme Court struck down in February 2026, the Trump administration has imposed sweeping global duties of 10% to 12.5% on more than 80 countries.

According to recent reports, according to a recent report from three New York Federal Reserve economists writing for Liberty Street Economics ("How Fast Do Tariffs Pass Through into Consumer Prices?"), Trump's 2025 tariffs added an estimated 2.9 percentage points to goods price inflation by February 2026. Goods prices would have fallen if not for the president's tariffs.

It has been revealed that the Trump-led Iran war is also pushing up prices. The Strait of Hormuz is a global crude oil choke point, and its closure has resulted in the largest energy supply disruption in modern history. Diesel prices climbed to an all-time high in September.

Recent findings suggest that A slow but steady rise in Core PCE, which removes volatile food and energy costs, also suggests that Iran-war-driven inflation has reached the broader economy. The added transportation and supply chain expenses associated with the Iran war are translating into higher costs for consumers.

According to recent reports, the newest source of inflation has put Fed Chair Kevin Warsh and the FOMC in a pickle. Image source: Official Federal Reserve Photo.

Industry observers note that but Trumpflation is no longer the only driver of elevated inflation. Beginning in June and in each subsequent FOMC meeting, Fed Chair Warsh and his colleagues have homed in on a new source of inflation -- one that may prove incredibly challenging to combat.

The FOMC's minutes for the June meeting contained the following statement:.

It has been revealed that that's right, folks... the AI infrastructure build-out, Wall Street's and the U.S. economy's No. 1 catalyst, is now officially a culprit for elevated inflation.

*KASHKARI: INFLATION DRIVEN BY SUPPLY CONCERNS, INCLUDING AI-BUILD Here we go: AI as source of inflation.

According to recent reports, the Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite wouldn't be where they are today without businesses spending a jaw-dropping amount of capital on AI hardware. A combination of otherworldly demand for data center infrastructure and ongoing supply shortages for graphics processing units and memory is affording AI hardware companies never-before-seen pricing power and record-high margins.

Likewise, the AI revolution is a key economic growth driver. President Trump favors as little regulation as possible to enable this infrastructure build-out.

Recent findings suggest that however, rapidly rising prices for electronic components are adversely affecting consumers and businesses. Any device with a central processing unit, memory, or storage has likely endured a price hike. This means higher costs for smartphones, laptops, and other devices.

The AI boom is transforming one of the biggest deflationary forces into a key source of US inflation: Import prices for computer and electronic products surged +7.4% in the first 6 months of 2026, to 77.1 points, the highest since January 2016. This also marks a +8.0% YoY jump, the largest annual increase on record. This represents a historic reversal from a downtrend which persisted for over two decades. Between 2006 and 2019, computer and electronic product import prices fell -30%, as improving technology and manufacturing efficiency consistently pushed costs lower. Now, the AI investment boom is straining manufacturing capacity for semiconductors, servers, and electronic components, as companies race to build out AI infrastructure regardless of cost. The AI revolution has flipped technology from a long-term source of deflation into a major driver of inflation.

Industry observers note that if Fed Chair Warsh and his colleagues maintain their focus on price stability and aggressively raise interest rates to do so, they could effectively cut off the stock market's and economy's No. 1 catalyst at the knees. Increasing borrowing costs for a partially debt-financed AI build-out would almost certainly slow this expansion, hurting growth projections and calling into question valuations amid the second-priciest stock market in history.

If the Fed does nothing, it could eventually prove just as damaging for Trump's economy and the AI-driven bull market, with inflation continuing to march higher.

Regardless of the solution, the economy and Wall Street appear likely to pay the price.

With Mortgage Rates Rising, Should You Hibernate Until Spring?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (797 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mortgage rates are back up this week, wiping out modest relief from a monthlong drop that began in mid-October.
  • The average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage shot up 29 basis points to 7.28% APR in the week ending Nov.
  • According to recent reports, A mortgage is a big ol’ loan, so when rates go up, those fractions of a percentage point add up fast.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mortgage rates are back up this week, wiping out modest relief from a monthlong drop that began in mid-October.

The average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage shot up 29 basis points to 7.28% APR in the week ending Nov. 19, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.) We calculate our weekly average using daily APRs recorded over the past five business days.

According to recent reports, A mortgage is a big ol’ loan, so when rates go up, those fractions of a percentage point add up fast. Say you’re borrowing $400,000 on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage. Compared with last week, your monthly principal and interest payment would be about $78 higher today.

One bad week doesn't make a trend, but a jump like this can make putting your house hunt on hold until spring feel like a safer bet. So … is it?

Before deciding whether to buy a house now or wait, it helps to know what's pushing mortgage rates higher.

Industry observers note that right now, mortgage rates are still feeling the aftershocks from two major inflation reports last week. First, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) highlighted consumer prices rose more than expected in October. Then, the Producer Price Index (PPI) showed wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its biggest annual increase in nearly four years.

It has been revealed that while CPI shows how prices have changed, PPI can offer clues about what's coming next. Faced with higher costs, businesses may raise their own prices to compensate, keeping inflation elevated. Federal Reserve policymakers aren't expecting much relief anytime soon, either. According to meeting minutes released Nov. 18, they expect inflation to remain elevated above their 2% target for a while.

According to recent reports, to cool rising prices, the Fed can raise the federal funds rate, which is the benchmark interest rate banks charge each other for overnight loans. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. A rate hike is widely expected at the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting.

Recent findings suggest that even after a Fed rate hike, there’s no telling how quickly inflation will cool — or whether mortgage rates will follow. (Inflation is just one of many forces that affect mortgage rates, after all.) So if you do wait until spring to buy a house, don't do it just because you're betting on a cheaper mortgage.

If you're not in a rush to move, winter can be a good time to regroup. Fewer homes typically go up for sale from November through February, so waiting until spring could give you more options.

Industry observers note that but fresh data from the National Association of Realtors suggests this year's slowdown goes beyond the usual seasonal lull. High mortgage rates and home prices are making it tough for many buyers to make the numbers work. For some buyers, waiting isn't a strategy — it's the only option.

Recent findings suggest that pending home sales, a measure of homes under contract, fell 16.7% in October compared with a year earlier, NAR reports. All four U.S. regions saw declines. At this rate, NAR chief economist Lawrence Yun warned that annual home sales could fall to their lowest level since the mid-1990s.

“Either sizable housing demand is building in the background, or the dream of homeownership is increasingly out of reach for many Americans,” Yun stated in a news release.

Whether you're waiting by choice or necessity, you can use the time to strengthen your finances. Paying down debt, strengthening your credit score or saving for a bigger down payment could help you qualify for a better mortgage deal.

Every little bit helps when today’s mortgage rates are this high.

According to recent reports, mortgage preapprovals typically expire after 60 to 90 days. If you're already preapproved, why not keep an eye on listings this winter? (Hey, I’m an optimist. All it takes is one house.).

Industry observers note that think like a seller for a second. If you're listing your house in the dead of winter, you're probably not doing it just for fun. You might have a deadline, and you’re probably more willing to negotiate. In the winter, buyers have less competition — and more room to negotiate a lower price, closing cost credits or repairs. Those savings on the sticker price might help offset today's higher borrowing costs.

Sources indicate that spring typically brings more homes for sale, but it also brings more buyers competing for them. And if mortgage rates end up dropping this spring, you won't be the only one coming out of hibernation.

NuScale Stock Has Lost 93% of Its Value. I'm Still Not Buying It.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that A share of NuScale Power (SMR -11.81%) cost $53.43 at the close on Oct.
  • NuScale ended September sitting on about $1.86 billion in cash and investments, with no debt.
  • For a stock that's lost almost all its value, that might look like a floor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Daniel Sparks – Nov 21, 2026 at 4:29AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than NuScale Power ›.

Industry observers note that A share of NuScale Power (SMR -11.81%) cost $53.43 at the close on Oct. 15, 2025, the stock's highest finish ever. On Thursday, Nov. 19, the shares ended the day at $3.81 -- a fall of about 93% for the small modular reactor developer, and the stock's lowest close since early March 2024.

NuScale ended September sitting on about $1.86 billion in cash and investments, with no debt. At Thursday's close, the market priced the whole company at around $1.6 billion (including both its share classes), or over $200 million less than that cash. And because NuScale loses money every quarter, there's no price-to-earnings ratio to weigh against it.

For a stock that's lost almost all its value, that might look like a floor. Unfortunately, I don't think it's one.

The fact that would make NuScale worth owning hasn't changed throughout the slide: the firm still doesn't have a firm order for its power modules.

Industry observers note that nuScale has stayed busy. In October, it signed a contract with a manufacturer in South Korea to make a key piece of its first power module, the upper reactor coolant system.

But it's building that module without a customer.

In a recent development, over 14 months ago, the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) and ENTRA1 Energy, NuScale's commercialization partner, signed a non-binding agreement for up to 6 gigawatts of new nuclear power. There's still no binding deal. NuScale's third-quarter earnings presentation says ENTRA1 is still in talks with TVA toward a definitive power purchase agreement.

Sources indicate that even a signed TVA deal wouldn't require anybody to buy NuScale's modules. NuScale's 2025 agreement with ENTRA1 names it a key supplier for ENTRA1's projects, but ENTRA1 has full discretion over whether to buy from NuScale at all.

Industry observers note that "Once we have an order, we work on an OEM agreement, we'll have further clarity on margins," CFO Ramsey Hamady noted on NuScale's third-quarter earnings call on Nov. 5.

Recent findings suggest that showing how little NuScale is selling in the meantime, its third-quarter revenue was $281,000, down from $8.2 million a year ago. The first two quarters of 2026 brought in just around $640,000 in total.

Revenue has sat near zero all year, after the company's engineering work for a planned plant in Romania finished in late 2025. And NuScale doesn't expect the Romanian project's owner to sign its next contract before it lines up financing.

Sources indicate that not for me. A stock selling under its cash can look like a textbook value stock. But NuScale's cash might shrink a lot before an order ever comes along.

Setting aside a one-time payment of around $260 million to ENTRA1, NuScale's operations have burned about $47 million of cash a quarter so far this year. And spending is climbing. Third-quarter research and development expenses grew 63% year over year to $18.0 million as NuScale worked on its module components, and its operating loss of $64.8 million was up from $57.5 million in the first quarter. Granted, management expects to recover those component costs through payments under a future equipment agreement. That agreement doesn't exist yet, either.

In a recent development, even more cash is set to leave under the ENTRA1 agreement. A binding power deal for ENTRA1 triggers a second payment from NuScale to ENTRA1, equal to 35% of the total. The first payment, which came due when ENTRA1 signed the non-binding TVA deal, was 15%.

Put simply, the next step forward would cost NuScale cash before it takes any in.

New share sales are the other way cash per share can shrink. NuScale raised around $1 billion from selling new stock earlier this year, boosting its Class A share count 29% from the end of 2025. And with a $750 million stock-sale program in place since August, it can keep adding shares over time.

Current cash per share, in short, likely isn't the cash per share shareholders wind up with.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

According to recent reports, is NuScale stock a buy after losing 93% of its value? I don't think so.

Recent findings suggest that yes, a binding TVA deal could push the growth stock sharply higher for a while. But it would also trigger that second payment to ENTRA1. And until NuScale signs an equipment contract, investors can't gauge what it might make per module.

In a recent development, what would change my mind is a signed order for NuScale's modules, with enough disclosure of pricing and costs to demonstrate the margins Hamady described. I'd be willing to pay a higher valuation for the stock when that contract exists. Until then, I'm not buying shares, even at a price below NuScale's cash.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • 10 stocks we like better than Goldman Sachs ETF Trust - Goldman Sachs S&P 500 Premium Income ETF ›.
  • Many income investors view the trade-off between high yields and growth potential as a necessary evil.
  • However, that doesn't have to be the case.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Keith Speights – Nov 21, 2026 at 4:44AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Goldman Sachs ETF Trust - Goldman Sachs S&P 500 Premium Income ETF ›.

Many income investors view the trade-off between high yields and growth potential as a necessary evil. They think having both is virtually impossible.

However, that doesn't have to be the case. The Goldman Sachs S&P 500 Core Premium Income ETF (GPIX -3.38%) offers both high yields and growth. This dividend ETF could be the passive income and growth engine that many investors didn't know existed.

Like several top S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) index funds, the Goldman Sachs S&P 500 Core Premium Income ETF provides exposure to the S&P 500. Its top holdings include the largest components of the S&P 500 index itself: Apple (AAPL -1.90%), Microsoft (MSFT -2.77%), Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%), Amazon (AMZN -4.10%), and Alphabet (GOOG -2.59%) (GOOGL -2.70%).

But this isn't an ordinary S&P 500 ETF. Two words in the fund's name hint at what sets it apart: "Premium Income." The Goldman Sachs S&P 500 Core Premium Income ETF paid a distribution yield of 8.3% over the last 12 months. That's roughly eight times the yields offered by the State Street SPDR® S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY -3.64%) and the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO -3.42%).

It has been revealed that how does this ETF generate such juicy distributions? It uses a dynamic options "overwrite" strategy. What that means is that the Goldman Sachs fund sells call options on some, but not all, of its equity investments -- usually between 25% and 75%.

The fund's managers sell more call options to generate greater premium income when they view the market's upside as limited. And they dial back the option selling when they expect the stock market to rally.

This approach allows the Goldman Sachs S&P 500 Core Premium Income ETF to generate both growth and income. Since its inception in October 2023, the fund has delivered an average annual total return of 20.4%, not far below the S&P 500's 22.7%. But it has also given shareholders significantly higher income than the S&P 500 has.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

It has been revealed that the Goldman Sachs S&P 500 Core Premium Income ETF isn't the ideal choice for investors seeking only growth. Buying a traditional S&P 500 index fund would provide more growth than this ETF will.

Sources indicate that however, this Goldman Sachs fund could be very attractive to income investors seeking some growth as icing on the cake. An initial investment of $100,000 would generate over $8,000 in annual income at the ETF's current distribution yield. And the initial $100,000 is likely to grow over the long term.

The cost of buying the Goldman Sachs S&P 500 Core Premium Income ETF is admittedly higher than the costs of investing in traditional S&P 500 index funds. But with a net annual expense ratio of 0.29%, the costs won't eat too much into your total returns. This annual expense ratio is also slightly lower than those of some covered call ETFs, such as the JPMorgan Nasdaq Equity Premium Income ETF (JEPQ -5.20%).

Sources indicate that one key thing to note is that where investors hold this ETF could make a difference come tax time. The Goldman Sachs S&P 500 Core Premium Income ETF's distributions consist of ordinary income and return of capital (which isn't taxed when received, but lowers the cost basis, which can increase capital gains when you sell). In the fund's latest fiscal year, the return-of-capital component of the distributions was roughly 91%.

All investments come with risk. The Goldman Sachs S&P 500 Core Premium Income ETF is no exception. If the stock market tanks, so will this fund's share price.

Recent findings suggest that that said, this dividend ETF is a genuine passive income supercharger. Investors should be able to count on high yields over time, along with long-term growth, thanks to its dynamic options overwrite strategy.

  • It has been revealed that room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, hilton is making a big play in South Florida with its Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort. The massive 1,000-room property — which underwent an $80 million renovation before opening under the Signia Hilton brand in May 2026 — sits on the beach in Hollywood, Florida, just outside of Fort Lauderdale.

The resort caters primarily to business and group travelers (it’s attached to a massive events space), but it’s also a strong option for vacationers looking for some R&R. The main downside: The location isn’t great if your trip primarily revolves around off-property excursions, dining and nightlife.

It has been revealed that room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable. There’s also a resort fee of $59 per night — but Hilton waives that when you book using Hilton points.

Sources indicate that hilton covered the cost of my stay for two nights, but the opinions in this review are my own. Here’s what guests can expect at this oceanfront resort.

Since the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort is part of Hilton Honors, there are several ways to book a stay there.

If you’re using Hilton points, expect to pay 70,000 to 80,000 points a night when standard rooms are available. Hilton elite status — a benefit you can earn by holding any Hilton Honors credit card — gets you the fifth-night-free perk, where you stay for at least five nights but pay for four when booking with points.

For example, if you were to stay five nights at 80,000 points a night, you’d pay 320,000 points total, bringing down your average nightly rate to 64,000 points.

You can also book using Hilton’s generous free night certificates, which can be used at almost any property in the portfolio. If you hold the Hilton Honors American Express Aspire Card, you automatically get a certificate each year. It’s also possible to earn certificates through reaching spending thresholds on the card and on the Hilton Honors American Express Surpass® Card. Terms apply.

Industry observers note that make sure to check the cash rate against the points rate to make sure you’re getting good value from your redemption. NerdWallet values Hilton points at 0.4 cent apiece.

For cash bookings of two nights or more, you might consider using The Hotel Collection via American Express’ travel portal for eligible cardholders. Eligible bookings come with benefits like a $100 property credit and other amenities subject to availability, including a room upgrade, early check-in and late checkout.

Keep in mind that third-party bookings typically don’t earn Hilton points or count toward elite status qualification.

It’s hard to miss the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort, with its signature H-shaped facade and sleek white-and-glass exterior.

Stepping into the hotel, I was immediately struck by the lush greenery filling the entrance and indoor courtyard. The grand lobby has soaring glass ceilings, giving the space a greenhouse feel, although the strong air conditioning keeps you cool.

Despite its massive size, it doesn’t have a sprawling layout, which I appreciated. Everything is close together, and you can walk from the check-in counter to any of the indoor restaurants in under a minute.

Industry observers note that I stayed in an oceanfront suite with a balcony, which was spacious and had a fun beachy vibe. To get to the rooms, you’ll need to use either the north or south tower elevator banks.

In the living room, there was a large sitting area featuring a TV, a couch, an accent chair and a four-person high-top table.

Although I didn’t spend too much time on the balcony — the October balminess was a bit too much for me — I enjoyed stepping out each morning to admire the view.

The bedroom had a king bed with extremely comfortable bedding and an oversized chair that was a great spot to relax and read a book by the window.

The bathroom was spacious, featuring a shower and a separate tub (something every room has).

It has been revealed that even the standard room I toured felt roomy. I liked that it shared similar elements with the suite, including the oversized lounge chair.

This is what you’d normally get when booking a room at the cheapest points price.

There are several dining venues on the property, ranging from a grab-and-go cafe to a high-end steakhouse. It is a luxury resort, so expect the prices to reflect that.

For breakfast, you can head to Palmea Kitchen, which is also open for lunch. I had the breakfast buffet, which offered a nice spread of classics, from hot food items and pastries to cold cuts and smoked salmon.

In a recent development, if you don’t have time for a sit-down breakfast, you can head next door to The Press, which offers made-to-order and grab-and-go food options throughout the day. You can also get smoothies, juices, snacks, pastries and other sweet treats.

The Canteen is another grab-and-go option that also sells snacks, drinks, souvenirs and sundries, similar to a convenience store.

Recent findings suggest that for lunch and dinner, try Solara. It doesn’t have a traditional restaurant feel, as it’s mostly an indoor-outdoor bar space. One side connects to the lobby, while the other side faces the Solara adults-only pool.

It serves a lunch menu, as well as a substantial bar food menu that’s available late into the night.

Sources indicate that you can also eat at Playa Beach Bar & Grill, a beachside restaurant serving Latin-inspired cuisine. I enjoyed spending a lazy lunch there and watching the waves crash onto the shore.

For a fancy sit-down dinner, go to Diplomat Prime, the property’s steakhouse. We had a group dinner at the restaurant, and the meats were, of course, the highlight. But don’t sleep on the seafood, which was also delicious.

According to recent reports, one of the best parts of the Dip, as it’s affectionately known, is its location right on the beach. Guests can access the stretch of beach directly adjacent to the property. But it’s not a private beach, so you might encounter crowds.

I didn’t spend any time on the beach itself — it was extremely windy while I was there — but the hotel’s resort fee includes amenities like a beach lounge (umbrella not included), a daily one-hour kayak or paddleboard rental, and beachfront yoga classes.

If you don’t want to get sand everywhere, you can head to one of the three pool options: the adults-only Solara pool, the family-friendly lagoon pool and the Verandah Social Club for those 21 and older (requires paid access).

The family-friendly lagoon spans the length of the property and runs beneath the Solara pool. It also has its own hot tub.

I spent an afternoon in a cabana at the Verandah Social Club, which has some smaller plunge pools and a hot tub.

I appreciated the attentive service from the staff there, who constantly checked on whether guests needed anything.

If you’re looking for other ways to stay active, head to the two-story fitness center, featuring a variety of equipment like free weights, exercise bikes, a rowing machine and treadmills.

Recent findings suggest that next door, you’ll find the spa and wellness center. I had a relaxing massage that incorporated hot stones and aromatherapy.

The locker rooms come with a sauna and steam room, although I wished there were more amenities like a hot tub and cold plunge.

Sources indicate that one of the resort fee inclusions is complimentary high-intensity interval training workout classes at the gym across the street. I signed up for an early morning class. The instructor was friendly, and it was a great way to start my day.

Other amenities include a complimentary one-hour e-bike rental each day, as well as a kids’ club with various activities (but drop-off fees apply).

I had a fantastic stay at this resort, but I’d recommend it for a specific traveler.

Sources indicate that if you’re planning to stay on-property your entire trip, it’s a great option. That’s probably why it’s such a popular convention hotel, since everything you need is easily accessible.

I loved the hotel’s design, including the jungle-like atmosphere in the lobby, and I found the dining options to be tasty, albeit pricey.

But if your trip revolves around visiting Miami attractions, you’ll likely want to stay closer to the action.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that social Security is a critical source of income for millions of older Americans.
  • Sources indicate that that makes annual cost-of-living adjustments (COLAs) particularly crucial.
  • Recent findings suggest that fortunately, Social Security recipients will get a relatively large raise in 2027.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Trevor Jennewine – Nov 21, 2026 at 4:48AM EST.

Recent findings suggest that social Security is a critical source of income for millions of older Americans. Nearly 72 million people receive Social Security benefits, including more than 55 million retirees. And according to Gallup, nearly 9 in 10 of those retired workers depend on Social Security to some degree.

Sources indicate that that makes annual cost-of-living adjustments (COLAs) particularly crucial. These automatic pay increases are designed to protect the purchasing power of Social Security payments against inflation, helping retirees keep pace with rising prices.

Recent findings suggest that fortunately, Social Security recipients will get a relatively large raise in 2027. Benefits will increase 3.6%, up from the 2.8% COLA in 2026. The increase is also slightly larger than the 3.4% average COLA over the preceding decade.

Recent findings suggest that importantly, while all Social Security payments will increase by the same percentage next year, the extra income will vary widely when measured in dollars. Read on to see the 10 states in which retired workers will receive the largest COLAs in 2027.

Image source: OpenAI (AI-generated illustration).

It has been revealed that social Security's annual cost-of-living adjustments (COLAs) are based on a subset of the Consumer Price Index known as the CPI-W. Specifically, the CPI-W from the third quarter (July to September) of the current year is compared with the average from the same period in the prior year, and the percentage increase becomes the COLA for the next year.

According to recent reports, social Security's COLA in 2027 will be 3.6%. The Social Security Administration estimates the average monthly retired-worker benefit will increase from $2,095 before the COLA to $2,170 after the COLA, meaning the average retired worker will receive an additional $75 per month or $900 for the full year.

To be clear, all retirees will receive the exact same 3.6% pay increase, but those with larger benefits will receive larger COLAs when measured in nominal dollars. To that end, retirees in the 10 states with the highest median Social Security benefits will receive some of the largest pay increases next year.

The table below shows the 10 states with the highest median Social Security benefits for retired workers as of December 2025, according to the Social Security Administration.

Data source: Social Security Administration, Annual Statistical Supplement, 2026, Table 5.J6.

Recent findings suggest that importantly, a retiree's state of residence has no direct impact on the amount of Social Security benefits they receive, but there is an indirect relationship. Benefits are primarily based on lifetime earnings and claiming age, so states with high median household incomes are likely to have high median Social Security benefits.

Indeed, six states listed in the table above -- New Jersey, New Hampshire, Maryland, Washington, Massachusetts, and Utah -- rank among the 10 states with the highest median income, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. And three others -- Connecticut, Delaware, and Minnesota -- have median incomes above the national median.

What about the other state? Michigan ranks among the 10 states with the highest median Social Security benefits despite having a median household income below the national median. That could mean more workers in Michigan claim Social Security at older ages, which results in larger benefits. Alternatively, workers with relatively high lifetime earnings may choose to retire in Michigan.

Industry observers note that here's the bottom line: Social Security benefits are not directly linked to where a retired worker lives, so moving to a different state will not automatically increase your monthly payments. Rather, workers in certain states tend to earn more money, often reflecting differences in local labor markets and living costs. And because Social Security benefits are based partly on lifetime earnings, those workers generally qualify for larger payments when they retire.

10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

It has been revealed that nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) stock has gotten slammed over the past few weeks. With former CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang resigning from his position, the market has grown uncertain about Nvidia's future. Furthermore, some of Nvidia's practices have drawn increased scrutiny, which is also adding to fears.

In a recent development, after the sell-off, Nvidia is down over 35% from its all-time high. Since the AI arms race kicked off in 2023, this is now the deepest sell-off Nvidia has seen, just surpassing the tariff-fear sell-off in April 2025. The market has made its opinion known, but does Nvidia actually deserve to be sold off this much? Or is this a generational buying opportunity?

Let's take a look at where the stock could be by 2028, and if now is the perfect time to buy.

According to recent reports, with Nvidia's sell-off, it's now down over $2 trillion from its all-time high market cap. So, is Jensen Huang really worth $2 trillion to Nvidia's market cap?

It has been revealed that I think the market has way overblown this sell-off. Nvidia’s visionary leader definitely helped shape and drive the company. However, there are still thousands of employees who run the day-to-day operations and designs that Huang had nothing to do with. The real risk is if these employees start to quit or resign from their roles and that knowledge is lost. If there is a mass exodus from Nvidia alongside Huang, that could represent a huge risk for investors.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Until we're a few months past Huang's resignation, the market is likely to stay cautious, which is one reason why Nvidia's stock price is down.

It has been revealed that another is the future. Huang's vision for where AI computing and GPUs will go placed Nvidia in a leadership role in the AI build-out. That will have driven product development over the next couple of years, but what comes after that is unknown. This is where a upcoming CEO will need to have a great technical mind and vision for what's coming next. The wrong person at the helm could cause Nvidia's leadership position to collapse in the future if they cannot replicate Huang’s success.

As a result, the market is once again discounting the stock until a newly introduced leader is selected.

Industry observers note that lastly, there are concerns that Nvidia’s chips are potentially circumventing export restrictions to China, with some restricted products funneled through Southeast Asian countries, before eventually making their way into China. These are all allegations right now, but Nvidia hasn't been cleared of any wrongdoing yet, so once again, the market is discounting the stock.

Nvidia has a lot of unknowns right now, and the market has kept it in a low-valued spot as a result. The question is, if these are resolved, what could it be worth?

Sources indicate that nvidia has guided for 75% revenue growth in fiscal year (FY) 2028 (ending January 2028), thanks to the strength of the AI build-out. That's up from the 70% guidance given last quarter. With Nvidia estimated to generate around $424 billion in revenue this year, that would indicate revenue of $742 billion next year. At Nvidia's 62% profit margin, the organization would generate $460 billion in profits.

Even if the stock traded at the same trailing earnings multiple it does now, that would give it a market cap of $7.4 trillion -- more than doubling today's levels and turning $5,000 into at least $10,000.

However, I think that is a dirt cheap price tag in and of itself, and most of Nvidia's problems will be solved by the end of next year. As a result, the market could value it like any other major tech stock and price it around 20 to 25 times earnings. That would result in an even larger market cap and make Nvidia a no-brainer buy today.

Sources indicate that next week, the Nerds are waiting for the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, due out Wednesday. It's the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, so investors will be watching closely. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. Stubbornly high inflation is a significant reason why we’re seeing upward pressure on mortgage rates right now.

According to recent reports, if PCE indicates inflation comes in hotter than expected, mortgage rates could climb as markets anticipate further Fed rate hikes. (An increase to the federal funds rate is already widely expected at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting.) A cooler reading could ease some pressure on mortgage rates for now.

Industry observers note that I’m not getting my hopes up too high for meaningfully lower inflation, though. Last week's Producer Price Index highlighted wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its fastest pace in four years. Wholesale inflation measures the price businesses pay for things. When businesses’ costs go up, they could pass those along to consumers in the form of higher prices — keeping the flames of inflation alive.

Whether Wednesday's PCE brings relief or another helping of bad inflation news, we'll know before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

Social Security Is Getting Its Largest COLA Since 2023 Next Year. Why It Likely Won't Be Enough for Many Seniors.

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (553 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 21, 2026 at 5:04AM EST.
  • There's good news and bad news for seniors on Social Security.
  • But despite the above-average increase, many seniors will likely still have to make some tough budgeting decisions for next year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 21, 2026 at 5:04AM EST.

There's good news and bad news for seniors on Social Security. The 2027 cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) will be the largest since 2023 at 3.6%, reflecting the high inflation Americans have faced throughout the year. This should add $75 to the average Social Security check (as of October 2026).

But despite the above-average increase, many seniors will likely still have to make some tough budgeting decisions for next year. And it all has to do with the way the government calculates Social Security COLAs.

The Social Security COLA formula looks at changes in average third-quarter inflation data from one year to the next. To do this, it looks at the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W) for July, August, and September of the current year and the previous one.

Sources indicate that the problem with this is that the CPI-W focuses on urban households in which at least 50% of household income comes from wages and at least one person has worked for at least 37 of the last 52 weeks. This rules out most retiree households by default.

Industry observers note that they're tracked through a separate index known as the Consumer Price Index for the Elderly (CPI-E). And the numbers are often quite different from the CPI-W. That's because senior spending habits typically look different from their younger counterparts'. Seniors often spend more on healthcare, for example, which can cause their average expenses to rise faster than those of younger adults.

Many have been calling for the Social Security Administration to start calculating COLAs using the CPI-E, which they claim is fairer to seniors. It would also result in larger COLAs in most years. However, that's not the case for 2027.

If the government were to calculate next year's COLA using the CPI-E, seniors would only be in for a 3.4% benefit boost. That would only increase the $2,092 average monthly retirement benefit as of October 2026 by $71 per month.

In this case, the CPI-W will give the typical senior an extra $4 per month, but this is unlikely to make much of a difference. The program's buying power has been slowly eroding for decades, and it will take more than a few extra dollars to reverse this trend.

According to recent reports, that's why organizations like The Senior Citizens League have called on the government to matter a one-time $1,400 benefit increase to make up for the loss of buying power over the last several decades. However, there are no current looks to make this happen.

In a recent development, that means it's up to seniors to figure out how to bridge the gap. If you have personal savings, this is your best bet. But if that's not enough, you might have to explore alternatives, like a job or other government benefits.

#73989. Breaking: When To End A Technology Pilot: 19 Warning Signs

📖 Baca
General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: When To End A Technology Pilot: 19 Warning Signs

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1325 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, technology pilots give organizations an opportunity to test latest solutions on a limited scale, evaluate their potential and identify challenges before committing to a broader rollout.
  • Recent findings suggest that for tech leaders, the challenge is distinguishing between setbacks that can be addressed by adjusting a pilot’s scope or timeline and more fundamental issues that call its viability into question.
  • A pilot without success criteria is not a pilot.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, technology pilots give organizations an opportunity to test latest solutions on a limited scale, evaluate their potential and identify challenges before committing to a broader rollout. But not every pilot warrants further investment, and knowing when to end one can be just as important as knowing when to expand it.

Recent findings suggest that for tech leaders, the challenge is distinguishing between setbacks that can be addressed by adjusting a pilot’s scope or timeline and more fundamental issues that call its viability into question. Below, members of Forbes Technology Council share warning signs that indicate it’s time to end a technology pilot rather than extend it, redesign it or move it into production.

A pilot without success criteria is not a pilot. Defining boundaries and expectations, and, importantly, being transparent, are critical to a pilot’s success. Users should also share any uncertainty during the pilot instead of waiting for it to pivot or improve. - Arunava Sen, Tata Communications America Inc.

Recent findings suggest that A clear sign is when the pilot team cannot tell you what the technology accessed, what decisions it made, or what data it touched. If you cannot answer those questions in a controlled environment (test group), you will not answer them in production. - Michael Nicosia, Salt Security.

Forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

Industry observers note that one sign a technology pilot shouldn’t progress doesn’t involve the new tech itself but the tools teams already work with. If teams are working in siloed workflows with tools that don’t collaborate with one another, introducing new technology can drive up costs, increase complexity and hurt productivity. Connected tools and workflows are integral to the success of any new tech deployment. - Usman Shuja, Bluebeam.

End a pilot when its success depends on hand-curated data that won’t exist in production. If someone cleaned the dataset, resolved definitions and fixed edge cases for the pilot, and no one owns doing that at scale in production, extending or redesigning the product in production won’t help. In many cases, technology isn’t the problem; the foundation is. Ask not whether the pilot worked, but what it worked on. - Prakash Reddy, Okta.

In a recent development, if the pilot only works while its champion is in the room or while the vendor quietly does manual work behind the scenes, you’ve tested enthusiasm, not technology. Hand it to a team that didn’t build it for 30 days. If results collapse, you’d be pushing a dependency into production, not a tool. End it and keep the learnings. - Damian Wasserman, BEON.tech.

When the team stops asking what we learned and starts asking when we get to stop, that’s the sign. A pilot without defined success criteria is avoidance. If you can’t name the specific business result it was supposed to prove or disprove, extending it won’t help. End it, define the outcome you actually need, and redesign around that from the start. - Ali Alkhafaji, APPLY.

It has been revealed that organizations should end a technology pilot when they have full visibility of the tool’s usage and cost metrics but still cannot connect either to a meaningful business outcome. Adoption alone is not enough without a clear path to measurable value, and extending the pilot risks turning experimentation into ongoing spend without a business case. - Conal Gallagher, Flexera.

A clear sign is when the people who were supposed to benefit stop asking about it. Pilots drag on because the sponsors like the idea, not because owners need it. If the pilot group has quietly gone back to their old way of working and nobody complains when the tool goes down, there’s nothing to extend. Name the lesson, thank the team and end it. - Hastimal Jangid, Coozmoo Digital Solutions, Inc.

According to recent reports, A pilot should be reconsidered when it performs well in a demo but can’t prove that it solves a real business problem. AI makes it easy to add capabilities, but more features don’t always mean more value. Teams need clear measures of success and feedback loops to understand what’s working and what’s not before investing further. - Tony Grout, M-Files.

Sources indicate that A clear sign to end a technology pilot is when it repeatedly fails to demonstrate measurable business value despite validated assumptions and reasonable adjustments. If the solution cannot deliver meaningful ROI, operational efficiency or strategic impact, extending it only increases sunk costs. Strong leadership means knowing when to stop, not just when to scale. - Kameshwar Singh, Cohesity.

Industry observers note that end a pilot if no effort was spent defining the vision and how value will be realized at scale. That’s like building a bridge from both ends without deciding where it should meet. - Venky Ramesh, LatentView Analytics.

In a recent development, A pilot should end when success depends on conditions that production will never have: handpicked data, expert customers, manual fixes, privileged integrations or constant vendor support. If removing that scaffolding collapses the value case, extending the pilot only perfects the illusion. The real test is not, “Does it work?” but, “Does it still create measurable value when exposed to ordinary users, messy data, real constraints and an ordinary day?” - Nicola Sfondrini, PWC.

End a pilot when making the technology operable, reliable and governable outweighs its business value. If protecting sensitive data, maintaining an audit trail and providing human oversight would cost more than the expected benefit, extending that particular pilot needs a stronger business case than the time and money already invested. - Brian Stimpfl, S-Docs.

Recent findings suggest that end a pilot when the evidence invalidates its core business premise. If users can complete the workflow but gain no meaningful time, cost or quality improvement over the current process, more engineering won’t create demand. Define that minimum benefit before launch, test it with real users, and stop when it remains out of reach. - Irina Shymko, Langate Software.

End the pilot when the team cannot define a credible path from the experiment to a measurable business outcome. If success still depends on vague future improvements, heroic manual support or assumptions the pilot was supposed to validate, extending it usually just delays the decision. - Dhyey Mavani, Abridge.

In a recent development, A pilot should end when the team cannot explain what newly introduced evidence another extension will produce. Every extra week should answer a specific open question about value, risk, adoption, cost or scale. Once the remaining time is only keeping the pilot alive, the experiment has already delivered its answer. - Sibasis Padhi, Walmart Inc.

Recent findings suggest that I would end a pilot when it successfully completes individual tasks but repeatedly fails to deliver the full business outcome. Often, the underlying glitch is the absence of a clear decision model for handling exceptions, approvals or unresolved work across teams. If nobody can authorize what happens next, scaling the technology only scales the problem. - Vamshi Noothi, Cisco.

A pilot should be ended if nobody uses it unless someone reminds them. A pilot that only stays alive while its sponsor keeps pushing won’t survive production, and extending it just postpones that answer. Software nobody uses isn’t free; it still costs money to run, maintain and support. End it, write down what you learned about the problem, and put the team on something people actually want. - Jeremy Suriel, Kustomer.

According to recent reports, A clear sign to end a technology pilot is when no business owner is willing to take responsibility for implementation. Even if the technology performs well, success requires business ownership, accountability and commitment to change. Without a sponsor willing to champion the solution, allocate resources and own the outcomes, extending the pilot is unlikely to deliver value. Technology cannot create lasting benefits without clear business ownership. - Eranda Maldeniya, Enterprise Analytics.

College Scholarship Breakdown: Types, Sponsors and Eligibility at a Glance
