💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college.
  • In a recent development, before you go searching for a scholarship, it's important to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding.
  • Scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college. You can learn about scholarships in a variety of ways, but looking through an online database of available scholarships — the most common way — can be overwhelming.

In a recent development, before you go searching for a scholarship, it's important to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding. Here’s what you need to know about scholarships to decide which ones are best for you.

Scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies. None is better than the other when it comes to awarding funds.

Nonprofit organizations and clubs that are looking for students either majoring in or researching certain fields, or who have experience volunteering in a specific field.

Companies that want to support all students or only fund those majoring in a field that relates to the companies’ industries.

Financial institutions, such as banks or credit unions, that want to support their community or their members.

Individuals or families that are funding private scholarships, usually in memory of a loved one.

Universities and colleges that are offering funds to students who attend their campuses.

Research organizations that want to fund students who will research in their areas of interest and further their causes.

These scholarships generally are provided by local, state or federal government agencies for a variety of reasons. Despite being funded by a government agency, the scholarships do not require you to pay back the money — unlike federal student loans.

Sources indicate that some scholarships pay for anything related to college expenses, including tuition, room and board, books and supplies, and more. Other scholarships limit what you can pay for with the funds, such as only tuition or tuition along with books. It’s notable to look at this restriction when applying for scholarships to ensure the funds will go toward what you need to cover.

Merit scholarships require you to show excellence or achievements in your schoolwork, through talents and abilities, and even leadership or service work. Because these types of awards can be highly competitive, merit scholarships might require more than just achievements, such as volunteer or leadership experience. This means merit-based scholarships can overlap with other types of scholarship categories. Here are some examples of merit-based scholarships:.

It has been revealed that merit scholarships often require you to have earned a minimum grade point average (GPA). The minimum GPA depends on the scholarship but often ranges from 2.0 to 4.0, with more competitive scholarships usually requiring higher GPAs. Scholarships with lower GPA minimums are more likely to consider additional factors, such as financial need.

Some merit scholarships might require a minimum ACT or SAT score instead of a GPA — or in addition to a minimum GPA.

Merit scholarships might also require applicants to have participated in activities outside of their schoolwork. This is common for scholarships that require membership in a certain group or organization. For example, membership in agricultural clubs, such as 4-H or FFA, and scouting groups, such as the National Eagle Scout Association, appear in scholarship requirements.

Some scholarships emphasize volunteering or community service and only consider applicants who have that experience. Applications vary in how detailed their requirements can be. Some scholarships want only a general description of where and how you’ve volunteered, and others might require experience with a service project that indicates more leadership experience or time volunteering with a certain type of organization.

Scholarships that are awarded to students who can’t afford college are called need-based scholarships.

According to recent reports, unmet financial need is the difference between what it will cost you to attend college and what you can afford to pay. Because calculating how much you can afford is a complicated process, many scholarships refer to your FAFSA to document your financial need.

Some scholarship requirements may be as straightforward as demonstrating that you have financial need, but some scholarships might have income limits. However, income restrictions are less common.

It has been revealed that athletic scholarships are for — you guessed it — athletes. They are usually offered by colleges and universities to recruit athletes onto their collegiate teams and can be competitive. Which sports have scholarships available and the scholarship amounts vary by college.

In a recent development, even though the main criterion for an athletic scholarship is being good at your sport, you’ll likely still need to show that you can keep up with your schoolwork. Most athletic scholarships require students to earn a minimum GPA or test scores to remain eligible while they’re in college.

Some scholarships are designated for students majoring in a general field, such as science or education, but others can be for very specific areas of study. For example, a scholarship for students majoring in a natural resource field could include majors in biology, ecology, wildlife biology, conservation education, forestry, soils and hydrology. However, a stricter scholarship might state that students have to major in more specific topics, such as biochemistry or microbial ecology.

Scholarships are available for active and former members of the military and members of their families. In addition to federal funds available for veterans to attend college, private organizations and some universities have scholarships for veterans to offset the cost of a degree.

Which family members can apply for funds depends on the individual scholarship. For example, some scholarships extend to children or spouses of veterans, but some go as far in a family tree as great-grandchildren.

Veteran- and military-focused scholarships might require that applicants or their family members enlisted in a certain branch, served during a particular time or conflict, or meet a certain rank or status such as receiving disability. Scholarships might also require that the applicant be a wartime veteran or family member of a wartime veteran; not all veterans meet this status.

Sources indicate that scholarships are also awarded to people who identify with a certain group. Common examples of identity-based scholarships include those for people who have disabilities, belong to certain ethnic or religious groups, identify as LGBTQIA+ or are first-generation students. Some identity-based scholarships require applicants to meet several criteria, such as belonging to more than one identity group.

Outside of what would be considered standard DEI groups, there are scholarships for applicants who identify with less common groups, such as veganism, homelessness and model railroad builders.

According to recent reports, the best scholarships for you depend on your situation. For example, if you are a skilled athlete with a good academic record, going for an athletic scholarship might give you the most funding. On the other hand, if you’re going to research a topic that isn’t common, looking for scholarships that support your research topic might be your best bet because competition could be lower.

Good tactics to figure out which scholarships are worth your time include:.

Recent findings suggest that think of the skills, talents, experience and identities that are unique to you. For example, being a child of a veteran immediately qualifies you for scholarships with fewer applicants than scholarships open to everyone. Likewise, if you embrace a certain ethnicity, identify with a specific group or have experience with a type of work, you might qualify for scholarships that appreciate and recognize those attributes more than the average scholarship.

Apply if you think you're eligible. Don’t apply to just a few scholarships and hope you get them. Instead, apply for as many scholarships as you can and for which you’re eligible. This increases your chances of receiving funds. Even small scholarships can make a massive impact when you add several of them together.

Understand how you can use the money. If you already have a scholarship that covers only books, applying for the same type of scholarship isn’t helpful if you don’t need the extra funds. Instead, look for scholarships that cover the costs you have remaining.

Sources indicate that not sure where to look? Our sister site Scholarships360.org provides students with vetted scholarship opportunities. That would be a good place to start.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stock markets remain volatile as investors weigh uncertainty in the Middle East, rising interest rates and concerns about the artificial intelligence (AI) trade.

Given this volatile backdrop, investors seeking a stable income stream can enhance their portfolios with the addition of dividend stocks. In this regard, tracking recommendations of top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist attractive dividend stocks that are backed by strong financials.

Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

In a recent development, integrated oil and gas giant Chevron (CVX) is the first dividend pick. Earlier this month, the firm paid a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share. At an annualized dividend of $7.12 per share, CVX offers a dividend yield of about 3.5%.

After a meeting with senior leadership, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on CVX and raised his price target to $240 from $225. Among the key takeaways Mehta emphasized was that Chevron is building a solid pipeline of promising international exploration projects across Latin America, the Middle East, West Africa and the Eastern Mediterranean. In particular, he mentioned the focus on Venezuela, where Chevron expects to more than double gross production to 600 kbd from about 280 kbd by 2031, using three joint ventures.

Mehta also noted Chevron's efforts to deploy newly introduced technologies, especially in shale and tight-oil operations. CVX is focused on boosting productivity and efficiency to maximize free cash flow, he added.

Initiatives such as artificial lift optimization, AI and machine learning, and advanced chemical treatments are expected to improve recovery by about 10% in latest wells. Consequently, capital spending per barrel in U.S. shale is projected to fall 25% in 2026, with total Permian spending dropping below $3.5 billion.

Mehta also remarked that Chevron sees power as a growth opportunity and is using its U.S. natural gas portfolio, key equipment and partnerships to meet rising demand. Notably, Chevron recently signed a 20-year power purchase deal with Microsoft (MSFT) to supply 2.67 GW of behind-the-meter capacity. This project, called Kilby, is expected to see its first power delivery in 2028 and generate mid-teens returns and long-term cash flows.

It has been revealed that mehta ranks No. 536 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of 11.3%. See Chevron Statistics on TipRanks.

Sources indicate that enterprise Products Partners (EPD) is a master limited partnership (MLP) that provides midstream energy services to producers and consumers of natural gas, natural gas liquids (NGLs), crude oil, refined products and petrochemicals. With a quarterly cash distribution of 56 cents per common unit ($2.24 per common unit annualized), EPD offers a yield of about 6%.

Following a recent call with the company, RBC Capital analyst Elvira Scotto reiterated a buy rating on EPD with a price target of $42. The analyst slightly lowered her estimates for the second half of 2026, citing margin and volume normalization, though demand dynamics remain strong.

While the 5-star analyst expects a sequential decline due to normal seasonality and normalization following high spreads in the first half of the year, she still expects EPD to report another solid quarter (Q3 2026) and enter 2027 with a favorable setup. Ahead of Q3 earnings, Scotto expects investors to focus on export demand durability, EPD's ability to profit from spot cargo sales and growth in Permian volumes.

Industry observers note that scotto continues to expect $150 million of common unit buybacks per quarter in the second half of 2026. She expects buybacks to increase to $200 million per quarter in 2027, as capex spending declines and free cash flow improves.

In total, Scotto is bullish on EPD and views it as a core MLP holding that has both offensive and defensive characteristics. The analyst praised EPD's diverse asset base as ensuring stable cash flows. "Furthermore, the partnership's multi-year organic growth backlog helps provide visibility on long-term distribution growth," Scotto said.

Scotto ranks No. 199 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been successful 67% of the time, delivering an average return of 15.9%. See Enterprise Products Partners Financials on TipRanks.

In a recent development, brookfield Infrastructure Partners (BIP) operates a diversified portfolio of high-quality utilities, transport, midstream and data assets. The firm declared a quarterly distribution of 45.5 cents per unit, payable on September 29. At an annualized distribution of $1.82, BIP offers a yield of 5.2%.

Industry observers note that recently, BMO Capital analyst Devin Dodge reaffirmed a buy rating on Brookfield Infrastructure with a price target of $47. The analyst cited improved visibility into BIP's growth and views its corporate simplification as a potential catalyst.

"Layering in the benefits from the proposed corporate simplification, a multiple well below historical levels and an attractive yield, we believe BIP offers a compelling risk/reward and it remains a preferred idea," mentioned Dodge.

In a recent development, with more organic growth projects in the pipeline and latest partnership investment opportunities, Dodge believes that BIP has clearer visibility into where it will deploy capital. That should support continued double-digit growth in funds from operations (FFO) per unit.

It has been revealed that dodge mentioned the semiconductor foundries that BIP is developing with Intel (INTC) are expected to be fully commissioned by the end of 2026, with returns improving through Q4 2026. Dodge expects the joint venture to boost FFO by 300-400 basis points.

Micron Stock Fell More Than 40% From Its June Record. History Claims What It Did After Its 5 Other Drops This Deep.

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that memory chipmaker Micron Technology (MU -13.89%) has lost a substantial part of its 2026 gain since early summer.
  • I looked back through the stock's daily closing prices since 1984 and counted a drop at the first close at least 40% below its highest close until then.
  • By that standard, Micron has done this five times before -- in 1985, 1995, 2000, 2022, and 2024.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Daniel Sparks – Nov 21, 2026 at 5:17AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Micron Technology ›.

Recent findings suggest that memory chipmaker Micron Technology (MU -13.89%) has lost a substantial part of its 2026 gain since early summer. On Nov. 5, the stock closed around $656, 46% below the $1,213.56 it ended at on June 25, its highest close ever. Yet at about $712 as of this writing, it's still up about 150% this year, after starting 2026 near $285.

I looked back through the stock's daily closing prices since 1984 and counted a drop at the first close at least 40% below its highest close until then.

By that standard, Micron has done this five times before -- in 1985, 1995, 2000, 2022, and 2024. The newest one started at the Nov. 5 close.

What came next varied a lot. And I think the difference had less to do with the stock than with memory chip prices.

According to recent reports, three of the five earlier drops kept going. A year (252 trading days) after the January 1985 drop began, the stock was another 63% lower, and it didn't close at a upcoming record until July 1993. The November 1995 drop left shares 42% lower a year later, with no new record until February 2000.

The drop that started in September 2000 was the worst of all. Shares were 68% lower a year in and around 97% lower by the late-2008 low. They didn't reach a new closing high until January 2022, over 21 years later.

The two latest drops went the other way. A year after the June 2022 drop began, Micron stock was up 22%, and it hit a record in March 2024. The August 2024 drop was followed by a 24% rise in the next year and a record close in September 2025, around 13 months later.

Recent findings suggest that but every one of the five got deeper before it turned. Even in the two fast recoveries, the shares lost another 11% (by September 2022) and another 28% (by April 2025) after first hitting the 40% mark.

Industry observers note that two of the long slumps lined up with memory chip price busts. From December 1995 to August 1996, the average selling price of Micron's 4-megabit DRAM chip fell 78% as industry supply outran demand.

Recent findings suggest that the 2000 bust was arguably even worse. Micron's sales in fiscal 2001 (the year ended Aug. 30, 2001) shrank 38% as average selling prices for its memory chips dropped around 60%, and a $1.5 billion profit a year earlier became a $625 million loss.

The 2022 drop came with a bust, too. Two weeks in, Micron reported record quarterly revenue of $8.64 billion but forecast around $7.2 billion for the next quarter as industry demand softened. Revenue in fiscal 2023 then dropped 49% to $15.5 billion, and the company went from an $8.7 billion profit to a $5.8 billion net loss.

But that bust was short. Fiscal 2024 revenue climbed 62% to $25.1 billion, and shares were back at a record before that fiscal year ended.

The 2024 drop came with no bust at all. Micron's fiscal 2024 fourth-quarter revenue surged 93% year over year, and fiscal 2025 revenue rose another 49%, to $37.4 billion.

So, shares tended to recover within around two years when the memory slump that followed was short or never happened.

According to recent reports, I'd say today's drop looks more like 2024 than 2000, at least so far. Micron's fiscal 2026 fourth quarter (which ended Sept. 3) was its sixth straight quarter of record revenue, at $54.2 billion, and management's forecast for the current quarter is around $61.5 billion.

And its prices keep rising. DRAM prices went up a high-teens percentage from the previous quarter in fiscal Q4. With industry demand growing, much of it driven by artificial intelligence, management expects memory supply to be "much tighter" in 2027 and 2028 than in 2026.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Of course, growth is cooling. The forecast calls for around $7 billion more revenue than fiscal Q4 pulled in, after a jump of almost $13 billion from fiscal Q3 to fiscal Q4. And Micron plans to boost its capital spending in fiscal 2027, with most of the increase going to build fresh factory space, which could in time loosen the tight supply driving today's prices.

Industry observers note that investors already look to be bracing for that. Micron's price-to-earnings ratio is around 10, based on the $74.33 in earnings per share it posted for fiscal 2026.

Sources indicate that has the stock bottomed out? If history is any guide, likely not. But the last five drops also show the year ahead can depend on memory prices, and Micron's own outlook suggests tighter supply in 2027. If I were adding shares today, I'd buy bit by bit.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Keithen Drury – Nov 21, 2026 at 5:35AM EST.

While AI gets all the headlines, quantum computing is starting to become a technology that's becoming more and more interesting. Several companies are making strides in quantum computing endeavors, and the technology is only years away from being commercially viable.

The major question investors must answer in this space is whether it's best to go with a massive firm that has huge resources that can make a successful quantum computer, or if it's better to back a pure-play company that is much smaller.

Two of the most popular options in this segment are Alphabet (GOOG -2.59%) (GOOGL -2.70%) and IonQ (IONQ -8.76%), with Alphabet being the giant and IonQ the smaller player. It's the classic David versus Goliath matchup, but which one makes the most sense? It all depends on your risk tolerance.

When comparing Alphabet's and IonQ's quantum computing technologies, it is a bit difficult to draw direct comparisons. IonQ releases information about every breakthrough it makes and keeps the investing public well informed of its progress. Alphabet is more silent, although it does release updates about its quantum successes from time to time.

At the surface level, some may think that Alphabet is being silent because it's behind and doesn't want to publicly display that information, but I don't think that's what's going on.

IonQ doesn't have a business to fund its operations. It must find partners and raise capital to continue its operations. Unless IonQ can show these entities that it's making progress and that its technology is coming along nicely, it won't be able to drum up enough interest to keep its organization going.

Recent findings suggest that on the flip side, Alphabet is self-funding its quantum research. It only has to keep internal leaders happy with progress, and staying under the radar is a smart idea on their part. So, it's natural that Alphabet doesn't release as many updates as IonQ.

But that doesn't mean IonQ is behind by any means.

Industry observers note that next year, it's releasing its Superion 256-qubit quantum computer. With IonQ's backlog rising to $1.2 billion, it has generated a lot of interest. While this machine isn't quite ready for commercial-level workloads, it's a step in the right direction, and several clients are ordering the machine so they can start to develop quantum computing programs for future implementation. Depending on how this launch goes, it could vault IonQ into a leadership position. It also has looks to build a 10,000-qubit computer, which would be the first commercial-level computer ready for purchase. That's still a few years out, but with quantum technology progressing rapidly, it will be here before investors know it.

But does that make it a better buy than Alphabet for a quantum-focused investment?

In a recent development, ionQ isn't a stock that everyone should own. In fact, I would argue that most shouldn't. Why? Its chance of success is low. While Alphabet hasn't been public with its quantum computing products, the reality is that its products are competitive with IonQ and boast similar fidelity. Alphabet isn't the only big tech company, either. Microsoft (MSFT -2.77%) and IBM (IBM +0.25%) are also heavily investing and represent well-funded competition to IonQ.

If IonQ works out, it will be a huge winner. But there's high risk involved because if it loses to any of its peers or the significant tech companies, the stock could plummet to $0. IonQ is a high-risk, high-reward investment. If investors want exposure to quantum computing without the risk of extreme failure, then Alphabet makes for a great stock pick. If you're OK with more risk in exchange for upside, then IonQ is a smart option. Just be sure to size the position appropriately to account for the risk.

What Is Net Interest Margin? 2 Bank Stocks Where It's Rising

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1142 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the banking business certainly seems complicated on the surface.
  • Recent findings suggest that and yet, at its core, the banking business is philosophically simple -- banks aim to earn more in interest payments than they must pay in interest themselves.
  • It has been revealed that here's a closer look at this core business metric you may know as net interest income, although we're even more interested in a derivative figure called net interest margin.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By James Brumley – Nov 21, 2026 at 6:00AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Bank of America ›.

Industry observers note that the banking business certainly seems complicated on the surface. The major companies in the industry operate multiple profit centers while simultaneously managing the challenges that come with sheer size. Maintaining regulatory compliance is another aspect of the complex machine.

Recent findings suggest that and yet, at its core, the banking business is philosophically simple -- banks aim to earn more in interest payments than they must pay in interest themselves. Everything else is ultimately a means to this end, or add-on revenue.

It has been revealed that here's a closer look at this core business metric you may know as net interest income, although we're even more interested in a derivative figure called net interest margin. Only a couple of significant banks saw improvement in this measure during the third quarter.

In a recent development, contrary to a common misconception, banks don't keep huge stacks of cash in their vaults to lend out when borrowers apply for loans. Most banks keep a relatively small amount of cash in their vaults, in fact. There's not even enough actual cash on hand at your local bank branch to cover the simultaneous closure of every checking or savings account serviced by that branch.

Industry observers note that rather, it's more cost-effective and logistically easier for your bank to borrow money from other customers' deposits, checking accounts, and certificates of deposit as it's needed to make loans, even knowing doing so will drain cash from your bank money. The bank will charge its borrowers a higher interest rate than it pays depositors, and then pocket the difference. This difference results in what's called net interest income.

According to recent reports, yes, net interest income can and does ebb and flow with the economy and changes in interest rates. A strong economy creates strong demand for borrowing, providing banks with more opportunities to make interest-generating loans. And although banks can earn net interest income at any interest rate, lending tends to be more profitable when rates are higher.

Sources indicate that this measure isn't quite the end-all, be-all indication of how well a bank is managing its assets and loan portfolio, however. While obviously more net interest income is better than less, it's the net interest margin figure that indicates how well a bank is using the assets it's got to work with at any given time.

Sources indicate that simply put, net interest margin is the amount of net interest income earned relative to the amount of interest paid. Although almost always in the low single digits, a bigger number is still better than a smaller one.

It has been revealed that it's absolutely possible for a smaller bank with fewer assets to report a higher net interest margin rate than a bigger bank. The key is to maintain a high-quality loan portfolio while ensuring you retain customers' deposits.

Neither the domestic nor the global economy is in a recession at this time. In fact, although persistent inflation is making most consumers miserable, the economy is technically strong, with the U.S. unemployment rate at a historically low 4.1% and third-quarter gross domestic product (GDP) growth exceeding 3%.

Recent findings suggest that nevertheless, there's no denying the lending business is experiencing turbulence. The Federal Reserve recently reported that as of the end of the third quarter, 5% of loans to U.S. borrowers are in some form of delinquency, led by auto loans and mortgages. Many banks are tightening their lending standards as a result, hoping to steer clear of any future loan write-downs or charge-offs. Higher interest rates are also discouraging some would-be borrowers, of course.

A couple of familiar banks, however, appear to be pushing through the headwind.

Bank of America (BAC -3.15%) is one of them. Its net interest income grew from a little less than $15.4 billion in the third quarter of 2025 to a little more than $16.6 billion in Q3. Moreover, its net interest margin -- what it calls net interest yield -- improved from 2.01% a year earlier to 2.16% in the third quarter. It's also worth noting that while its loan and lease portfolio grew more than 7% year over year, its provision (money set aside) for losses on loans was actually slightly reduced compared to Q3 2025. BofA is clearly managing its business well in this tricky environment.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

JPMorgan Chase (JPM -3.03%) too is doing well, even if not quite as convincingly as Bank of America. Last quarter's net interest margin rate (excluding capital-markets-related assets) came in at 2.48%, up from a year-earlier 2.45% and from Q2's 2.40%. And like BoA, its interest-earning asset base grew from just under $2.5 trillion to almost $2.65 trillion.

Not every big bank is doing as well. Wells Fargo (WFC -2.47%) saw its net interest margin slip from 2.61% in the third quarter of last year to 2.43% in the three months ended in September, despite net interest income growth of nearly 5% to a little more than $12.5 billion. Charge-offs and loan-loss provisions were also up from year-ago levels for both its consumer and commercial lending businesses.

Citigroup (C -4.04%) also bumped into a bit of a headwind in Q3. Although its net interest margin rolled in at 2.43% versus the year-ago figure of 2.4%, that was also down from Q2's 2.54% despite a 12% increase in its interest-earning asset base. Like Wells Fargo, Citi's provision for credit losses is inching higher, although the biggest crimp may be that its average effective yield on assets slipped from 5.89% in the third quarter of last year to 5.54% this time around.

Recent findings suggest that there's always more to the story, of course. Widening net interest margins don't necessarily mean that bank's stock is a better buy. Narrowing margin rates don't inherently mean a bank is in trouble either. And one quarter's worth of data rarely means very much.

It's one of several important fiscal metrics to monitor all the same, since it indicates how well a bank minimizes its interest costs while maximizing its interest revenue. Indirectly, it points to the quality of loans a bank is making, and how cost-effectively it's retaining customers' deposits. These seemingly little things can actually end up being a pretty big deal.

In a recent development, we know it is a time in the pre-season when the legs are not that fresh, we train very intense but we want to play with an idea of how we want to play football. Intense with a vertical approach for sure, everyone gets 45 minutes except the goalkeeper.

Big Dunc and Moyes catch up pre-match! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/Jh4APHOZvX.

A word that keeps being used about Jaissle is “special”. Newcastle’s hierarchy believe they have secured the services of a manager who will soon be recognised in the elite tier of European managers. We shall see how this view of the 38-year-old survives contact with a brutal and relentless Premier League campaign.

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; Shahar, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Joelinton, Bamba; Elanga, Wissa, Toure; Osula.

Newcastle subs: Gillespie, Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Johnson, M Miley, Finneran, Ramsey, Steur, Willock, J Murphy, Barnes, Neave, Woltemade.

In a recent development, your Mags at Murrayfield! ✊ pic.twitter.com/rDXpn0MqCg.

Everton XI: Travers; Patterson, Tarkowski, Keane, Mykolenko; Hackney, Deswbury-Hall, Armstrong, Ndiaye; George, Barry.

Here's how we start against Newcastle. UTT! 🔵📺 https://t.co/2VsWpyRq02 pic.twitter.com/vpnLPTRmLl.

Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the upcoming season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s a challenge, a substantial challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

In a recent development, “We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”.

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about newly introduced signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

It has been revealed that “Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”.

Jaissle remarked he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

Sources indicate that “The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”.

  • In this climate, investors with a long-term horizon can track recommendations from top Wall Street analysts to find stocks with solid growth prospects.
  • Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

September ended on a mixed note, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 0.5% and 4.3%, respectively, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.9%. Markets remained on edge with higher oil prices and Treasury yields weighing on investor sentiment and triggering fears of additional interest rate hikes.

In this climate, investors with a long-term horizon can track recommendations from top Wall Street analysts to find stocks with solid growth prospects.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Neocloud tech giant CoreWeave (CRWV) is benefiting from robust AI-driven demand for cloud computing.

It has been revealed that recently, JPMorgan analyst Samik Chatterjee upgraded CoreWeave to buy from hold, raising his price target to $125 from $120. The analyst cited favorable pricing, driven by solid demand, for the upgrade.

Chatterjee stated CoreWeave is now more willing to sign premium priced, shorter-term contracts, which lift his revenue and margin estimates. CRWV stock performance has been underwhelming as investors worry about high capital spending, the analyst noted. That said, he believes that higher prices and increased margins will more than offset the rise in debt to fund capital spending, improving the stock's valuation.

Chatterjee noted the 25% price hike in July across CoreWeave's product offerings and frequent price increases by rivals like Nebius (NBIS), adding that some peers are charging nearly three times more for short-term compute contracts than what CoreWeave charges on longer-term deals.

"CoreWeave's leverage of the opportunity [is] evident in its recent press release highlighting contracts signed in F3Q at ~$40M/MW," mentioned Chatterjee. JPMorgan said higher pricing is already contributing 5-10 percentage points to contract margins versus earlier deals.

Industry observers note that chatterjee ranks No. 4 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 75% of the time, delivering an average return of 55.3%. See CoreWeave Statistics on TipRanks.

Palo Alto Networks (PANW) is a provider of cybersecurity solutions across network, cloud, security operations, AI and identity. Following a discussion with management, BTIG analyst Gray Powell reiterated a buy rating on PANW and raised his price target to $425 from $404.

After a review of Palo Alto's product-level growth catalysts, Powell sees clear upside to both revenue and next-generation security (NGS) annual recurring revenue (ARR) in fiscal 2027. He expects PANW to deliver pro forma revenue growth of more than 17%, above the consensus estimate of 14.6%, and NGS ARR growth of more than 26% versus the Street's expectation of 24.5%.

Over the past five years, the Palo Alto business mix, has moved to higher-growth product areas and new markets. from what was earlier viewed as a hardware-centric network security tech giant, Powell said. The 5-star analyst estimates that hardware firewalls and attached subscriptions now account for less than 50% of revenue.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, high-growth solutions, including Prisma SASE, software firewalls, Cortex XSIAM, Chronosphere and Idira now represent more than 35% of PANW's revenue. "Investors may not fully realize the growth potential within PANW's platform story," Powell noted.

BTIG is optimistic about the prospects of Chronosphere in observability, CyberArk in identity and software firewalls and Prisma AIRS in the network and AI security business.

Industry observers note that powell ranks No. 320 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of 17.3%. See Palo Alto Networks KPIs on TipRanks.

Sources indicate that in a research note on September 30, Rosenblatt analyst Scott Devitt reiterated a buy rating on e-commerce and cloud computing platform Amazon (AMZN), raising his price target to $360 from $335. Fears that agentic commerce poses a major threat to Amazon's advertising business seem "overstated," he mentioned.

Devitt noted that the growing adoption of personal agents and AI shopping assistants has sparked concern about displacement of Amazon's retail media business. But the 5-star analyst remains bullish, given Amazon's ability to adapt to changing consumer behavior, as it's done in the past.

Additionally, Devitt argues that even if an AI agent helps a shopper discover a product, Amazon can still handle the purchase and delivery, keeping much of the transaction value. He highlighted that management believes that existing Amazon shoppers will likely continue to start their shopping journey on the platform because it has better personalization, accurate pricing and inventory information that third-party agents still lack.

Recent findings suggest that overall, Devitt expects Amazon's retail business to prove a net beneficiary of agentic commerce. Fewer clicks would not hurt the company if the value of each remaining click and overall volumes keep rising, he remarked. The argument is that even if Amazon loses some sponsored ad revenue over the next few years, it would likely be only a small part of the company's total business and could be offset by growth in other areas.

It has been revealed that "Consistent with our AI framework, we continue to view Amazon as one of the most resilient leaders in our coverage, combining owned compute infrastructure with a physical fulfillment moat," remarked Devitt. His bullish view is supported, Devitt said, by expectations that Amazon Web Services (AWS) will exit the year at a more than 45% growth rate with continued margin improvement.

Devitt ranks No. 765 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 49% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Amazon Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 18:10 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 19:58 EST, 15 November 2026.

Thomas Tuchel hailed the 'best performance of my time as manager' after England beat world champions Spain in a crazy, brilliant see-sawing drama of a Nations League tie.

England played the best football of Tuchel's two-year reign as coach to end Spain's world record 43-match unbeaten run.

England raced into a 3-0 lead with a penalty from Harry Kane, and further goals from Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

But they played the last half an hour of the game with ten men after Elliot Anderson was sent off for pulling back Lamine Yamal.

Spain got two goals back to set up a nerve-wracking finish but goalkeeper James Trafford, in the team ahead of Jordan Pickford, pulled off a miracle double save in the dying minutes to seal the win.

'What a performance we put out there for 60 minutes to be deservedly 3-0 up,' Tuchel said after the game. 'Thirty minutes against Spain with ten men feels like three hours.

Thomas Tuchel noted England's display in the win over Spain was the best in his time as boss.

'It was a statement victory. It was on the highest level football-wise. It is a wonderful feeling for us in the dressing room.

Industry observers note that 'It is the best performance of my time and they are unbeaten for 43 matches and that was a complete performance in that environment. To impose our identity on them was a real achievement.

'Declan Rice said he knew we were going to win and I could feel the true belief. This was the moment we wanted to prove ourselves. You need to rely on your teammates. That is why I am very proud of the win.'.

Tuchel also questioned the decision to give Anderson a straight red, made by a referee he once labelled a 'one out of 10'.

The Man City midfielder was sent off because Clement Turpin adjudged him not to have been making an attempt to play the ball when he fouled Yamal.

Sources indicate that 'The red card and the penalty is always a major decision and I needed to understand why it was a double punishment but... OK,' Tuchel told ITV Sport.

'From then it was a long 30 minutes but I don't want to focus on that because there were so, so many positives.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Alex Carchidi – Nov 21, 2026 at 6:03AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Zcash ›.

With Zcash (ZEC -2.76%) falling to $922 during its first big drop below $1,000 since September, it's natural for investors to wonder whether it's time to buy the dip, especially considering that the coin is still up 73% this year so far.

Price action alone doesn't make for a good investment thesis, so let's take a closer look at this privacy coin and determine whether it's worth buying right now, despite the turbulence and uncertainty in the crypto market and the world.

Zcash's recent decline from its highs is to be expected, given the bumps in the road it has faced.

Recent findings suggest that for instance, on Oct. 29, hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the largest crypto exchange, marking the largest-ever crypto theft and worsening the climate of fear that has been intensifying since a spate of other crypto hacks earlier in the year. Similarly, when October's Consumer Price Index (CPI) data came in above market forecasts, it sparked a flight from risky assets like crypto amid expectations that the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates at its next meeting in December. Separately, investors pulled $46 million from Grayscale's Zcash exchange-traded fund (ETF) in October, followed by another $15 million in early November.

CRYPTO · As of 8:51 AM ET 11/21/26.

According to recent reports, none of those issues were caused by anything related to Zcash itself. Its main investment thesis, namely that investors will continue to seek to conceal their transactions and account balances from prying eyes, is still valid.

Now, let's turn to whether it makes sense to buy this coin right now.

According to recent reports, zcash just launched its latest network upgrade, NU7, which makes the chain significantly faster. It cuts the target block time, the gap between each batch of its confirmed transactions, from 75 seconds to 25 seconds. It also sequesters 60% of the network's transaction fees into a reserve that will disburse its funds to pay miners starting in around 2031. Those changes are well and good, but they don't imply any need to rush with a purchase.

Industry observers note that one interesting factor that might make it a better buy is the spread of privacy in crypto. On Nov. 10, Helius, a Solana (SOL -0.72%) infrastructure company, rolled out a privacy protocol for use on Solana. Its CEO signaled the design was inspired by Zcash's. This imitation validates Zcash, but it also means more competition in the future.

Industry observers note that overall, I believe in Zcash's long-term investment potential, but the market is a bit too fragile for me to buy. A coin that lost over 41% in just eight weeks can do it again, and I do not want to be taking risks like that in the current environment of uncertainty.

But for those with a very high risk tolerance and a five-year-plus holding horizon, not to mention already having a diversified portfolio, buying a small amount of Zcash right now could still pay off.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Geoffrey Seiler – Nov 21, 2026 at 6:15AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

The AI chip market is starting to shift, and with it, Nvidia's (NVDA -14.01%) grip. Anthropic recently revealed that its Claude Mythos model could start running part of its AI models on alternative AI chips to Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs) in just a few days with basically no human intervention, a process that used to take six to 12 months and dozens of engineers. This greatly reduces Nvidia's CUDA moat at a time when competitors are starting to catch up.

Alphabet's (GOOGL -2.70%) (GOOG -2.59%) Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) have started to outperform Nvidia's GPUs on a performance-per-dollar basis, according to Semianalysis (though some dispute the results). Meanwhile, Advanced Micro Devices' (AMD -13.25%) GPUs continue to gain traction. The organization has improved its software stack, and its chips' larger memory capacity makes them ideal for inference.

If the gap between AI chips continues to shrink and AI models can be rapidly shifted to run on any AI accelerator, this is very bad news for Nvidia. Not only will the firm continue to lose market share, but, more importantly, its pricing power will erode, and its margins will shrink. The Nvidia premium can be seen in its gross margins, which are in the mid-70% range, versus AMD’s in the mid-50% range. Meanwhile, all of Nvidia's largest customers, outside of SpaceX (SPCX -7.69%), have been developing their own custom AI chips to try to break free of Nvidia's high prices.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Industry observers note that all is not lost for Nvidia, as the organization still holds some advantages. It has created a cohesive hardware, software, and networking ecosystem that should still be able to command a premium. It also has major current supply chain advantages, having locked up more access to constrained high bandwidth memory (HBM) supply and having more manufacturing and packaging capacity with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM -9.48%). That will help it maintain its leadership position, even as it will likely face continued market-share and pricing pressure.

While Nvidia may struggle, these three AI stocks look set to benefit.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Lower AI accelerator prices and more Nvidia GPU alternatives could boost overall AI chip demand, which would benefit Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing. It would also lower TSMC's customer concentration and could actually help with pricing power and gross margins.

Whether a hyperscaler, neocloud, enterprise, or government buys Nvidia GPUs, AMD accelerators, or ASICs through a company like Broadcom (AVGO -12.19%) or Marvell Technology (MRVL -11.69%), TSMC still wins at the end of the day. That makes the stock a buy.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

According to recent reports, as both a cloud computing giant and a developer of TPUs, Alphabet is one of the best-positioned companies to benefit from the commoditization of AI chips. Alphabet has more than a decade's head start with custom chips and is creating an ecosystem to rival chipmakers like Nvidia and AMD. This lets it get better utilization out of its data centers and gives it an advantage over other companies using their own custom AI chips.

Meanwhile, because its offerings cost much less than Nvidia's, it should be able to gain share with external customers without sacrificing margins. This ultimately could make Alphabet one of the biggest winners in the AI space during this transition.

Starting from a much smaller market-share base with an operating model already built around slimmer gross margins, AMD should benefit as AI chips become more commoditized. Between its lower prices, improving cost performance, and the recent introduction of a complete AI rack system (Helios), AI chip pricing normalization and chip fungibility actually become a tailwind rather than a headwind for a smaller Nvidia competitor like AMD.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, the market is heading in AMD's direction with inference and agentic AI, with customers caring far more about memory capacity, central processing unit (CPU) integrations, and cost-per-action, which is where its chips shine. With its newly introduced Helios system, which combines its GPUs and CPUs, AMD has a substantial opportunity to establish itself as a meaningful alternative to Nvidia in the coming years. This makes the stock a buy.

By Rick Orford – Nov 21, 2026 at 6:30AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›.

Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -7.69%) just reached another major milestone with its Starship program, and the outcome could have huge implications for where its stock heads by 2030. Specifically, Flight 15 launched Nov. 13, and SpaceX caught the upper stage the day after. However, the Super Heavy booster aborted its catch and was lost in the Gulf.

Overall, the catch could strengthen confidence in SpaceX's ambitions, while the lost booster could raise concerns around development timelines.

Here's what investors should watch and how the mixed result could affect SpaceX stock.

In a recent development, starship is a heavy-lift launch vehicle designed to be fully reusable, enabling SpaceX to launch, recover, and fly its rockets again rather than building a new vehicle for every mission. Now that Starship's upper stage has been caught for the first time, the vehicle could be a future game changer for SpaceX as the organization could change the economics of getting into space and back.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Industry observers note that from there, if the company can make that process (reliably) repeatable, it could dramatically lower launch costs and increase the number of missions it can undertake. Plus, with a much larger payload capacity, Starship could potentially carry more cargo and satellites into orbit than existing rockets.

That could lead to cheaper launches and make previously uneconomical businesses more attractive, from satellite deployment and space-based communications to orbital infrastructure and lunar transportation.

Beyond that, Starship could also make it easier and cheaper for SpaceX to expand its Starlink business, allowing it to deploy more satellites, ramp up coverage, and increase network capacity.

Of course, the upper stage catch was only half of the planned double recovery. What does the lost booster mean for SpaceX?

SpaceX shares slipped about 0.6% on launch day, but have since edged higher. Even so, the lost booster could raise questions about development timelines, future launch costs, and the organization's ability to deliver on its longer-term ambitions.

The unsuccessful booster recovery attempt could delay the timeline for achieving full reusability.

According to recent reports, there's also a timing consideration. SpaceX has major ambitions for Starship, including its role in NASA's lunar program and the expansion of Starlink. Any delays would affect expectations surrounding both opportunities.

Recent findings suggest that still, the lost booster doesn't necessarily undermine the investment case for owning SpaceX. After all, Starship is a much more ambitious launch vehicle, so the development process is naturally more complicated. And if/when Starship finally becomes operational, it could provide the company with a latest avenue for growth.

Today, SpaceX stock trades at a price-to-sales (P/S) ratio of about 61, and based on the latest reported sales data, that works out to $2.36 in sales per share. This high multiple may be justified, assuming revenue increases significantly as SpaceX successfully recovers Starship.

Data source: Calculations by the author.

In a conservative case, if SpaceX generates $11.95 per share in sales, an 8-times compressed multiple could put shares near $96 by 2030, about 32% below today's level. At $17.49 per share in sales and a 12-times multiple, shares could trade near $210 by 2030, about 48% above today's level. Finally, in a more optimistic case, sales of $24.77 per share at 15 times sales could put shares near $372 by 2030, about 163% above today's level.

To be clear, these are scenarios, not promises, but they show where Starship's progress after Flight 15 could take the stock by 2030. In the end, the bigger opportunity is Starship's potential to make space transportation dramatically cheaper, opening up entirely newly introduced markets.

📅 09 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1025 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

📅 09 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1025 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt.
  • It has been revealed that high-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago.
  • The high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt. It isn't time to ditch high-yield bonds, but investors should pay attention to the warning signs.

It has been revealed that high-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago. The increase reflects a jump in yields across the curve as investors bake in more inflation from high energy prices and other pressures, including concern about the deficit — hitting nearly $2 trillion in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30.

The high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Credit spreads are the difference in yield between the bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. Wider spreads mean investors are demanding higher yields for holding corporate debt, viewing it as riskier.

It has been revealed that spreads are at 315 basis points in the overall high-yield market, higher than a year ago but still below levels in March when they reached 346 bps. One basis point equals one one-hundredth of a percent, or 0.01%.

The high-yield market consists of bonds rated BB+ by S&P and Fitch and Ba1 and under by Moody's. The lowest-rated cohort, CCC and below, has seen the most movement with spreads climbing dramatically over the past year to roughly 1,250 bps.

Right now, the high-yield market is "flashing yellow" but is "far from red," said Michael Arone, chief investment strategist at State Street Investment Management.

It makes sense that investors are demanding more compensation for taking on additional credit risk as borrowing costs rise, he said.

Yields are elevated across the board with the 10-year Treasury reaching its highest level since 2002 earlier in the week.

"The bigger question is whether this is simply a repricing of interest rate risk, or the beginning of a more fundamental reassessment of credit quality," Arone remarked.

He's in a wait-and-see mode since earnings are still growing, interest-coverage ratios remain good, and while default rates have ticked up some, he believes it is not concerning.

That mentioned, the starting point in spreads is likely weighing on investors' psyche, since they are still low by historical standards.

"There's a small margin of error here, which I also think raises the anxiety level," Arone explained. "The compensation that investors are receiving for taking on this credit risk isn't overwhelming relative to history, and therefore subtle changes in credit spreads can be concerning.".

While there may be concerns about part of the lower-rated market, the overall high-yield market is in good fundamental shape.

In fact, credit quality is at a record high, with BB bonds making up over 60% of the market compared with 38% prior to the global financial crisis, said Kelley Gerrity, a fixed income strategist at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

Industry observers note that "We've had higher-quality companies coming in, and with higher rates now, you also have more discipline from companies that are more indebted ... just because of the higher cost of capital, so that actually is creating a bit of a healthier picture as well," she said.

The lowest tier of high yield has always been more speculative, since the bonds have a higher default risk. Therefore, it's no surprise that they are the ones seeing the most widening in spreads, mentioned Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.

Recent findings suggest that the overall move in high-yield spreads have been "orderly," he remarked. "Are there cracks forming? I think the cracks are logical cracks with the lowest-rated bonds and it's too early to say that it's spreading to the broad credit market.".

In addition, fluctuations within the CCC-rated and lower spreads have been idiosyncratic, Gerrity added. Morgan Stanley recently broke down the spreads in the lowest cohort into two buckets: performing assets and non-performing assets, which are defined as spreads above 1,000 bps.

The non-performing spread to worst is 2,818 bps, while the performing bucket — the biggest piece of the CCC market — is 461 bps, she noted.

"It is isolated," she said. "I'm not necessarily sure that that will go away anytime soon, but it doesn't tell the story of overall concern and flashing caution for credit markets right now.".

For now, investors should remain selective within higher yield, Gerrity advised.

"We're looking for the best relative value opportunities, and we think that exists within that single-B cohort, and so we're leaning into that," she said.

Investors should be concerned if there is a steep widening in the broader high-yield market.

But there's scant evidence of stress in the BB cohort. Spreads in that group are at 194 bps, up from 179 bps a year ago — although the move hasn't been in a straight line.

"We're going to be focusing our attention on what are considered some stronger businesses," Martin stated. "If we start to see the markets demand higher spreads there also, that's what we'll be looking at to see if risks are really rising.".

It has been revealed that it's also vital to understand that the Federal Reserve is raising rates in a strong economic environment, said R.J. Gallo, chief investment officer of global fixed income at Federated Hermes. The central bank is concerned about an inflation problem amid high fossil fuel prices due to the Iran war, while growth has been stronger than expected, he noted.

"With growth being good as the reason that the Fed is hiking, then you wouldn't expect high yield to blow out because growth means revenues stay up, means cash flow and profitability stays up," he explained.

High yield becomes a disaster when the economy is heading into a sharp economic downturn, Gallo said.

It has been revealed that "That's when spreads really widen out," he noted. "But a recession is not the odds-on bet. Now, talk to me in six months if the Fed keeps hiking over and over, if oil prices stay high for longer, well, then maybe we will start to wonder.".

#73952. Tech Report: Social Security's Trump Bump-Led 2027 COLA Is the 5th Largest in 35 Years -- but There's a Dark Side to This Outsize Increase as Well

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1145 w)
📖 Baca
Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Social Security's Trump Bump-Led 2027 COLA Is the 5th Largest in 35 Years -- but There's a Dark Side to This Outsize Increase as Well

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1145 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For Social Security’s nearly 72 million traditional beneficiaries -- retired workers, workers with disabilities, and survivors of deceased workers -- there are few, if any, announcements more anticipated than the annual cost-of-living adjustment (COLA).
  • It has been revealed that social Security's COLA is the near-annual "raise" given to beneficiaries to account for inflation (i.e., rising prices).
  • It has been revealed that social Security's unveiled 2027 COLA offers something of a mixed bag for recipients.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sean Williams – Nov 21, 2026 at 6:36AM EST.

For Social Security’s nearly 72 million traditional beneficiaries -- retired workers, workers with disabilities, and survivors of deceased workers -- there are few, if any, announcements more anticipated than the annual cost-of-living adjustment (COLA).

It has been revealed that social Security's COLA is the near-annual "raise" given to beneficiaries to account for inflation (i.e., rising prices). If the price for the goods and services that seniors regularly purchase kept climbing without an adjustment in benefits, the buying power of Social Security income would steadily decline over time.

It has been revealed that social Security's unveiled 2027 COLA offers something of a mixed bag for recipients. On the one hand, it's set to deliver one of the largest raises over the last 35 years. This larger payout comes courtesy of President Donald Trump and a handful of his policies.

Sources indicate that president Trump's policies offer a good-news/bad-news scenario for Social Security. Image source: Official White House Photo by Molly Riley.

Sources indicate that but this outsize Trump bump isn't without its consequences. Larger payouts in the new year can make the program's precarious financial outlook that much worse.

It has been revealed that on Oct. 14, the Social Security Administration revealed that monthly payouts would increase by 3.6% in 2027. For the average retired-worker beneficiary, their monthly payout is expected to climb by $75. Meanwhile, the typical worker with a disability can expect their monthly Social Security check to rise by $59 in the new year.

According to recent reports, A 3.6% raise is well above the norm. It marks a tie for the fifth-largest percentage increase over the last 35 years, surpassed only by COLAs of 4.1% (2006), 5.8% (2009), 5.9% (2022), and 8.7% (2023).

It's also the sixth consecutive year in which recipients have received at least a 2.5% cost-of-living adjustment. It's been 30 years (1988-1997) since benefits rose by at least 2.5% for six straight years.

It has been revealed that while modest inflation associated with a growing U.S. economy results in a Social Security raise most years, next year's outsize COLA was pumped up by two of President Donald Trump's policies.

In a recent development, fresh from the New York Fed: "By February 2026, tariffs had contributed 2.9 pp to goods price inflation, and without them goods prices would have fallen slightly." About one quarter of every point in higher tariff rates indicates up in consumer prices within one year. • A 10% across-the-board tariff yields a 2.6% rise in consumer goods prices after one year. • About two thirds of the increase comes from pricier imports, which get passed through swiftly. • Another third comes from U.S. made goods, as producers face higher input costs and less import competition. This takes longer, about 6-12 months, to filter through.

To begin with, each of the last two Social Security COLAs has been influenced by Trump's tariff and trade policy. Adding duties to imports directly raises their price and can increase manufacturing costs for domestic producers.

A recently published report by three New York Federal Reserve economists writing for Liberty Street Economics ("How Fast Do Tariffs Pass Through into Consumer Prices?") found that Trump's 2025 tariffs increased goods price inflation by an estimated 2.9 percentage points by February 2026. Without tariffs, the NY Fed economists estimate that goods prices would have otherwise fallen.

According to recent reports, the other major policy contributing to Social Security's 2027 Trump bump is the Iran war. Closing the Strait of Hormuz has resulted in the largest energy supply disruption in modern history, sending gas and diesel prices notably higher.

Recent findings suggest that with Trumpflation (inflation driven by Trump's policies) becoming entrenched in the U.S. economy, it's quite possible that these policies provide a third consecutive year with a Trump bump in 2028.

Unfortunately, outsize Social Security COLAs come at a potentially steep cost to America's leading retirement program.

Every year since 1985, the Social Security Board of Trustees Report has warned of a long-term unfunded obligation. In simpler terms, the projected income to be collected in the 75 years following the release of a report is expected to be insufficient to cover outlays (primarily benefits, but also the administrative costs to oversee Social Security). As of 2026, this long-term unfunded obligation had ballooned to $29.3 trillion.

However, this isn't the most pressing concern for the program or its nearly 72 million traditional beneficiaries.

In a recent development, according to the latest Trustees Report, the Old-Age and Survivors Insurance trust fund (OASI) is forecast to exhaust its asset reserves by the fourth quarter of 2032. The OASI's asset reserves represent the excess income collected since inception that is invested in special-matter, interest-bearing government bonds, as required by law.

US Old-Age and Survivors Insurance Trust Fund Assets at End of Year data by YCharts.

The positive news is that Social Security isn't going bankrupt and is in no danger of halting benefits. More than 91% of the program's income is collected through the 12.4% payroll tax on earned income (wages and salaries, but not investment income). As long as Americans keep working, the payroll tax will continue generating income for disbursement to eligible beneficiaries... even if the OASI's asset reserves are depleted.

In a recent development, but just because Social Security isn't going bankrupt, it doesn't mean everything is peachy. If the OASI's asset reserves run dry over the next six years, as predicted, it would indicate that the current payout schedule, inclusive of annual COLAs, isn't sustainable. Sweeping benefit cuts of up to 22% may be necessary for retired workers and survivors of deceased workers.

The concern is that Social Security's Trump bump may have materially altered the trajectory to the OASI's asset reserve insolvency.

When the Trustees Report complications its short- and long-term outlooks, it takes into account a long list of variables, including birth rates, death rates, net migration rates, and even annual COLAs. The Trustees assume that annual COLAs will be modest -- but as we just saw, a 3.6% annual raise is anything but average.

Social Security's outsize 2027 raise risks draining the OASI even faster than initially forecast.

President Trump's "Massive, Beautiful Bill" already moved up the projected OASI asset reserve insolvency timeline by one quarter (from the first quarter of 2033 to the fourth quarter of 2032). It's entirely possible the 2027 Trump bump further accelerates the timeline to sweeping benefit cuts.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

Emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the significant positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

Signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the newly introduced year.

Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj.

His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”.

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

Recent findings suggest that england centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

Industry observers note that while some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

Industry observers note that the Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

According to recent reports, hemmings, 19, has emerged from the academy and already made a real impression on his manager. Despite the high regard for those youngsters, this always appeared likely to be a tough proposition against a full-strength PSG team. Indeed, before this game in Salzburg only 39 per cent of Europa League winners have beaten their Champions League rivals in this fixture.

The French champions did start slowly, but had been cranking up the pressure before taking a 20th minute lead with a spectacular strike from their Georgian superstar.

Doué forced a save from Marco Bizot and, after Villa failed to clear, the loose ball landed in the path of Kvaratskhelia, who cut inside on the left to his right foot before smashing a shot into the roof of the net.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx.

Industry observers note that it was a strike of sheer power and accuracy, catching Bizot by surprise. PSG briefly appeared in control, but Villa responded superbly. In 17 minutes they created six goal-scoring chances before the outstanding Madjo finally made one of them count.

Before his goal, he had narrowly missed the target twice with a pair of headers from John McGinn’s crosses. Villa also had another opportunity 10 minutes before half-time, when Pacho’s mistake allowed Hemmings to run from the centre circle unopposed. As he entered the penalty area, the PSG defenders had raced back to recover and a promising moment ended with Madjo curling a shot wide.

PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov then produced his first save just before the break, turning away Boubacar Kamara’s close-range header. Villa did carve out another golden chance when Madjo’s strength took hm past Pacho, but he hit the outside of the post. Madjo’s moment did come, though, as he once again bullied Pacho to divert a McGinn cross into the roof of the net.

Recent findings suggest that villa were buoyant, but it was PSG who scored the crucial second goal after Doué was awarded the goal following a VAR review. Doué was sent clear down the right by substitute Ousmane Dembélé and confidently beat Bizot, with reviews concluding that he had been played onside by Matty Cash.

The game was refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but was denied entry to the United States.

Recent findings suggest that it became rather fractious as time began to tick away, with McGinn booked after complaining over the placement of a free-kick. Madjo was replaced by Tammy Abraham with 17 minutes left and this will be an evening he will never forget.

Recent findings suggest that the Champions League and Europa League winners fight it out in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg as PSG take on Aston Villa. PSG took on English opposition in the Super Cup a year ago, when they played Tottenham. PSG fell 2-0 down in that game in Udine but scored two late goals to take it to penalties, where they won 4-3. These sides met in the Champions League knockout stages two seasons ago; PSG did progress from the quarter-final encounter as they went on to win the competition but not without a scare as Aston Villa did win at Villa Park and PSG only progressed 5-4 on aggregate. The two clubs have been involved in a transfer this week, with left-back Lucas Digne re-joining PSG from Aston Villa.

Aston Villa have played in the Super Cup once before back in 1982 when they took in Barcelona. They lost the first leg 1-0 over at Camp Nou but fought back to win the second leg 3-0 at Villa Park to claim the trophy. Aston Villa were last in action out in the Far East last Friday, falling to a 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich in Hong Kong. It has been a substantial summer of change at the club, with key starters like Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans departing and the likes of Alejandro Garnacho and Joao Gomes arriving.

Industry observers note that “I feel like the club is in a new era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”.

Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

Industry observers note that “I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.
