It has averaged a 9.2% annualized return during the past five years compared to Berkshire's 15.7% average return. During the past 10 years, Markel stock has posted an average return of 8.5% to 14.1% for Berkshire.

But like Berkshire, there is a lot to like about Markel.

You can't gauge Markel's quarter by looking at traditional earnings based on generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) because the unrealized investment gains and losses from its portfolio are included. Those unrealized gains or losses distort the actual performance of the company.

Sources indicate that but if you look at its adjusted operating income, that reveals how much the company made on the businesses it owns. In Q3, its adjusted operating income rose 14% from a year ago to $707 million, or $37.51 per share. That soundly beat analysts' estimates of $27.76 per share. Its revenue jumped 6% year-over-year to $4.16 billion, which easily beat estimates of $3.78 billion.

According to recent reports, within insurance, Markel saw its adjusted underwriting gross premium volume increase by 9% for the quarter. This excludes its global reinsurance division, which it exited in the past year, and its specialty car insurance business Hagerty, which transitioned to a fronting arrangement. Also, its net investment income increased 5% to $233 million.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Recent findings suggest that the key result in insurance is the combined ratio, which measures how much the manufacturer makes in profits from premiums after claims are paid out and operating expenses are subtracted. Markel had a combined ratio of 92%, down from 93% a year ago.

For the full year, the combined ratio is 92%, down from 95% in 2026. This is a good thing because a combined ratio of more than 100 means you are paying out more than you are taking in. A ratio below 100 means you are making more than you are paying out. So, a combined ratio of 92% means Markel is making more profit per dollar of premiums than it was last year.

Sources indicate that markel's businesses, known as Markel Ventures, also performed well. Its industrial holdings saw operating income rise 29% year-over-year to $131 million, while its financial segment increased 30% to $80 million and its consumer properties rose 80% to $31 million.

In a recent development, markel doesn't provide short-term projections, but its trends within insurance and its holdings are promising. The company is built to perform well in negative markets, which is a massive reason the shares surged in recent weeks.

When investors make a flight to safety, they head for companies like Markel, which is grounded by its insurance holdings and conservative underwriting and its durable, value-oriented investments with low debt and stable earnings.

The stock is also fairly cheap right now, trading at less than 14 times earnings. I like it as a long-term buy, and it's particularly valuable now during bouts of market volatility.

In a recent development, the market for server central processing units (CPUs) has been growing rapidly amid the increasing adoption of agentic AI and inference applications. This explains why Nvidia decided earlier this year to offer its latest-generation Vera server CPUs as a stand-alone product to customers.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

The company already had a server CPU before Vera, known as Grace, but it was available as part of rack-scale systems that integrated graphics cards, networking chips, memory, and other components into a single package. Nvidia's latest quarterly report is proof that its move into the stand-alone server CPU market is paying off.

It has been revealed that the product has been adopted by leading hyperscalers, neocloud providers, and AI companies, including Oracle, Meta Platforms, OpenAI, CoreWeave, Nebius, and others. In fact, Nvidia has doubled down on the server CPU market by offering a CPU-based rack-scale server platform to handle agentic AI and inference applications.

Interim CEO Colette Kress remarked on the latest earnings call:.

Investors may be wondering what's going on with Bank of America (BAC -3.15%)stock, as it has trailed other large bank stocks in recent weeks.

The second-largest bank in the U.S. has seen its share price plummet by about 5% during the past month (as of Nov. 19) to $48.57 per share. And since it hit a 52-week high of $65.23 on Aug. 17, it has dropped about 25%.

Meanwhile, the KBW Nasdaq Bank Index, which tracks the 24 largest U.S. banks, has fallen about 3% during the past month and 15% during the past three months..

So why has Bank of America stock lagged behind its major competitors, and is it a buy at recent prices?

Bank of America did not have a great third quarter, missing revenue and earnings estimates.

Overall, revenue rose 3% to $30 billion but that missed Wall Street estimates of $30.7 billion. Net interest income (NII) accounted for more than half of that, up 8% to about $16.4 billion, on higher loan and deposit balances and a net yield that was 15 basis points higher at 2.16%.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

But what hurt Bank of America more than other megabanks was its lackluster trading and investment banking results. Trading revenue fell by 5% when the firm had expected it to be little changed. Investment banking was worse, with revenue down about 11% year over year in Q3.

By comparison, it underperformed the other massive banks as JPMorgan Chase (JPM -3.03%), Citigroup (C -4.04%), and Wells Fargo (WFC -2.47%) all had double-digit percentage gains in investment banking fees. JPMorgan Chase and Citigroup also had solid gains in trading, while Wells Fargo was down 1%, but better than Bank of America.

After the results were released in mid-October, Wells Fargo analyst Mike Mayo called Bank of America's capital markets performance "easily worst in class.".

In investment banking, Bank of America missed out on some hotter parts of the market, including debt underwriting and artificial intelligence (AI) financing. And equity underwriting grew only 3.4%, lagging behind its rivals. In trading, Bank of America saw fixed income trading decline 17% while global debt issuance was up 10% in Q3.

Earnings also fell short of estimates, with Bank of America reporting earnings of $0.91 per share. However, that was offset by a $0.17-per-share hit from a $1.2 billion Treasury Department fine for violations of anti-money-laundering rule compliance. Without this fine, EPS was $1.08 per share, which was still below the average estimate of $1.10 per share.

It has been revealed that these problems all contributed to Bank of America stock being dumped more than its peers last quarter. Is Bank of America stock now a buy at a considerable recent prices?

Shares are super cheap right now, trading at less than 12 times earnings and 9 times forward earnings. Wall Street analysts have a median price target of $62 per share, which suggests 23% upside, so basically clawing back what it lost.

According to recent reports, the sell-off makes Bank of America stock attractive from a valuation standpoint, so it's a hold if you own it, with a solid dividend. I don't know if it stands out as a great buy even at its low valuation relative to its large-bank peers, mainly because it may be more vulnerable to rising interest rates and U.S. economic cyclicality than JPMorgan Chase and Citigroup, given its larger reliance on consumer banking.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that according to Ripple, the creator of XRP (XRP -1.60%), the XRP Ledger (XRPL) will have quantum-secure wallets by 2028.
  • XRP could sure use a catalyst, with its price being down 73% from its all-time high set in July 2025.
  • First, let's get some clarity on what is even at stake with the issue of security against quantum computers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Alex Carchidi – Nov 21, 2026 at 7:05AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than XRP ›.

Sources indicate that according to Ripple, the creator of XRP (XRP -1.60%), the XRP Ledger (XRPL) will have quantum-secure wallets by 2028. Ripple itself set that target date in April of this year, and the XRP Ledger Foundation officially placed the corresponding upgrade onto its roadmap on Nov. 4.

XRP could sure use a catalyst, with its price being down 73% from its all-time high set in July 2025. But making more secure wallets will probably not do what holders are hoping for regarding the coin's price, at least not outside a very narrow and improbable set of circumstances. Here's why this upgrade probably won't be a game changer.

First, let's get some clarity on what is even at stake with the issue of security against quantum computers.

In technical terms, each XRP wallet, like nearly all other crypto wallets, has a secret private key and also a public key that anyone can see on a wallet-scanning website. The private key is what grants access to move funds from the account.

Deriving the private key from the public one is impossible in practical terms with today's hardware. But a powerful enough quantum computer could theoretically do exactly that in the future, meaning an attacker with such a computer could steal funds from individual wallets and likely spark a mass exodus of capital once the theft was discovered.

According to recent reports, in March of this year, Alphabet's Google researchers published a paper estimating that breaking the cryptography that secures most crypto wallets could be possible with a significantly weaker quantum computer than previously expected. In a survey published in March 2026, the Global Risk Institute found that experts put the odds of such a machine arriving within 10 years at 28% to 49%.

CRYPTO · As of 8:49 AM ET 11/21/26.

Therefore, the XRPL's target preparedness date of 2028 probably leaves it with a decent margin of error if quantum computers advance faster than anticipated due to quantum computing companies ramping up their efforts.

Recent findings suggest that plus, given that quantum computers are massive, complex systems, the first dangerous machines will probably belong to governments and the largest companies building them, not ordinary hackers. However, an owner of such a machine may not announce it.

The direct impact of XRPL wallets becoming quantum-secure on its price will almost certainly be minimal.

The upgrade will not increase demand for the coin on its own. And while financial institutions might find it appealing that the XRPL is quantum-secure in advance, it's unclear whether they're willing to pay anything for it.

However, adapting early could pay out major in one specific future scenario.

If a powerful enough quantum computer becomes widely available years before most cryptocurrencies have implemented security measures and it's successfully used to carry out a major crypto hack, capital might flee to XRP as a safe haven.

But don't hold your breath for that to happen; even if the XRPL is an early mover in this domain, there are many other quantum-secure blockchains already in existence, and likely more to come.

Greg Abel Just Approved a Record $9.6 Billion in Stock Buybacks for Berkshire Hathaway Last Quarter, More Than Double the Pace Set in the Second Quarter. Is Berkshire Still a Buy as Shares Sit Near All-Time Highs?

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that greg Abel took over as CEO of Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA -0.47%)(BRKB -0.36%) at the start of 2026, when longtime CEO Warren Buffett stepped down.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 21, 2026 at 7:15AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Berkshire Hathaway ›.

Industry observers note that greg Abel took over as CEO of Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA -0.47%)(BRKB -0.36%) at the start of 2026, when longtime CEO Warren Buffett stepped down. It was the biggest change at the manufacturer in decades. However, Buffett hand-picked Abel and helped to train him for the top spot. And yet, Abel has been surprisingly aggressive in his decision to repurchase Berkshire Hathaway's own stock, something Buffett was very careful about.

With Berkshire Hathaway's stock sitting near all-time highs, is it worth buying? Abel clearly thinks the answer is yes. If you have been thinking about buying the stock, you may want to listen to what his actions are saying.

Recent findings suggest that before digging into Berkshire Hathaway's repurchase, it is worth taking a quick look at another investment Greg Abel orchestrated during the quarter. But that story actually goes back to the first massive acquisition under Abel: Taylor Morrison Home. It was an $8.5 billion purchase, with Abel specifically stating, "Over time, we expect to unify our site-built homebuilding operations into a combined platform enabling us to deliver the dream of homeownership to more Americans.".

Sources indicate that home builders are deeply out of favor today, with home affordability already an concern even before interest rates started to rise (making mortgages more expensive). It was an opportunistic acquisition that was reminiscent of Warren Buffett's investment approach. This is why it was notable that Abel nearly doubled the tech giant's position in publicly traded homebuilder Lennar (LEN +1.01%) during the third quarter. Abel is essentially buying into an industry he believes is mispriced by the market, extending the bet he made with Taylor Morrison Home. Again, this is really no different than what Buffett had done many times before in his long tenure as CEO.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

In a recent development, the key point here is that Abel hasn't suddenly and dramatically changed the way Berkshire Hathaway operates. Historically, the company bought back its own shares only when it believed the stock was trading below its intrinsic value. Of course, that value is determined by the company, and it doesn't disclose the figure it arrives at. But the fact that Greg Abel is buying back stock is a clear indication that he sees value, even though the share price is near all-time highs.

Recent findings suggest that the pace of the share repurchase picked up materially between the second and third quarters, too. In the second quarter, the financial giant bought $4.5 billion worth. In the third quarter, that more than doubled to $9.6 billion. Those are huge numbers, but there's an vital nuance here that shows up on the balance sheet.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Far too often, companies take on debt to fund stock buybacks. Berkshire Hathaway ended the third quarter with roughly $377 billion in cash. That is a massive sum of money, so the $9.6 billion won't weaken the company's financial position. In fact, the company has more cash now than it did at the start of 2026, when it had $373 billion. Buying back Berkshire Hathaway shares is just another investment decision, and it isn't hugely material to the company's operations or financial position.

Industry observers note that essentially, Greg Abel's actions suggest he and the board believe Berkshire Hathaway's stock is worth buying today. These weren't bold moves, but that's not the point. The buyback is a signal, and it's pretty clear: Berkshire Hathaway stock is attractive even at current levels.

Industry observers note that would it be fair to suggest that Berkshire Hathaway is a screaming buy? Probably not. However, if you have been thinking about buying the stock yourself, don't let the stock's lofty price tag scare you away. After all, that fact didn't scare Abel away.

Recent findings suggest that uncertainty in the Middle East, elevated Treasury yields and fears about an AI bubble continue to keep global markets on edge. Given this volatile backdrop, investors seeking stable income can consider enhancing their portfolios by adding dividend-paying stocks.

Industry observers note that however, the vast universe of dividend stocks can make selection challenging. Tracking the ratings of top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist attractive dividend stocks, as their recommendations are backed by in-depth research.

Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Chord Energy is an independent exploration and production organization with long-lived assets primarily in the Williston Basin. With a quarterly base dividend of $1.30 per share, CHRD offers a dividend yield of 3.67%.

In a recent development, in a research note on third-quarter expectations, RBC Capital analyst Scott Hanold reiterated a buy rating on CHRD stock with a price target of $175. "We model production near the top of guidance and continue to see strong performance from fresh wells and base production," said Hanold.

Specifically, the five-star analyst expects Q3 2026 production at 283 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day, or Mboe/d, in line with the Street's consensus and near the high end of the 278 to 284 Mboe/d guidance. Hanold said his Q3 2026 earnings per share estimate increased to $5.29 due to lower non-cash depreciation, depletion and amortization.

Meanwhile, cash flow per share estimate moved lower to $13.59 to reflect Hanold's update based on the current backdrop and commodity mark-to-market. He expects Chord Energy to report capital spending of $375 million for Q3 2026, slightly above the Street's estimate of $369 million.

It has been revealed that overall, Hanold remains bullish on CHRD, given its best-in-class balance sheet. He expects a free cash flow payout of 80% in the third quarter, with the possibility of an upside. Hanold expects investors to focus on management commentary on 2027 capital prepares, Williston M&A opportunities, and long-term performance of 4-mile wells.

It has been revealed that hanold ranks No. 310 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 14.9%. See Chord Energy KPIs on TipRanks.

Williams, an energy infrastructure organization that delivers natural gas, is the next dividend pick. The company recently completed the $5.5 billion acquisition of Momentum Midstream, which will expand its natural gas infrastructure in the Haynesville to meet growing Gulf Coast LNG, power and industrial demand. At a quarterly dividend of $0.5250 per share, Williams offers a yield of 2.89%.

It has been revealed that in her latest research note, RBC Capital analyst Elvira Scotto reiterated a buy rating on Williams stock with a price target of $87. Ahead of Q3 2026 earnings, the analyst noted that she expects WMB to announce strong quarterly performance.

Sources indicate that scotto raised her estimates to reflect insights from the quarterly catch-up call, the completion of the Momentum Midstream acquisition, and mark-to-market quarter-to-date commodity prices. She expects WMB to report Q3 2026 adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of $2,036 million, which is modestly above the Street's consensus estimate.

Furthermore, Scotto expects Williams' Transmission, Power & Gulf segment to increase quarter-over-quarter, driven by the startup of the Socrates power project and favorable natural gas liquids, or NGL, margins.

According to recent reports, scotto noted that WMB stock has underperformed due to backlash related to data centers and investor anticipation of another Power Innovation project. She expects the organization to announce at least one more project before the end of this year, potentially with a fresh customer and a contract duration of 15 to 20 years, which would be a positive catalyst for the stock.

Sources indicate that scotto ranks No. 175 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been profitable 67% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.2%. See Williams Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

EOG Resources, a crude oil and natural gas exploration and production manufacturer, will hold its third-quarter earnings call on Nov. 6. At a quarterly dividend of $1.02 per share, EOG offers a dividend yield of 2.75%.

According to recent reports, heading into Q3 earnings, Jefferies analyst Lloyd Byrne reiterated a buy rating on EOG Resources stock and increased his price target to $185 from $175. The analyst expects the company's Q3 cash flow per share to exceed the Street's consensus by 13%, driven by better-than-expected production.

Byrne expects crude oil production, excluding the UAE, to reach 551 Mboe/d, which is at the high end of guidance (546-551 Mboe/d) and above the Street's projection of 548 Mboe/d, driven by continued growth in the Utica.

According to recent reports, furthermore, Byrne expects cash operating expenses to come in at $10.27 per barrel of oil equivalent, below the midpoint of guidance of $10.05 to $11.35, helped by lower lease operating expenses. Overall, the analyst expects EOG to deliver free cash flow of $2.65 billion, supporting another quarter of buybacks near the minimum 70% shareholder return threshold and implying about $1.5 billion in share repurchases.

"As a first indication of the '27 blueprint, we expect EOG will message another year of mid-single-digit (~3.5%) growth on a flat capital budget (~$6.55bn), which is above the Street modeling 1% oil growth at $6.6bn," noted Byrne.

Breakfast News: When Tech Wobbles, Dividends Pay

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1282 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By TMF Breakfast News – Nov 21, 2026 at 7:30AM EST.
  • Tech stocks have had a bumpy few weeks, to say the least.
  • “When a sell-off is driven more by fear than by fundamentals, it often creates opportunities for patient investors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TMF Breakfast News – Nov 21, 2026 at 7:30AM EST.

Tech stocks have had a bumpy few weeks, to say the least. Before we continue this edition of Breakfast News, here are some words of wisdom from Fools:.

By Matt Frankel, CFP®Team Hidden Gems.

“When a sell-off is driven more by fear than by fundamentals, it often creates opportunities for patient investors. My advice is the same as it was in 2020. Keep your emergency fund intact, don’t sell in a panic, and if you have long-term money to invest, consider putting it to work in great businesses at better prices.”.

By Yasser El-ShimyTeam Rule Breakers.

In a recent development, “We are technically in correction territory today. My rule in moments like this is simple: if you worry about short-term volatility, avoid unprofitable companies or cash-burning businesses trading on high price-to-sales (P/S) multiples. When liquidity tightens, the market stops being generous. Ideally, we plan to keep our investments for at least five years, and be diversified across asset classes, market caps, industries and geographies. Ultimately, the market will find its footing, and it is vital we do not lose our heads in the meantime.”.

The Nasdaq-100 has fallen more than 13% in one month, as of this writing. Dividend payers, meanwhile, have held up well, and many have risen.

According to recent reports, in October, the market’s dividend yield was about 1.1%, the lowest in 155 years. But dividends have driven a massive share of the market’s long-term returns. In their recent FoolFest session, Investing for Income: Dividends and More, TMF analysts Anthony Schiavone and Jason Moser showed how big: If you’d invested $100 in 1871, price gains alone would have turned it into about $168,000. With dividends reinvested, you’d have almost $114 million.

We asked four of our analysts their favorite dividend stocks right now. Here’s what they noted.

The cornerstone of Berkshire Hathaway’s (BRKB -0.36%) sustained success, as articulated by Warren Buffett in his 2022 shareholder letter, is the identification of companies that consistently increase their dividends at an above-average pace over extended periods.

As Buffett explained, dividend “growth occurred every year, just as certain as birthdays,” highlighting Coca-Cola (KO +0.94%) and American Express (AXP -3.02%) as prime examples. Buffett labeled dividend growth as the “secret sauce” to Berkshire’s investment philosophy.

I think Domino’s Pizza (DPZ -1.04%), which Berkshire bought in 2024 and sold in early 2026, also has the attributes of a dividend darling. The manufacturer has an enduring, asset-light business model that generates a ton of free cash flow, which is used to shrink the share count and to pay consistently higher dividends. That’s the secret sauce for me: higher dividends with a shrinking share count.

In a recent development, GE Aerospace (GE -2.90%) won’t land on many dividend enthusiast lists, because it only emerged as a stand-alone aviation business in April 2024. But in the 2.5 years since, GE has raised its quarterly dividend by 68% cumulatively, and given its lean business model and market position, I believe we’ll see additional aggressive hikes ahead.

According to recent reports, GE merges AI capability with kaizen (continuous improvement) processes through its “Flight Deck” platform to speed production processes and reduce costs. It’s on track to end 2026 with stellar net income and free cash flow margins — both around 18%. And demand stretches to the horizon given the aerospace industry’s supply-constrained state.

Sources indicate that GE’s commercial services backlog of $170 billion alone is more than triple total manufacturer annual revenue of approximately $51 billion. For investors seeking diversification from technology investments, note that backlog orders tied to jet engines are likely firmer than those linked to AI infrastructure (and I invest in both types of backlogs!).

The current dividend yield is 0.6%, but there’s room for growth through dividend payout increases, given GE’s healthy payout ratio of only 20%. This capable aerospace giant stands out for its excellent financial condition and relative safety for dividend investors.

Five-year price prediction: $562.78, implying an annualized return of around 11%.

Cisco Systems (CSCO -4.29%) rarely steals the spotlight from flashier chipmakers, yet this networking giant has quietly become a reliable dividend compounder.

Industry observers note that cisco has raised its quarterly payout every year for 15 consecutive years, currently paying $1.68 per share annually, for a roughly 1.7% yield. With a conservative earnings payout ratio under 45% and generous free cash flow growth, there is plenty of runway for future dividend increases.

Under the hood, Cisco’s business is far stronger and more tied to artificial intelligence than many income investors realize. In its fiscal Q1 2027 report, Cisco posted its fastest revenue and earnings growth in over 15 years, with quarterly sales jumping 24% to a record $18.5 billion.

Management also doubled its full-year forecast for hyperscaler AI infrastructure revenue to $9 billion as cloud giants snap up its high-speed switches and optical gear to connect massive AI clusters, all while returning $3.7 billion to shareholders through dividends and buybacks.

Trading around 18 times forward earnings with an entrenched enterprise and AI footprint, Cisco gives long-term investors a dependable income stream backed by accelerating growth.

In a recent development, pharma boasts a range of dividend payers with long, reliable histories. But it’s hard to beat AbbVie (ABBV +0.94%) right now. The company’s 50+ year history of increasing its annual dividend goes back way before its 2013 spin-out from Abbott.

It has been revealed that its yield, around 2.5%, is attractive and sustainable, with a reasonable payout ratio (based on cash flow) — a true Dividend Aristocrat. And the organization has already navigated past its most difficult patent expiration, making growth easier going forward.

Recent findings suggest that pfizer (PFE -0.51%), on the other hand, offers a very different profile. Earlier this year, I noted that they were paying out all their cash flow (and then some) to cover their dividend. The yield has come down a bit (to around 6%) thanks to price appreciation, and their payout ratio, while still stretched, is a little less alarming at about 83%.

Nevertheless, recent revenue growth is likely to be short-lived — a new round of patent expirations peaks in 2027-2028. Pfizer recently committed to maintaining its dividend, but my guess is that they’ll cut it in the next few years, so higher yields aren’t always better!

Sources indicate that dividends rarely make headlines, but they pay you in cash regardless of what the market does. That steady income makes it easier to stay invested when prices fall. And when a tech giant keeps raising its dividend, it’s also signaling confidence that it will keep earning the money to pay it.

Recent findings suggest that still, not all dividends are equal. A very high yield could be a trap if the stock price has fallen because the business is struggling and the payout is unsustainable. So look past the yield. Check whether the tech giant earns enough cash to cover its dividend and whether its debt is under control. The best dividend stocks keep paying you more over time.

If you could own only one dividend stock, which would it be and why?

  • Here's a look at the case for and against investing in UPS stock right now.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt DiLallo – Nov 21, 2026 at 7:30AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than United Parcel Service ›.

UPS (UPS -2.65%) stands out for its dividend yield these days. At 6%, it's several times higher than the S&P 500's 1.1% yield. That wide divergence might have you wondering whether it's a trap or a bargain.

Here's a look at the case for and against investing in UPS stock right now.

UPS recently reported its third-quarter earnings, giving investors a glimpse into the safety of its dividend, which the firm has maintained or increased every year since its 1999 IPO. The metric that matters most for dividend investors is its cash flow. UPS has generated $6 billion in cash from operations through the first nine months of this year. Meanwhile, its free cash flow, after accounting for payments made under its Driver Choice Program, was $4.2 billion. That was just barely enough to cover its dividend, which cost the company $4.1 billion.

According to recent reports, UPS now expects to generate about $6.1 billion in free cash flow for the full year and anticipates paying $5.4 billion in dividends, subject to board approval. That would put its payout ratio at roughly 89%, which is high. If market conditions unexpectedly deteriorate, its dividend could be at risk of a reduction. On a positive note, the company has $6.8 billion in cash on its balance sheet, providing a bit more cushion.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

UPS is in the middle of a strategic transition away from less profitable Amazon volumes toward higher-margin business, including healthcare logistics. The organization is nearing the completion of its Amazon glide-down and the reconfiguration of its cost structure to align with these lower volumes. Its third-quarter report indicated that this strategy is delivering results. Its revenue rose 6.7%, with growth across all segments. That gave the company the confidence to boost its full-year outlook, including for free cash flow.

The company is now on track to deliver $7.28 per share of adjusted earnings. At its recent $110 share price, UPS trades at about 15x earnings. That's a bargain compared to the broader market (the S&P 500 trades at over 23x earnings).

Sources indicate that UPS wouldn't have to grow very fast to deliver strong total returns from here. With a 6% yield, the organization could deliver double-digit total returns with around 4% annual earnings-per-share growth (assuming it maintained its current low valuation multiple). Meanwhile, if earnings grow faster and its valuation improves, UPS could deliver much stronger total returns, potentially in the mid-teens.

It has been revealed that I lean toward bargain, but this isn't a dividend stock you can bank on just yet. I'm watching three things. First, revenue needs to continue rising. Second, I want to see next year's free cash flow guidance, since it needs to remain well above $5.4 billion to cover the dividend. Finally, I want to make sure debt doesn't creep up to fund the payout. If UPS continues executing its turnaround strategy and gets back on a sustainable growth trajectory, it's a bargain at the current price. However, if it faces a setback, the dividend could be at risk.

Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end

📅 13 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 20 min read (4093 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~20 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events?
  • There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.
  • Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

According to recent reports, it was a shame because in that cameo, Fernandes indicated he has returned from the World Cup in excellent shape, the tempo of United’s play immediately lifting when he had the ball. It is wrong to make conclusions in the summer, but you are on safe ground to state he will be integral to their ambitions.

Croke Park is a stadium steeped in history and another chapter was penned here, as the capacity crowd made this the highest attended soccer match in Ireland with 82,000 coming through the gates: it is a magnificent venue, one that would be well capable of hosting a Champions League final.

Michael Carrick hopes in years to come that is the stage where his team will be but, right now, it is a case of learning to walk again before they can run and he more than anyone will know how far off that target is, not that it will stop him trying to get there.

Industry observers note that the one thing that is obvious about the way United play under him is the first thought from everyone is to go forward rapidly. Yes, this was only a friendly, but the ambition to be on the front foot and cause problems was evident from the start.

The team in red had much the better of the opening exchanges, with Diogo Dalot having the first shot that went over but, unlike on July 25, when Mayo beat Kerry here in Gaelic football’s All Ireland final, which went viral, nobody was cheering the sight of a ball clearing the bar.

It was like a home game for United and the majority got what they wanted in the 15th minute when a slick counter-attack ended with Bryan Mbuemo sliding a pass into Joshua Zikzee, who rifled past James Trafford with a first-time finish.

In a recent development, devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n.

Zirkzee is unlikely to be part of Carrick’s squad beyond the transfer window, with interest from clubs in Italy, and it would be disingenuous to suggest his career at Old Trafford has been successful, but his attitude was exemplary and he played as if he was desperate to change his manager’s mind.

There may have been an anticipation that United would stride clear, but this game was also about Leeds, whose summer has been encouraging and whose confidence from staying up last season has evidently enabled them to blossom.

In a recent development, you would be way off the mark if you include them in your conversations about which clubs are going to be relegated next May, and the sense they demonstrated to stay with Daniel Farke has paid off. They have bought some good players, not least goalkeeper James Trafford and Harry Wilson.

Top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA.

Trafford has done the right thing getting away from Manchester City and you could argue that he is already reaping the benefit of playing for a manager who wants him, as he made a fabulous save in the 23rd minute to thwart Mbuemo. It was all part of performance that led to him being named player of the match.

He was involved in the move that brought the Leeds equaliser, too, as his long clearance caused uncertainty and led to Tyler Fletcher being pickpocketed by Dan James and he nudged a pass into Brenden Aaronson, who kept his cool and danced into the area, ignoring Senne Lammens, to finish.

Leeds hit back with their first shot on target! 💥Brenden Aaronson with a cool finish 🥶 pic.twitter.com/5WsSZY41j6.

Recent findings suggest that it was an entertaining affair, mercifully lacking the bile that would usually bubble away when it is staged in England, and the longer the game advanced, the better Leeds looked. They finished the opening period strongly and came back after the restart, with 10 changes, in the same fettle.

Farke, whose team had shown their ability to score heavily when they pummelled Liverpool 4-2 in Chicago 10 days ago, would have taken plenty of encouragement, but the perfectionist in him would have cursed the opportunities that were squandered early in the second period.

Recent findings suggest that the misses proved costly as the game meandered and the shoot-out went United’s way, after Wilson and James Justin failed from 12 yards, with Noussair Mazraoui thumping in the decisive kick. It really is never dull.

Manchester United Lammens (Mee 61); Dalot (Mazraoui 60), Yoro, Heaven (Armer 46), Amass (Shaw 60); Santos (Collyer 46), T Fletcher (Tielemans 61); Diallo (J Fletcher 60), Zirkzee (Cunha 60), Dorgu (Thompson 46); Mbuemo (Fernandes 60).Subs not used Heath, Honor, Lacey, Gabriel.

Leeds United Trafford (Cairns 46); Bijol (Rodon 46), Muharemovic (Cresswell 46), Bornauw; Bogle (Gnonto 46), Longstaff (Stach 46), Tanaka (Ampadu 46), Chadwick (Justin 46); James (Okafor 46), Aaronson (Wilson 46); Nmecha (Calvert-Lewin 46).Subs not used Mahady, Lienou, Mills, Piroe.

Recent findings suggest that decent enough watch for roughly half the game, settled on a shoot-out in which Alex Cairns got nowhere near any of Manchester United’s penalties. Doubt he will lose much sleep over it. Bruno Fernandes grinned broadly when he missed.

Leeds United 4 Manchester United 5.

Bottom left. Manchester United win the Boyle Sports Cup.

Leeds United 4 Manchester United 4.

Leeds United 4 Manchester United 4.

Leeds United 4 Manchester United 3.

Industry observers note that top right. Sudden death now effectively.

Rolls it casually past the right post.

So there will be another short delay.

And I think Amapdu’s signal means Leeds will go first.

The ref decides to call time as the stewards cannot catch the juvenile intruders.

According to recent reports, not sure what we can say about stadium safety here but the game has ended prematurely after five kids came on, all of whom got to Bruno Fernandes to take selfies. It was very funny but, equally, plenty on the Manchester United bench were far from happy. Penalties to follow.

Some sealion ball juggling from Mazraoui involving foot, thigh and head, gets him past Justin on the right  but Gnonto heads away his cross.

It has been revealed that two young Man Utd fans run on to the pitch to try to take selfies with Man utd players. They are joined by three more and now another.

It’s like Euro 2016 all over again.

Bruno Fernandes lets fly from 20 yards, cushioning a pass from Tielemans before hammering his shot into the crossbar with little backlift.

Gnonto breaks down the right, plays it infield to Wilson who runs at the heart of the Man Utd defence but smacks his shot into a defender.

Cresswell blocks Mazroui’s shot with his right elbow which was pinned to his side and the ball falls to Bruno Fernandes but Cresswell is there again to block the shot, this time with his legs. From the corner, Bruno Fernandes balloons a long shot over the bar.

Enormous frustration for the masses who have wanted a Bruno goal. He’s just “scored” - right on the moment when our friend the stadium announcer bellowed the match was a sell out but never provided the actual figure – but a linesman’s flag has stopped him in his tracks. You fancy he will have one more involvement before the game creeps towards a penalty shootout.

Bruno Fernandes shoots past Cairns with a left-foot shot from 16 yards, smacking it inside the left post but the flag had long been raised.

The ball pinballs out to Justin by the D from the corner and he hammers a shot that Mee saves with great agility by the right post.

Sources indicate that excellent pass from Okafor from the left ought to have put Calvert-Lewin through but Armer does brilliantly to hold him up. Gnonto makes a run down the side but Calvert-Lewin checks back to shoot into Armer and the ball deflects behind for a corner.

It has been revealed that there will be a shootout if the match is drawn after 90 minutes. The Boyle Sports Cup cannot be shared, it seems.

Mazraoui drives down the right and feeds it inside to Fletcher whose deflected cross falls kindly for Thompson but the young striker cannot control it and Leeds recover.

Amapdu hurls a long throw into the box on the diagonal from the right. Rodon flicks it on and Calvert-Lewin dives to try to nod it past Mee but he can only stick his effort wide. It was just a bit too far in front of him to reach with control and power.

It has been revealed that clever pass from Gnonto sends Wilson into the box on the underlap to cross low, seeking Calvert-Lewin. Mee is out to stop it reaching him. Oakfor sets off on a  bustling run down the left for 35 yards but then fluffs the cross.

Jack Fletcher is playing on the right with Tielemans and Collyer as the central two. Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha are playing centrally with Thompson on the left. Nothing much happening as Leeds keep their defensive shape while Manchester United probe away.

It has been revealed that yoro and Bornauw are the only two starters left. Stach intercepts Matheus Cunha’s cross in from the right.

It has been revealed that understandably Manchester United look disjointed now. Leeds have had longer for their changes to settle.

Seven Manchester United changes: Mee, Tielmans, Shaw, Bruno Fernandes, Jack Fletcher, Matheus Cunha and Mazraoui incoming for Dalot, Lammens, Amass, Mbeumo, Diallo, Zirkzee and Tyler Fletcher.

Dalot slides in to trip Okafor after the Swiss forward was played through the middle by Calvert-Lewin. Stach takes the free-kick from 22 yards, bends it round the wall but Lammens read it well and steps across to catch by the right post.

Sources indicate that zirkzee’s trickery down the right leaves Justin in his wake but having done the hard bit he fluffs the cross, delivering it too high for a shot and too low for a header. Thompson tries to contort himself to reach it but no one is that flexible.

Couple of threatening crosses from Gnonto from the right just elude Calvert-Lewin and Alfie Cresswell, son of Richard, brother of Charlie, follows up the second to shoot from the edge of the box. Lammens gathers comfortably.

Just the 10 half-time changes for Leeds and the worst thing about that was the fact it gave the stadium announcer, who hadn’t grasped that he didn’t need to shout into a loud speaker system, the opportunity to screech unchecked for close to two minutes, leaving everyone with tinnitus. Give the wrong man a microphone and chaos will ensue. Anyway, we are underway in the second period and the one change the majority of the stadium wants to be see is the introduction of Bruno Fernandes. His presence would help United regain some impetus.

Huge cheer as Bruno Fernandes, Luke Shaw et al start to warm up.

Lammens saves from Harry Wilson’s shot from 10 yards after Rodon’s underlapping ran down the right caught Amass off guard.

Sources indicate that senne Lammens to the rescue! 🧤A great reaction save from the Belgian 👏🇧🇪 pic.twitter.com/GRau9yk02n.

Thompson tackles Rodon as he tried to lengthen his stride down the right.

Oddly Bornauw, who is poised to join Hamburg on loan, is the only player kept on from the first half for Leeds.

Sources indicate that gnonto, who is playing at right wing-back, is palyed down the line by Rodon and bends over a low cross looking for Calvert-Lewin’s late run. Lammens dives out to smother it.

Manchester United make three changes – Tynan Thompson, Toby Collyer and Dan Armer replace Santos, Heaven and Dorgu.

While Leeds have made 10 changes.

Cairns; Rodon, Bornauw, Cresswell; Justin, Ampadu, Stach, Gnonto; Wilson, Okafor; Calvert-Lewin.

Pleasant summer watch between largely second string players. Mbeumo looks a class apart from the other attacking players. On this evidence he might be worth a punt for goals and assists topping 25 this season like they did in 2024-25 for Brentford. Though he may have to take pens off Bruno Fernandes to get there.

The ref blows directly on 45 minutes moments after Nmecha rab out of room to control Tanaka’s cross and booted it out for a Man Utd goal-kick.

Manchester United probe patiently for half a minute around the Leeds area but the pass supposed to play Mbeumo through is picked off by Bijol and he plays it out to James who hares off down the left for 50 yards, cuts in on his right after leaving Yoro in his vapour trail, and whacks a shot over the bar from 22 yards.

According to recent reports, yoro hooks Bogle’s long chip out for a throw-in. This time Leeds take it short and try to engineer a crossing opportunity but go back to Trafford when they can’t find space.

It has been revealed that mbeumo’s on fire tonight as he has been all pre-season, causing Leeds problems whenever he runs at the defence. Now he storms down the centre-right and arcs a shot from 18 yards that beats Trafford’s leap and crashes into the underside of the crossbar. Bornauw hacks it away.

Amass tries to play a one-two with Zirkzee but the crucial middle pass of the three, from Zirkzee, goes astray.

It has been revealed that trafford dives to catch Dorgu’s cross. But he then boots his punt out for a throw-in and Tanaka is penalised for tussling with Dorgu who was thrown the ball and set off on a dribble down the inside-right.

Sources indicate that bikol heads Longstaff’s free-kick from the right over the bar after clever work from Bogle to earn the opportunity. .

It has been revealed that manchester United 1 Leeds United 1 (Aaronson) James robs Tyler Fletcher in the inside-left position and sprints towards the 18-yard line before slipping it inside to Aaronson. The once erratic finisher takes a touch to put Heaven on his heels then slots a right-foot shot crisply into the bottom left corner.

Leeds hit back with their first shot on target! 💥Brenden Aaronson with a cool finish 🥶 pic.twitter.com/5WsSZY41j6.

Tanaka has two long throws in from the right. Dorgu heads the first one out for the second which is flicked on by Bornauw but Man Utd clear the second ball.

Tyler Fletcher takes a trick out of his old man’s book by grabbing James round the waist once the speed merchant had knocked the ball past him. Leeds go backwards from the free-kick as Man Utd’s press hounds them.

Sources indicate that trafford confidently catches the cross from the corner then bowls it out 40 yards to set Aaronson off on a counter. His solo raid down the right is stymied by Amass’s diligent defending.

Mbeumo drives down the gap between Muharemovic and Bijol, tries to find Doegu but Bornauw slides in to intercept but only succeeds in playing it back to Mbeumo who lashes a left-foot shot that Trafford tips round the right post at full stretch.

In a recent development, top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA.

Industry observers note that there is certainly more urgency about Manchester United’s play. Leeds are living dangerously.

According to recent reports, in the couple of minutes after the goal Manchester United almost punish Leeds’ high defensive line again but Muharemovic rides to the rescue. Bijol is a very good box defender but he lacks pace.

United’s start has been bright and confident and the system they playing is flipping between 4-4-2 and 4-2-3-1 and the first thought is always to go forward. The goal they have just scored is indicative of how they have started and it’s a positive for Joshua Zirkzee, who has spent much of his time at Old Trafford under a cloud, to have finished it with aplomb. Whether it will be enough to keep him at Old Trafford for the long run remains to be seen, particularly as interest from Italy persists, but what can’t be doubted is his attitude. He looks sharp.

It has been revealed that manchester United 1 Leeds United 0 (Zirkzee) Leeds, on the attack, lose possession down the middle and Dorgu works it out to Mbeumo who beats Bijol 20 yards inside the Man Utd half. He pokes it through the Leeds captain;s legs and hares off down the wing until he gets to the 18 yard line and from there he bends the perfect pass to Zirkzee who sweeps home a shot into the bottom left with his left foot.

Devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n.

Industry observers note that manchester United build slowly down the right and then Dalot injects some urgency by whipping in a low cross. Zirkzee meets it not so much with a shot but with the timing of his arrival on the ball, deflecting it towards the right of goal powerfully, Trafford gets down well to save.

Recent findings suggest that leeds cross the free-kick into the box and James’ volley strikes a defender in the midriff and then hits the deck when going for the rebound, bundled over by Yoro. The ref waves play on and Manchester Unted counter with Amad Diallo dribbling down the right until tackled by Chadwick at the price of a corner.

In a recent development, dorgu is penalised for a scissors-tackle on Bornauw. He did get the ball but only after he had caught he blond defender with his other leg. Carrick leaps up to protest, as does Farke but he is saying that Dorgu has twice slid in wildly.

Leeds defend the corner fairly solidly but Manchester United recover possession 30 yards out and set up Dalot to have a crack with a dipping, swerving effort that Trafford pats down in front of his face and catches after it bounces.

Amad Diallo finds Mbeumo down the right and he tries to head the ball across the box but Muharemovic is well-placed to head it back out but an attempt to nod the ball back to Trafford goes astray and the £45m man can’t stop it going out for a corner.

Leeds free-kick for either a foul by Amass on Aaronson or Dorgu on Bogle. Hard to tell, one was a split-second after the other.

In a recent development, amass pulls back Bogle after being tackled by the Leeds wing-back and Leeds build up the right from the free-kick, earning themselves a throw-in parallel with the penalty spot. In Ampadu’s absence Tanaka is the trebuchet, hurling in the long throw that Bornauw nods on but Manchester united clear the second ball.

Recent findings suggest that leeds work the ball back to Taafford from the kick off and he chips it long up the right. Dorgu heads it out for a throw-in. Leeds go backwards again and pass the ball around confidently.

Jaka Bijol captains Leeds, Diogo Dalot leads out Manchester United.

They would be as well delaying the start of the game here the concourses outside this magnificent and historic stadium are packed with crowds taking in the solar eclipse. What a genuinely extraordinary moment! There will be plenty of time later this evening to talk about the football, for now attentions are firmly elsewhere!

🤩 Ready for a first #LUFC start! pic.twitter.com/KU5ica0HcG.

And for Senne Lammens, a fresh shirt number, from 31 to Numero Uno:.

Sources indicate that lammens is not the only one. Marcus Rashford wore 39 in his debut season with Man Utd, moved to 19 for the next three then changed to 10 when Zlatan Ibrahimovic left the club. The 10 shirt has been given to Matheus Cunha so now he will wear 14, the number he had at Barcelona in his Liga title-winning season.

If you’re watching in the UK, the match is live on ITV. A friendly! Live on ITV. That’s Croke Park for you.

Manchester United  Lammens; Dalot, Yoro, Heaven, Amass; Andrey Santos, T Fletcher; Diallo, Mbeumo, Dorgu; Zirkzee.

The most expensive British goalkeeper, James Trafford, makes his unofficial debut.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester United and Leeds United at a sold-out Croke Park in Dublin. Last year Leeds played Milan in the Irish capital and drew a crowd of 52,000 but at the GAA citadel, as I think I’m contractually obliged to call it, there will be 83,000 present, a testament to the Premier League’s reach and these two clubs’ popularity in Ireland founded on the exploits of Billy Whelan, Noel Cantwell, Johnny Giles, Roy Keane, Gary Kelly et al. It’s the first club match ever held at the stadium.

According to recent reports, it’s a fixture that always stirs the blood and whenever it comes around you can guarantee that there will be reams of stuff about the War of the Roses, clash in styles, Busby and Revie, Bobby and Jack, large swathes of which this author has been guilty of producing. I’ll spare you all that today because while it’s relevant to fans of both clubs, they know it backwards. And it’s a match that has come around a wee bit too frequently in pre-season recently, first in Perth, Western Australia, in 2019 when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s side beat Marcelo Bielsa’s 4-0, then in 2023 in Oslo when Erik ten Haag’s second or third string defeated Daniel Farke’s threadbare, just relegated squad 2-0 and last year in Stockholm, which ended in a 0-0 draw between two scratch sides.

This one comes round later in the pre-season schedule than those three so we can expect to see stronger XIs, at least for part of the game. Leeds’ pre-season has gone well: after a 3-2 defeat by Wrexham in Tampa, they have beaten Sunderland in Upcoming Jersey, Liverpool in Chicago and RB Leipzig at Elland Road. Manchester United also lost to Wrexham (in Helsinki) then beat Rosenborg in Trondheim, Atlético in Stockholm and drew one apiece with the European champions, PSG, in Gothenburg last time out.

While Leeds will have latest signing James Trafford available and Noah Okafor, who scored twice in Leeds’ first league victory at Old Trafford for 45 years last April, in the squad for the first time after the World Cup, Manchester United have Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford back in training since the start of the week but it seems too soon for them to start but Youri Tielemans is pushing to make his first start.

Is AMD the Stock to Buy With Nvidia in Limbo?

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (733 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • 10 stocks we like better than Advanced Micro Devices ›.
  • It has been revealed that with all the unknowns surrounding Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) right now, some investors are starting to wonder if Advanced Micro Devices (AMD -13.25%) is the semiconductor stock to turn to instead.
  • Any analysis of a possible change should start by asking whether AMD is a viable alternative.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Keithen Drury – Nov 21, 2026 at 7:40AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Advanced Micro Devices ›.

It has been revealed that with all the unknowns surrounding Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) right now, some investors are starting to wonder if Advanced Micro Devices (AMD -13.25%) is the semiconductor stock to turn to instead. This is a natural progression because the two are competitors in the data center space.

Any analysis of a possible change should start by asking whether AMD is a viable alternative. Does AMD have problems of its own to contend with?

In a recent development, my analysis suggests there's at least one concern that investors must watch out for, and I think it is definitive in determining which stock is the better pick right now. Let me explain.

Industry observers note that AMD is commonly viewed as an alternative to Nvidia. Nvidia's data center products were more advanced than AMD's when the initial artificial intelligence build-out kicked off, and that allowed Nvidia to seize early market share. First-mover advantage can be difficult to overcome, and with a significant majority of data center computing infrastructure being built for Nvidia products, AMD has found itself in a deep hole.

Recent findings suggest that however, the biggest problem AMD faces isn't hardware; it's software. Nvidia's CUDA software is considered better than AMD's ROCm software, although AMD has improved recently. Still, this is an advantage Nvidia holds over AMD, and it has created a gap unlikely to be closed.

Recent findings suggest that AMD has seen increased success in the data center realm as clients look for cheaper alternatives to Nvidia GPUs, which can be quite expensive due to high demand. During the third quarter, AMD's data center revenue rose 97% year over year to $8.5 billion. However, because AMD also has significant consumer and embedded processor divisions, the results are a bit worse when the entire company is examined. Companywide, AMD's revenue rose 45% year over year to $13.4 billion. Considering that Nvidia is posting $100 billion-plus in quarterly revenue, AMD is a much smaller company.

In a recent development, normally, being a smaller organization is an advantage because it's easier to grow faster. But that hasn't been the case here. Nvidia has outpaced AMD's growth every step of the way, which is impressive considering the fact that it's almost 9 times larger than AMD. I think this speaks to the unbreakable lead that Nvidia has built from a technological and market-share standpoint.

It has been revealed that however, with new leadership coming to power at Nvidia, it could shift how the company approaches product development and the market. This could lead to a shifting landscape over the next five years, but as of now, Nvidia remains the leader, with AMD in second place.

That's still not the reason I'm avoiding investing in AMD. AMD has stock problems of its own.

AMD is one of the more expensive stocks in the market right now. If you use next year's earnings projections to value the stock, it trades for about 29 times next year's earnings.

AMD PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts.

Industry observers note that that's a pretty expensive price tag. Not even some of the AI hyperscalers have that expensive a price tag. Furthermore, Nvidia is far cheaper, trading at around 10 times next year's earnings.

While I understand that Nvidia deserves something of a price discount due to leadership uncertainty and the sources of its sales, 10 times next year's earnings is an absolute steal. Nvidia could lose half of its earnings and still trade at less than 20 times next year's earnings.

That's a huge pricing mismatch, and I think that the market has gone too far in discounting Nvidia. As a result, I don't think that AMD is the best stock to buy during Nvidia's turmoil. Instead, Nvidia is likely the best stock to buy, as the market has far overblown what is going on with the stock.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that that remarked, for a five-figure investment, you could pay for these coffees from your dividends alone.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Thomas Niel – Nov 21, 2026 at 7:40AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Starbucks ›.

"Stop buying coffee out" has become commonplace personal finance advice, but is there a way to invest and cover your monthly Starbucks (SBUX -1.28%) bill? Let's say you go to Starbucks a few times a week, which, over the course of a year, can really add up: 150 trips a year at $4.96 per cup, or just under $5, comes out to $744 annually.

Industry observers note that that remarked, for a five-figure investment, you could pay for these coffees from your dividends alone. However, in terms of potential gains from holding the stock, is it worth it? Not necessarily.

According to recent reports, following Starbucks' latest dividend increase, shares in what is one of the largest consumer discretionary companies now pay $0.63 per share quarterly. That comes to $2.52 per share in annual dividend payments. Divide $744 by $2.52 per share, and you get 296 Starbucks shares needed to cover this expense. Starbucks stock currently trades for around $106.50 per share, meaning you would need around $31,524 to enter this position.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Industry observers note that any way you slice it, that's a tall order. Even as annual dividend growth has averaged nearly 8% over the past five years, the latest dividend increase was only 1.6%. If low dividend growth persists, the price of a cup of Starbucks coffee could outpace the payouts. Also, don't assume buying today means trading lower dividend growth for the potential for greater gains down the road.

According to recent reports, the organization's "Back to Starbucks" turnaround, focused on improving the in-store experience, has been in motion for over two years now. Recent results, including a 7.2% increase in same-store sales during the September-ended quarter, have investors very confident about further improvements in growth and profitability.

However, after this rally, the stock trades at 33.5 times forward earnings, a massive premium to peers like McDonald's. Although further strong quarterly results could help sustain this valuation, any sort of earnings hiccup could quickly send shares back in the wrong direction. Considering this, I would skip buying Starbucks shares for now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fears around the artificial intelligence trade and higher pressure on oil prices are weighing on global markets, but a few stocks offer investors solid growth prospects even in choppy times.

Investors with a long-term horizon can look beyond the ongoing volatility and track the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts to pick attractive stocks with strong long-term growth potential.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Health insurer UnitedHealth delivered better-than-expected results for the third quarter of 2026. The tech giant also raised its full-year earnings outlook, reflecting continued progress on its turnaround initiative.

Following the Q3 print, Morgan Stanley analyst Erin Wright reiterated a buy rating on UNH stock with a price target of $529. "UNH's beat & raise reinforces turnaround momentum, with improving MA [Medicare Advantage]/Optum Health supporting a higher '26 EPS baseline & upside to '27 consensus," said Wright.

It has been revealed that the five-star analyst added that better-than-expected performance in the UnitedHealthcare and Optum Health businesses supported another upgrade to the firm's 2026 adjusted earnings per share outlook to at least $20.50. Wright noted that UNH raised the earnings guidance despite incremental investments planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.

According to recent reports, furthermore, Wright highlighted management's view that the consensus 2027 EPS of $22.63 was too conservative. Reaching even the low end of the tech giant's 13% to 16% long-term EPS growth target would imply an EPS of $23.17.

Wright raised her 2026 EPS estimate to $20.65 from $19.82 and 2027 EPS to $23.24 from $22.54, reflecting the latest upside and an improving 2026 medical loss ratio to 87.4% from 88.1%. Overall, she believes that UNH's operational performance continues to improve, increasing her confidence in its UHC strategy and Optum Health turnaround execution.

According to recent reports, wright ranks No. 264 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 15%. See UnitedHealth Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

Social media giant Meta Platforms has been making headlines since the launch of its Muse AI agent, which is seeing solid traction. Investors look forward to updates on the company's AI strategy when it announces its third-quarter results on Oct. 21.

Sources indicate that heading into Q3 earnings, Guggenheim analyst Michael Morris maintained a buy rating on Meta stock and increased his price target to $850 from $700, reflecting higher estimates for 2027. He expects Muse usage momentum and engagement levels to shape investor sentiment into the Q3 earnings call.

Industry observers note that specifically, Morris highlighted that, according to Apptopia, Muse reached 1.3 million daily active users in five weeks versus 300,000 in the first week. Given that Muse's current adoption represents less than 0.05% of Meta's 3.6 billion daily active user base, the analyst expects management to prioritize boosting usage over near-term monetization.

"Over time, we believe Muse monetizes primarily through businesses paying to reach consumers through their agents, consistent with the economics of Meta's core advertising business, rather than consumer wallets," remarked the five-star analyst. He added that the checkout integrations with Shopify and PayPal reflect this framework.

While there are concerns that a rival could overtake Muse or the recently rolled out Muse Wonder and push Meta into a prolonged cycle of overinvestment, Morris remains bullish due to the manufacturer's strong record in scaling WhatsApp and competing strongly with TikTok via Reels as well as free distribution to an extensive user base.

Morris ranks No. 629 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Meta Platforms KPIs on TipRanks.

Next is semiconductor company Marvell Technology. Earlier this month, Marvell held its Investor Day, where it raised its total addressable market estimate to $400 billion by 2030, reflecting solid AI-led demand tailwinds.

After hosting a non-deal roadshow with Marvell's senior management following the Investor Day, Stifel analyst Tore Svanberg reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $370.

The five-star analyst noted that a major focus of the roadshow was the XPU and XPU Attach mix, as Marvell's Custom business expands toward its FY31 revenue target of $30 billion. In this regard, management reiterated that it expects a balanced mix of XPU and XPU Attach revenue in FY31, though it noted that either segment could grow rapidly enough to shift the mix toward 60/40 or 40/60.

While XPU drove most of the nearly $1.5 billion Custom revenue in FY26, Svanberg expects Marvell's XPU Attach business to grow substantially through the end of the decade, leading to a more balanced mix in this business. At the Investor Day event, the company raised its FY29 Custom target from more than $10 billion to over $12 billion, mainly driven by strength in the XPU Attach business.

It has been revealed that svanberg said that another key topic in the roadshow was whether Marvell can secure enough capacity to meet its raised targets. Management said that it met with suppliers ahead of Investor Day to share its five-year goals and received commitments to support these targets. The analyst believes that Marvell's supply chain commitments give it a competitive edge over rivals as customers seek reliable partners for large-scale infrastructure buildouts.

Svanberg ranks No. 91 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 58% of the time, delivering an average return of 31.8%. See Marvell Technology Statistics on TipRanks.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Greg Abel has already started to make his mark on Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA -0.47%) (BRKB -0.36%).
  • While Abel increased his share repurchases in the third quarter and continued to look for opportunities to fully acquire other companies, he stopped buying Alphabet shares.
  • Buffett built Berkshire Hathaway on the ethos of long-term buy-and-hold investing, and Abel has promised to maintain that philosophy in every investment decision he makes for the organization.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adam Levy – Nov 21, 2026 at 7:58AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Alphabet ›.

Greg Abel has already started to make his mark on Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA -0.47%) (BRKB -0.36%). The CEO took over the job from Warren Buffett at the start of the year, and he's since gone to work deploying tens of billions of dollars worth of capital for shareholders. He completed the acquisitions of OxyChem and Taylor Morrison Homes for a total of $18 billion. He reinitiated repurchases of the stock, buying back more than $16 billion worth of Berkshire through October. And he's added considerably to Berkshire marketable equity portfolio, including buying an estimated $28 billion worth of Alphabet (GOOG -2.59%) (GOOGL -2.70%) stock.

While Abel increased his share repurchases in the third quarter and continued to look for opportunities to fully acquire other companies, he stopped buying Alphabet shares. That's despite the fact that the share price moved meaningfully lower than the price he paid in Alphabet's $10 billion private placement with his firm. Investors may be wondering if anything's changed for Alphabet since that purchase and whether it's worth buying right now.

Greg Abel. Image source: The Motley Fool.

Buffett built Berkshire Hathaway on the ethos of long-term buy-and-hold investing, and Abel has promised to maintain that philosophy in every investment decision he makes for the organization. That said, a long-term outlook doesn't mean Buffett hasn't been known to rapidly change his mind on a company, especially if things change. Only a handful of marketable equity investments have stuck around for Buffett's preferred holding period of "forever.".

Industry observers note that buffett laid out the investment thesis for Alphabet, a position he initiated for Berkshire last year, in an interview this summer. It boils down to the fact that Alphabet has an opportunity to deploy a lot of capital and earn a high return on its invested capital doing so. In other words, Buffett believes Alphabet's massive AI build-out will produce exceptional cash flows over the long run.

While there are growing concerns that Alphabet won't achieve high returns on capital, the financial results so far suggest it's seeing excellent results. Alphabet's Google Cloud segment grew revenue 103% year over year last quarter while expanding its operating margin. That acceleration is tied to a ramp-up in investments starting in 2023, right in line with the timeline of how long it takes before breaking ground on new data center construction translates into placing servers and networking equipment available for rent on its platform.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

According to recent reports, alphabet's reported payback period is well above that reported by other hyperscalers. Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian noted it takes about two years for it to generate revenue equal to the cost of the average server for its cloud platform. However, its custom TPU systems have a payback period of half of that. Over time, a greater portion of Alphabet's capital expenditures will go toward revenue-generating servers and a greater share of those servers will be its own custom hardware with faster payback periods.

As such, it makes sense for Alphabet to raise capital and burn cash to build newly introduced data centers. The return on invested capital is extremely high and the opportunity is absolutely massive. It's playing out exactly as Buffett expects.

If Abel liked Alphabet stock at a price of $355 per share, which is what Berkshire paid for the stock in its private placement, he should like it even more at $280 per share, where it trades today.

Sources indicate that the stock traded around $340 per share throughout the second half of the third quarter, so there was an opportunity for Abel to add to the position before the quarter ended at a price he was previously comfortable paying. However, Alphabet was already Berkshire's third-largest position as of the end of the third quarter, without any additional shares. That could push the bar higher for Abel to add to the position and increase Berkshire's portfolio concentration. (It's notably why I personally haven't added to my own position in Alphabet amid the pullback, as it already accounts for a significant portion of my portfolio.).

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

For investors without a significant position in Alphabet, though, right now looks like an incredible buying opportunity for the stock. Shares trade at just 21 times forward earnings expectations, and the long-term growth potential of its cloud computing segment (which includes its TPU system sales) looks better than ever.

Considering the drop in share price pushed Alphabet to become a much smaller portion of Berkshire's portfolio, Abel may be inclined to buy more shares again this quarter after last quarter's pause.
