💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, five hundred dollars doesn't stretch very far anymore.
  • Recent findings suggest that the idea behind quantum computing is easier to picture than it sounds.
  • Recent findings suggest that the fix is the "logical qubit," a team of physical qubits that works like a choir.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Micah Zimmerman – Nov 21, 2026 at 8:00AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Infleqtion ›.

According to recent reports, five hundred dollars doesn't stretch very far anymore. It buys a nice pair of headphones, a few weeks of groceries, or one good weekend away. It can also get you a small stake in one of the strangest machines anybody is trying to build.

Recent findings suggest that the idea behind quantum computing is easier to picture than it sounds. A regular computer bit works like a light switch: on or off. A qubit is closer to a dimmer that can sit anywhere in between, and when qubits are linked, they can work together to explore a huge number of possibilities. The problem is that qubits are as fragile as a soufflé. A tiny bit of heat or vibration and the whole thing collapses.

Recent findings suggest that the fix is the "logical qubit," a team of physical qubits that works like a choir. If one singer drifts off key, the others hold the note. Whoever builds lots of reliable logical qubits first wins the race.

Here are two quantum computing companies working on this very issue that I'd be willing to split a $500 investment in.

Sources indicate that infleqtion (INFQ -13.43%) traps single atoms with lasers and uses them as qubits. In September 2026, it stated it had linked 30 logical qubits in a single computation using just 80 physical qubits, hitting its 2026 goal. "Delivering 30 logical qubits is an important step on our technology roadmap," CEO Matt Kinsella said.

Sources indicate that its hardware is already in real machines. Infleqtion's processor powers Shunkai, Japan's first working full-stack neutral-atom quantum computer. "Bringing a full-stack quantum system into production operation is a meaningful step toward fault-tolerant quantum computing," noted CTO Pranav Gokhale.

In a recent development, the part I like most is that the same atoms do other jobs today. Infleqtion's Tiqker clock keeps precise time when GPS is jammed, and it recently ran for two weeks straight aboard a U.S. Navy vessel. "The Navy needs dependable timing to navigate, communicate and coordinate operations in the field," Kinsella noted. NASA also expanded its quantum gravity sensor contract, and the U.K. funded a compact radio-direction-finding system.

Sources indicate that that government work is also its weak spot. Last quarter, it cost Infleqtion more to deliver its work than it earned, partly because of timing on the NASA gravity program and thin margins on a contract that was wrapping up. Spending is climbing fast too. Its operating loss was about five times larger than a year ago. The cash it raised through its special-purpose acquisition manufacturer (SPAC) merger gives it room for now.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

It has been revealed that xanadu Quantum Technologies (XNDU -6.59%) uses particles of light as qubits. "Our chips compute without coolant," CEO Christian Weedbrook mentioned, and they can be made with the same kind of silicon processes chipmakers already use.

Light's enemy is loss, meaning photons that leak away before the math is done. Weedbrook called it "our most important engineering challenge," but added, "This is primarily a challenge of engineering, not physics." In November, Xanadu and HyperLight cut the loss in a key optical switch by nearly two-thirds.

Recent findings suggest that it's also lining up help. Xanadu signed hardware partnerships with GlobalFoundries (GFS -8.68%), ASML (ASML -6.63%), and Bluefors, and released Backline, error-correction software built with Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD -13.25%). Mitsubishi Chemical used its algorithms to model semiconductor materials, and Royal Bank of Canada and Booz Allen use its software to train staff. Canada is putting about $140 million toward Inception, a Toronto photonics plant Xanadu expects to start using early next year.

Here's the catch: Xanadu barely has revenue, and it's choosing to keep it that way for now. "Pursuing revenue before meaningful quantum utility or selling systems prematurely would ultimately divert talent and resources," Weedbrook noted. Its target for a commercially viable machine is 2029 or 2030, and until then, its cash burn keeps rising. Xanadu can also sell more shares through an existing program, and an executive said the company weighs that "almost on a day-by-day basis.".

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Industry observers note that quantum stocks like these trade on hope as much as results, so I'd treat both like small-cap stocks and size them so a bust stings rather than hurts. I'd put about $300 into Infleqtion, since it's already getting paid for its atoms, and $200 into Xanadu as the long shot. One is earning while it builds. The other is betting everything on getting the light right, and $500 lets you own both stories without needing either one to be perfect.

It has been revealed that abbVie stock recently sported a dividend yield of 2.4%. That's quite solid, but it might have been higher had the stock not popped by 28% year to date (as of Nov. 18). (A stock's dividend yield is its total annual dividend amount divided by the stock price, so when the stock price rises, the yield falls, and vice versa.).

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Better still, it's a growing dividend. The current $1.82 quarterly payout is up 5.2% from the previous $1.73, and up from $1.41 in 2022 and $0.57 in 2016. And AbbVie has hiked its payout for 53 years in a row, making it a Dividend King.

In a recent development, let's say you're looking for $1,000 in annual income from AbbVie. How many shares would you need to own? The math is straightforward: The total payout for the year is $1.82 times four, or $7.28 for the year. Divide $1,000 by $7.28, and you'll get the needed number of shares: 137.36.

At a recent stock price of $284 per share, 137 shares will cost you... roughly $39,000.

It has been revealed that but would you want to invest in AbbVie? I'm a shareholder myself, but I'd hesitate to jump in right now because the recent valuation seems a bit high. The recent price-to-sales ratio of 7.7, for example, is well above the five-year average of 5.4, and the forward-looking price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 17.6 is also well above the five-year average of 13.9.

In a recent development, so maybe just add it to your watch list, hoping for a lower entry point. Or just start a small position in it now -- as long as you aim to hang on for many years. By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 14:11 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 21:21 EST, 15 November 2026.

Tenerife have returned to action for the first time since Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel was tragically killed in a collision during a game with FC Andorra earlier this month.

Goalkeeper Jesus Owono came flying out of his goal and wiped out De Miguel with a high challenge, which resulted in the striker being admitted to intensive care, where he later died.

Thirteen days on from the incident, Tenerife played their first game since the player's death as they took on AD Ceuta CF in LaLiga Hypermotion action – with the game filled with tributes to the star.

Players gave a floral tribute as they arrived for the match, and gathered outside gate nine of the Heliodoro Rodríguez Lopez Stadium – the shirt number he wore.

Grief-stricken Tenerife stars, meanwhile, took to the field carrying a bouquet of flowers, and placed it at the scene of the incident.

Both sets of players and fans then observed a minute's silence in memory of De Miguel before the game kicked off.

According to recent reports, 🕊️❤️ THE NINTH MINUTE BELONGED TO JESÚS DE MIGUEL! 🥹🏟️ Football took a back seat during Tenerife's first match following his passing.👏 In the ninth minute, the stadium came together in a heartfelt tribute to honor his memory.💔 Some losses are felt far beyond the pitch.… pic.twitter.com/mqPy4aE9Q3.

CF Tenerife returned to action for the first time since the death of Jesus de Miguel in a game flooded with tributes.

Both sets of players gathered around the centre circle before the game to pay tribute.

The forward (pictured in 2025) passed away after being on the receiving end of a brutal tackle.

The game was then brought to a pause in the ninth minute, so the players could pay another tribute.

Fans inside the stadium unveiled a tifo which read: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternal blanquiazul', which translates to: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternally white and blue.'.

Other fans held up white and blue cards beside the tifo, with others in the ground applauding. When Tenerife scored, De Miguel's shirt was held in the air.

After the game, which Tenerife won 2-0, both teams gathered in the centre circle to place De Miguel's shirt on a bouquet of flowers, and the fans applauded to bring an end to an emotional day.

The tragedy occurred as the game against Andorra entered the seventh minute of stoppage time, when De Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for Tenerife in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, De Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

Sources indicate that owono was initially given a red card for the challenge before the decision was soon taken by the referee to abandon the fixture. Fans have chanted 'murderer' in his direction.

Before the game, players gathered outside gate nine - the shirt numebr de Miguel wore.

Goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been handed a 12-match ban and may never play football again.

On Friday, the goalkeeper was hit with a 12-match ban - but may never play again.

His manager Carles Manso has said: 'We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return.

'When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that (he will do so).'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 21, 2026 at 8:15AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Bright Horizon Energy ›.

The S&P 500 index (^GSPC -3.70%) is near all-time highs despite multiple geopolitical conflicts, inflation, rising interest rates, and the risk of the AI bubble bursting. Wall Street is justifiably worried that a bear market could soon arrive. The smartest move you can make right now is to prepare yourself emotionally for a market downturn. My preferred approach is to distract myself with dividends. Here's why.

It has been revealed that history is clear: a bear market is on the way, though nobody knows exactly when it will arrive, and your emotions will be taxed. It could be a sizable downturn, too, given the similarities between the artificial intelligence (AI) bubble today and the dot-com bubble at the turn of the century. I remember the dot-com crash very well. It was brutal.

It has been revealed that then, just as the market was finally putting that deep and prolonged bear market in the rearview mirror, the Great Recession hit. That economic downturn and the associated bear market were just as brutal. There were legitimate concerns that the global financial system might collapse. And yet, history is very clear: the S&P 500 index, generally considered "the market", has recovered after each bear market and gone on to hit upcoming highs. So the best course of action during a massive downturn is to stay invested.

Staying invested, unfortunately, is easier remarked than done. It is hard to remain calm as you watch the value of your portfolio decline day after day. Bear markets like the dot-com bust and the Great Recession are relentless, and you will almost certainly feel panic building as the days drag on to weeks, months, and even years.

Having invested through some really bad bear markets, I know exactly how hard they can be on one's emotional well-being. The fear you feel can take physical form in sleepless nights, an unsettled stomach, and mental stress. My cure for the emotional hit of market volatility has long been to focus on the dividends my income-focused portfolio throws off each month.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Recent findings suggest that that may sound a bit like King Midas counting his gold, but I know from experience that watching my dividends helps me ignore stock price volatility. And I focus on owning a diverse collection of well-run dividend stocks, including Dividend Kings like Procter & Gamble (PG +0.91%), Federal Realty (FRT -0.14%), and Black Hills (BKH +0.55%), all of which have increased their dividend annually for at least 50 consecutive years. For reference, that's a consumer staples tech giant, a REIT, and a utility, with diversification being another of my investment focuses.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

However, the key piece of this story isn't that I track my dividends during bear markets. It is that I track them all of the time. I have a spreadsheet that I upgrade every month, in bull markets and bear markets. I'm not waiting for the next bear-market stress test to deal with the emotional toll of a downturn. I'm proactively preparing right now and have been for years. Simply put, I've developed a habit of focusing on dividends rather than stock prices.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

I'm not suggesting that stock prices aren't relevant. They most certainly are crucial. But I also know there will be another bear market, and that sticking to my long-term investment approach through it to benefit from the next bull market is likely to lead to the best outcome. So I invest in a way that prepares me to buy and hold, no matter what the market is doing. For me, that means buying reliable dividend stocks and focusing on dividends more than stock prices. It's how I keep calm and carry on, to quote the famous British World War II slogan.

Only you can decide what will help you stay calm during a bear market. For me, it's focusing on the dividends I collect from reliable dividend stocks. But the smartest move right now is to figure out what you need to do before the next bear market comes along. Once it is here, your emotions will be elevated, and that means you will be more likely to make the kind of short-term decisions that could be bad for your long-term performance. Don't wait; prepare today for the bear market that history says is on the way.

  • Bitcoin is right now trading nearly 14% below its 200-week moving average (WMA).
  • History claims the bulls should stay patient.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Neil Patel – Nov 21, 2026 at 8:19AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Bitcoin ›.

Sources indicate that in typical fashion, Bitcoin (BTC -1.80%) is taking investors on a bumpy ride. The world's first and most valuable digital asset has had short spurts of positive momentum this year. But in the past month, the price has tanked 28% (as of Nov. 21), with a five-day drop of 9%.

Bitcoin is right now trading nearly 14% below its 200-week moving average (WMA). According to River, a Bitcoin financial services firm, the leading cryptocurrency has only been in this territory 8.4% of the time in its entire life. It's a rare occurrence, indeed, and it shows that bearish sentiment is ruling the narrative right now.

History claims the bulls should stay patient. This is when investors get paid.

It has been revealed that the 200 WMA smooths out Bitcoin's wild price swings. It tracks the average closing price over roughly four years, which coincides with the investment community’s view of the digital asset's full market cycle. This is why many long-term investors treat it as a baseline.

Sources indicate that as of Nov. 21, the 200 WMA sits at $68,130, and Bitcoin is trading about 14% beneath it. According to River, Bitcoin purchased during past periods when it traded below its 200 WMA returned an average of 120% over the following year. The subsequent three-year gain is 582%. At those averages, $10,000 would have grown to $22,000 after 12 months and $68,200 after 36 months.

It has been revealed that it all sounds so easy, but investors shouldn't take those figures at face value. Because Bitcoin has rarely traded this low relative to its long-term average, the sample size is small. Many of those episodes came when Bitcoin was a niche experiment a decade or more ago. At a $1.2 trillion market cap, the cryptocurrency is unlikely to compound at the same pace as in its early years. Still, the direction of the pattern is hard to ignore.

The recent drop also needs context. Every past Bitcoin bear market included several rallies of 25% or more. This time is similar. That last surge occurred in the back half of August and September.

It has been revealed that however, depth is the noticeable change. So far, this downturn has been much more muted than prior ones. Bitcoin is 53% below its peak now.

In a recent development, there are many takeaways. A smaller fall suggests a more mature asset with steadier holders. It could mean the bottom isn't in yet, and it might leave less upside going forward.

CRYPTO · As of 8:43 AM ET 11/21/26.

Every bear market brings its own reason to declare Bitcoin dead. The past down cycle in 2022 saw major exchange failures that harmed the industry's reputation. Before that, there were worries about government intervention.

In a recent development, today's fear is more technical in nature. Critics argue that advances in artificial intelligence and quantum computing could break Bitcoin's cryptography. This would undermine the network's security. That's a real concern for any industry in 2026 and beyond.

Recent findings suggest that there's no reason to panic yet. The real threat is likely many years away, and the Bitcoin community, fully aware of how technology is rapidly evolving, can adapt. Network updates can bolster the cryptographic setup over time.

Recent findings suggest that there's also a track record worth noting. The Bitcoin network has operated for over 17 years with virtually no outages. That's a remarkable streak for any piece of financial infrastructure.

Recent findings suggest that the smart money is paying attention. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings show that many of Wall Street's biggest companies added to their Bitcoin positions last quarter. But the leading cryptocurrency probably still accounts for less than 0.1% in most of their clients’ portfolios, River notes. That's a very tiny percentage among powerful companies with trillions of dollars in assets under management. A modest allocation bump could bring in demand and translate into substantial buying pressure.

Of course, Bitcoin is no sure thing. It's volatile, and past performance offers no guarantees.

In a recent development, that's where dollar-cost averaging comes in. Investors commit a fixed sum at regular intervals, whether the price is up or down. You avoid market timing, and in periods like the current one, a fixed sum gets you more Bitcoin.

Just remember to never invest more than you're willing to lose, and keep your eyes on the long term.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Daniel Sparks – Nov 21, 2026 at 8:26AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Broadcom ›.

Recent findings suggest that broadcom (AVGO -12.19%) shares have dropped about $135 apiece since their record close on June 2, putting the stock roughly 28% under that peak at about $347 as of this writing. The chip designer reports results for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 (the period ended Nov. 1, 2026) after the market closes on Wednesday, Dec. 9.

There'll be lots of numbers in that release. But one line matters more to me than the rest: artificial intelligence (AI) semiconductor revenue. I'll be checking it twice -- once for the quarter Broadcom just wrapped up, against the $21.7 billion management forecast in September, and once for what the tech giant expects in the first quarter of fiscal 2027.

After all, AI chips made up 56% of Broadcom's revenue in its latest quarter, and they accounted for over 80% of its year-over-year revenue growth.

Broadcom has made a habit of landing a bit above its own AI forecasts this year. In the first quarter of fiscal 2026 (the period ended Feb. 1, 2026), AI semiconductor revenue was $8.4 billion, against the $8.2 billion management had forecast. The fiscal second quarter brought $10.8 billion, against a $10.7 billion forecast. And the fiscal third quarter (the period ended Aug. 2) delivered $16.7 billion, over the $16.0 billion management had guided for.

Growth has accelerated the whole way, too. Year-over-year AI revenue growth rose from 106% in fiscal Q1 to 143% in fiscal Q2 and 221% in fiscal Q3. For fiscal Q4, management expects 236%.

Sources indicate that in other words, Broadcom's guidance has leaned a little conservative. But the beats have been small -- between around 1% and 4% above the forecast. I'm not expecting a blowout in fiscal Q4, then. AI revenue at or a bit above $21.7 billion would show me the organization is still on the schedule management laid out.

A result under $21.7 billion would break that streak for the first time this fiscal year.

Recent findings suggest that management's goal for next year is about $115 billion of AI revenue in fiscal 2027 -- almost double the $58 billion or so it expects for fiscal 2026. And on its September earnings call, Broadcom mentioned it doesn't strategy to update that figure every quarter. That arguably makes each quarterly forecast the best checkpoint investors have.

Do the math, and $115 billion comes to almost $29 billion a quarter on average. That's about a third higher than the fiscal fourth-quarter forecast. If AI revenue rose at an even pace from $21.7 billion, the first quarter of fiscal 2027 would likely need to land somewhere near $24 billion to keep the year on track.

A first-quarter forecast in the mid-$20 billion range, then, should be a sign the doubling is on schedule. A forecast closer to $22 billion might mean more of next year's growth is being shifted into the second half of fiscal 2027.

Management sounded confident in September.

"Our demand actually exceeds this outlook, and we will work to improve supply," remarked CEO Hock Tan.

It has been revealed that if that holds, the first-quarter forecast might land above my rough math. Either way, Dec. 9 is the first chance to check.

Industry observers note that after a 28% fall, I don't think Broadcom needs a major upside surprise to work from here. Of course, the tech giant has kept growing through the slide. Fiscal third-quarter revenue rose 86% year over year to $29.6 billion, and non-GAAP (adjusted) operating income climbed 92%.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

In a recent development, that growth hasn't made the stock cheap, though. At around $347, each share costs about 44 times Broadcom's earnings per share over the past four quarters. This price-to-earnings ratio only makes sense if AI revenue continues to rise as management expects.

In a recent development, what the stock needs is evidence that next year's doubling is still on track. And the AI revenue line, along with the forecast behind it, is where that evidence should first appear.

Granted, one good report won't settle everything. Much of next year's AI revenue hinges on deployment looks from a few big AI customers, and those plans can change. But the first-quarter forecast is the closest look investors will get at whether these plans are holding.

According to recent reports, in the end, if fiscal Q4 AI revenue comes in at or above $21.7 billion and the first-quarter forecast calls for the mid-$20 billion range, I think today's price looks fair for a growth stock with sales climbing this fast. A forecast well below that would make me more cautious, even at a lower stock price.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Breaking: Why Isn't Walmart's Stock Bouncing Back After Weak Earnings Results?

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (795 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that walmart's (WMT +1.51%) third-quarter results, which were posted Thursday morning, certainly weren't bad.
  • Recent findings suggest that but the tech giant's growth rates for key metrics were lower than in the second quarter, including two that had soared in previous frames.
  • According to recent reports, to put some concrete numbers and percentages on this, Walmart's third-quarter revenue totaled $188.8 billion, which was 5.2% higher year over year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Eric Volkman – Nov 21, 2026 at 8:37AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Walmart ›.

It has been revealed that walmart's (WMT +1.51%) third-quarter results, which were posted Thursday morning, certainly weren't bad. The massive retailer topped analyst estimates, if only slightly, and delivered growth in both revenue and non-GAAP, or adjusted, earnings per share (EPS).

Recent findings suggest that but the tech giant's growth rates for key metrics were lower than in the second quarter, including two that had soared in previous frames. I think this is why Walmart's stock slumped during Thursday's trading session, only to recover the following day amid investor rotation out of beleaguered tech stocks and into defensive sectors like retail.

According to recent reports, to put some concrete numbers and percentages on this, Walmart's third-quarter revenue totaled $188.8 billion, which was 5.2% higher year over year. This was on the back of comparable sales in its core Walmart U.S. operations that rose by 2.9% when stripping out fuel sales. On a constant-currency basis, revenue was 4.5% higher at $187.6 billion.

On the bottom line, attributable net income under generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) sank in that one-year stretch, falling to just under $4.95 billion from the year-ago $6.14 billion. Yet on the non-GAAP (adjusted), per-share basis that analysts and many investors consider a truer indication of profitability, there was an improvement. Adjusted EPS rose to $0.65 from third quarter 2026's $0.62 for a 4.8% increase.

Those leading fundamentals were barely high enough to outpace the consensus analyst estimates of almost $187.3 billion for headline revenue and $0.64 per share for adjusted net profit.

CEO John Furner flagged the quarter as a resounding success. This, he was quoted as saying, derived from "growing our core business and gaining market share. The strength of our omnichannel model gives us room to do even more.".

That growth, however, was down from the second quarter's headline revenue increase of 5.9% and the 19% rise in adjusted EPS to $0.81. At least frame No. 3's 2.9% bump in U.S. Walmart ex-fuel "comps" (modestly) topped the previous quarter's 2.6%.

In a recent development, another major growth driver, global e-commerce sales, advanced 17% year over year. This sounds very robust until it's compared to the second quarter's 23%. A smaller but fast-emerging revenue stream, the company's global advertising business, slowed to 25% year over year from the quarter-ago gain of 38%.

According to recent reports, walmart noted that its results were adversely affected by Big Billion Days (BBD), which occurred later in the quarter than in fiscal 2025, due to the timing of the Diwali holiday in the Hindu calendar. This meant that a large chunk of the increase in sales from BBD -- a monster shopping holiday in advance of Diwali for the company's majority-owned e-commerce business Flipkart in India -- will be booked in the current (fourth) fiscal quarter.

Industry observers note that CFO John David Rainey remarked in Walmart's quarterly conference call that the growth of net sales (the bulk of its revenue) on a constant-currency basis, which was 4.4%, would have been around one percentage point higher. The timing shift also affected global e-commerce and advertising growth, although the company didn't provide estimates on the impact to those overall metrics.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

This is all to say that Walmart's third quarter wasn't materially better than its predecessor, and investors are expecting more from such a powerful and historically innovative presence in the retail industry.

In a recent development, to its credit, for the third time this calendar year, the company's management raised certain guidance for fiscal 2027. The period's net sales on a constant-currency basis should rise from 4.9% to 5.2% over 2026; the previous range was 4% to 5%. Adjusted EPS is forecast to range from $2.84 to $2.89 per share, compared favorably with the prior $2.80 to $2.87 estimate.

Perhaps the zip the lingering BBD lift provides to fourth-quarter results will be a pleasant surprise to Mr. Market. And looking past that, the company seems poised to continue cranking out growth rates that are high for an already-huge enterprise operating in the tough and competitive retail industry. I think Walmart can still deliver for its shareholders, and I remain bullish on its stock despite the ultimately forgettable third quarter.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Costco (COST +0.76%) is far removed from the artificial intelligence trade, but it's still juicing investor’s portfolios.
  • The organization's strong performance remains the highlight.
  • Sources indicate that investors that seek high-quality businesses might already have Costco on their radar.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Neil Patel – Nov 21, 2026 at 8:50AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Costco Wholesale ›.

Costco (COST +0.76%) is far removed from the artificial intelligence trade, but it's still juicing investor’s portfolios. Shares have surged 29% in 2026 (as of Nov. 16), with huge gains coming in the past couple of months. Investors are warming up to the retail stock, perhaps as a safe-haven play in these uncertain times.

The organization's strong performance remains the highlight. Costco's comparable sales in the U.S. jumped 12.6% year over year in October (specifically the four weeks that ended Nov. 1). Even excluding impacts from gasoline sales and foreign exchange, this figure rose 8.1%. The growth has proven durable in various economic environments.

Sources indicate that investors that seek high-quality businesses might already have Costco on their radar. Here's the one number that demonstrates the economic moat is widening.

Industry observers note that at the end of the 2026 fourth fiscal quarter (ended Aug. 30), Costco reported having 84.1 million membership households. That's up 3.8% year over year. And it has risen 36% in the past five years. I believe this single metric underscores the firm's moat, as it represents a sticky customer base that brings in recurring membership revenue.

Sources indicate that an ever-expanding membership base proves that Costco is delivering an impressive value proposition to more people around the world. This is particularly key in the competitive retail sector. Walmart’s (WMT +1.51%) Sam's Club and BJ's Wholesale Club (BJ -5.35%) are direct rivals. Amazon's (AMZN -4.10%) popular Prime membership also can't be ignored.

Industry observers note that and even at its huge size, with $24.5 billion in October net revenue and more than 900 warehouses globally, Costco is still able to grow. If the customer base was shrinking, that would be a clear sign of a weakening moat.

Recent findings suggest that A higher membership base also means that Costco's key competitive advantage remains valid. The company's massive scale is critical to its enduring success. The average warehouse sells 4,000 stock-keeping units, well below the 30,000 at typical supermarkets. Costco's significant revenue base means that it's buying enormous volumes from suppliers of fewer goods, which gives it negotiating leverage. These savings get passed on to shoppers.

According to recent reports, inflation is rising more than expected. In these times, when households are focused on getting the most value from their spending, it seems that becoming a Costco member is a no-brainer decision. That mentality drives greater membership sign-ups.

The leadership team is happy with the results. Although consumers remain under pressure, chief executive officer Ron Vachris states Costco is gaining market share.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

It has been revealed that buying an outstanding business doesn't guarantee above-average returns. Investors don’t want to overpay. Valuation is the missing link.

Five years ago, this large-cap stock traded at a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 46.7. At that time, Apple (AAPL -1.90%), which was the most valuable manufacturer in the world whose shares soared 449% in the prior half decade, sold at a P/E multiple of 26.9. Knowing this, any rational observer would've agreed that Costco was expensive, a stance that would have discouraged owning the leading retailer.

Recent findings suggest that in the last five years, however, the stock price has climbed 114%. It crushed the overall market.

Today, the P/E ratio sits at a steeper 53.5. Again, the consensus view is likely that this presents no margin of safety. In fact, value investors will say that buying now is a risky move, as expectations are high, which introduces more downside risk should Costco miss analyst estimates in any upcoming quarterly financial update.

The stock moved 24% higher in the past two months, after starting at a P/E ratio of 43.1. It's impossible to know what the "right" valuation to pay is when it comes to Costco. I believe this tech giant is uninvestable right now. Paying a significant premium to the market, even though the business has staying power, is hard to justify.

  • Recent findings suggest that robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.

Sources indicate that here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

Recent findings suggest that robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

In a recent development, robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly important sources of transaction revenue, while the tech giant has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

It has been revealed that transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

Industry observers note that net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

—With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney.

Raul Jimenez’s late penalty seals share of spoils for Wolves against Blackburn

💡 Key Takeaways
  • An injury-time penalty from returning hero Raul Jimenez ensured Wolves came away with a point in their Championship opener after Blackburn had produced a comeback.
  • Wolves led through Marshall Munetsi’s cool finish on 18 minutes only for Sean McLoughlin’s first Blackburn goal to draw the visitors level on 27 minutes with a well-timed run and header.
  • According to recent reports, the visitors turned the game around on 48 minutes through Andri Gudjohnsen’s close-range strike only for substitute Jimenez to level the game three minutes into injury time from the spot after Ryan Alebiosu handled the ball in the box.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An injury-time penalty from returning hero Raul Jimenez ensured Wolves came away with a point in their Championship opener after Blackburn had produced a comeback.

Wolves led through Marshall Munetsi’s cool finish on 18 minutes only for Sean McLoughlin’s first Blackburn goal to draw the visitors level on 27 minutes with a well-timed run and header.

According to recent reports, the visitors turned the game around on 48 minutes through Andri Gudjohnsen’s close-range strike only for substitute Jimenez to level the game three minutes into injury time from the spot after Ryan Alebiosu handled the ball in the box. Jimenez and his wife marked his return to Molineux by giving 5,000 fans black scarves emblazoned with the words ‘Si Senor’ - a nod to his song - and Jimenez did not disappoint as he rifled in his penalty.

LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU.

In a recent development, cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

According to recent reports, peixoto said: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

Sources indicate that “We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

Industry observers note that “We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”.

Tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

Mowbray remarked: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

In a recent development, “Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we showed there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”.

The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

However, Wolves scored the first goal of the new campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

"A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq.

Blackburn drew level through an unlikely source just nine minutes later as McLoughlin headed in his first-ever goal in English football in more than 150 games when he met Ryoya Morishita’s cross from the right at the near post.

The home side had chances to retake the lead before the break as Lopez curled a shot narrowly over the top from 20-yards while Kieran Trippier teed up Mateus Mane for a chance as the teenager found the top of the net from distance.

Blackburn turned the game on its head minutes after the break as Gudjohnsen turned home Afolayan’s deflected ball in from the right from close range to stun Molineux into silence.

"It's brilliantly worked by Blackburn Rovers!" 💥Andri Guðjohnsen finishes from close range to turn the game around and the visitors the lead 👏 pic.twitter.com/vkKQQezicK.

Peixoto introduced Jimenez from the bench on the hour mark but even the Mexican could not lift Wolves with Blackburn comfortable for long periods as frustration grew in the stands.

However, Alebiosu handled Jackson Tchatchoua’s cross from the left in injury time and the referee awarded a spot kick which allowed Jimenez to mark his Wolves return with an equaliser from 12-yards as he sent Balazs Toth the wrong way.

Munetsi 18, R. McLoughlin 27, A. Gudjohnsen 48Yellow card: Pickering ​34, Cantwell 35, ‌Forshaw 45Attendance: 30,984Referee: Farai ⁠Hallam.

“I think it is a really harsh one. He [the referee] has to be sure at such a critical time of the game. And I do not think he can be sure. I think he has almost had a guess that he is in the box. It is such a big call.”.

“We see the ref’s position. The fact the ref makes the decision to give the penalty in my opinion, it is a bigger decision to give it then to not. We have got the luxury of the replays and we are still not sure. His whole body is outside the box.”.

“It looks outside the box to me [the penalty incident]. The still picture suggests to me it was outside the box. We can get better and we will have to. We have to be more dominant with the ball at times and be better in attack. We have done a lot of work on that in pre-season. Having been in this league a long time, the power of the dressing room is crucial and any motivation tool you can you use is important. I think we will be fine. You have to enjoy football and love it. I think the boys enjoyed it tonight.”.

It has been revealed that “Obviously frustrated. The boys did everything to get the three points but it is gutting in the end. I thought I was outside the box when the ball came in and the decision went against us. They are saying it is in the box and it is frustrating. We dug deep and thought we had it. I cannot fault everyone as we all put in a shift, it was just the final details with the penalty decision. We deserved the three points. If we play like that every week, we will go far in the table.”.

Raul Jimenez reacts after his late penalty saved a point for Wolves against Blackburn 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/aXvVeWw6fc.

Recent findings suggest that “Before the game we were predicting Wolves would be right up there [this season] and we thought it would be a comfortable win. But that was not the case. Blackburn gave a really good account of themselves and had lots of openings. [Cesar] Peixoto will be breathing a massive sigh of relief with that handball.”.

It has been revealed that “Wolves got away with one if I am being really honest. In terms of their second-half performance, they did not do anywhere near enough. I thought Blackburn were excellent throughout and deservedly took the lead. It is a huge decision [to give the penalty], but in the end Raul Jimenez steps up to get his side the point. [Cesar Peixoto] will be delighted to get something in the end.”.

Industry observers note that due to his Burnley ties, fresh Wolves defender Trippier is booed by the travelling Blackburn fans. On the other side of defence for Wolves is Moller Wolfe, who started for Norway against England in the World Cup quarter-finals in Miami.

According to recent reports, after Jeff Beck’s Hi Ho Silver Lining rings around the stadium and tributes paid to former Wolves goalkeeper Phil Parkes, we are under way at Molineux. The 2026/27 Championship season is officially under way.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off on opening night in the Championship.

When Wolverhampton Wanderers last attacked the Championship under a Portuguese manager upcoming to English football, it proved a vintage season.

Molineux was under the spell of Nuno Espírito Santo in that 2017-18 campaign, and the big question is whether César Peixoto can lead a repeat nearly a decade later.

Peixoto was a surprise appointment in June, replacing Rob Edwards, and he has been entrusted with the mission of returning Wolves to the Premier League at the first time of asking.

Industry observers note that “I have changed some things with set-pieces and some things in other moments of the game because I want the team to be organised and understand all the different moments within a match. During pre-season we have scored some goals from high pressing, but we will not be able to press high in every moment of every game. The players have to understand the game and recognise what each moment requires. It is important that we work as a team. When we can press high, we’ll press high. When we need to defend in a mid-block, we will stay organised. When the opposition pushes us deeper, which will sometimes happen, we have to be organised there as well.

Industry observers note that “There are a lot of crosses in the Championship, for example, so the team needs to understand what to do in those situations. We want to play our football, be offensive and react strongly when we lose the ball, but we also need to understand the different moments of the game. I think we are at a good level to attack the Championship.”.

Our experts have been having their say ahead of the new Championship season. A number of them believe Wolves will be promoted, including John Percy:.

It is difficult to look beyond West Ham. Nuno Espírito Santo romped to the Championship title with Wolves in 2018 and remains a shrewd operator (along with his No 2 Rui Pedro Silva), while convincing Jarrod Bowen to stay is significant. I am going to go for Wolves and Middlesbrough as the other two promoted clubs.

It has been revealed that the 2026/27 Championship season kicks off at Molineux as Wolves host Blackburn, with the home side hoping to put the bad memories of last season firmly behind them. There are new playoff rules in place for this season, with six places now up for grabs in the play-offs.

In a recent development, wolves are aiming to return to the Premier League at the first attempt, having endured a miserable season in the top flight last year as they finished bottom with just three wins to their name. It has been a summer of change at the club as they chose to change managers. Rob Edwards lost his job in what was a shock move and was replaced by 46-year-old Cesar Peixoto, with this being his first head coaching position outside of his home country Portugal. Back in 2017/18, Wolves won the Championship title led by Peixoto’s compatriot Nuno Espirito Santo.

“I am ready,” Peixoto told Wolves’ club website. “We have worked very hard during pre-season, and I think we have had a great pre-season. All the players have worked very, very hard and they understand what I want from them. I am ready and confident going into the first game. Football is football, whether it is in Portugal or England, but there are different characteristics to the game here. We have watched, observed and analysed the Championship. We did that work before I came to the club, so we know what to expect.

According to recent reports, “It is going to be a tough season with good teams, but we are prepared to fight for the three points game after game and week after week. We know what we want from the team and we know what our big goal is. We’re going to work very hard and fight to achieve that goal.”.

In a recent development, they have brought in vast experience on the player side in the shape of Kieran Trippier and Raul Jimenez, who is back at Molineux three years after leaving for Fulham. Although they have lost Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes to Aston Villa, most of their squad has stayed intact as they pursue promotion back to the top flight. It is a special year for the club as they celebrate their 150th anniversary.

In a recent development, blackburn, led by experienced manager Tony Mowbray, did not enjoy a great season in the Championship last year, finishing down in 20th place and just five points above the relegation zone. 14 years have now passed since Blackburn last played in the top flight.

“I think it is a tough start,” Mowbray said. “On paper, I would suggest the first couple of games, particularly, jumped out as a tough start. One of the Premier League sides from last season, away from home. They have got a very talented squad, a pretty expensive squad. They have got some very good individual talent. Yet, there is an argument to say they have not won many football matches in the last calendar year. So, what we get, we will have to wait and see.”.

Recent findings suggest that these sides last met in the FA Cup during the 2024/25 season, with Wolves winning that fourth-round tie 2-0 thanks to goals from Matheus Cunha and Gomes, both of whom are now plying their trade elsewhere. The omens would appear to be on Wolves’ side as they are unbeaten in their last eight league meetings with Blackburn. Both sides progressed to the second round of the League Cup last weekend, with Wolves beating Port Vale 3-0 and Blackburn overcoming Burton Albion 2-1.
